| \$120 001 – \$180 000 | \$29 467 plus 37 cents for each \$1 over \$120 000 |
| \$180 001 and over | \$51 667 plus 45 cents for each \$1 over \$180 000 |

The amount of income tax her friend Hallie pays is exactly twice the amount that Amanda pays. Using the tax table above, find Hallie's taxable income.

A painter needs to paint a wall on one side of a home movie theatre. The wall is a trapezium: the top edge is 9 m long, the left side is vertical and 4 m high, the right side is vertical, and the bottom edge makes an angle of elevation of $10^\circ$ with the horizontal (rising to the right). What is the area of the wall, correct to the nearest square metre?
questions.answer: The bottom edge rises by $9\tan10^\circ=1.587\ldots$ m over the $9$ m length, so the right side is $4-9\tan10^\circ=2.41\ldots$ m high. The area is a rectangle of $9\times4=36$ m$^2$ minus the triangle under the bottom edge: $36-\tfrac12\times9\times9\tan10^\circ=36-7.14=28.86\approx29\ \text{m}^2$. (Equivalently, the area of the trapezium is $\tfrac12(4+2.41)\times9=28.86$.)

questions.question: A painter needs to paint a wall of area 29 m$^2$. A 5 L tin of paint costs \$98 and covers 10 m$^2$. How much will it cost to paint the wall?
questions.answer: $29\div10=2.9$, so $3$ tins are needed (tins cannot be bought in parts). Cost $=3\times\$98=\$294$.

questions.question:
The activities needed to complete a local council roadwork project, and their durations in weeks, are: A (6), B (3), C (5), D (3), E (unknown), F (8), G (4) and H (6). The network is shown in the diagram: A and C both lead into the node from which D and E start; B starts the path through C and F; D leads into G, G into H, and E, F and H all end at the finish.

The council has determined that activities E and H are critical. Determine the duration of activity E.
questions.answer: The path $B-C-D-G-H$ has length $3+5+3+4+6=21$ weeks. Since H is critical, the minimum completion time of the project is $21$ weeks. Activity E starts after A and C: its earliest start time is $\max(6,\ 3+5)=8$ weeks. Since E is also critical, $8+E=21$, so $E=13$ weeks.

questions.question:
The activities needed to complete a local council roadwork project, and their durations in weeks, are: A (6), B (3), C (5), D (3), E (unknown), F (8), G (4) and H (6). The network is shown in the diagram: A and C both lead into the node from which D and E start; B starts the path through C and F; D leads into G, G into H, and E, F and H all end at the finish.

The duration of E is 13 weeks, and the minimum completion time of the project is 21 weeks. List the critical path(s) for this project.
questions.answer: The critical paths are the paths of length $21$ weeks: $B-C-D-G-H$ ($3+5+3+4+6=21$) and $B-C-E$ ($3+5+13=21$).

questions.question:
The activities needed to complete a local council roadwork project, and their durations in weeks, are: A (6), B (3), C (5), D (3), E (unknown), F (8), G (4) and H (6). The network is shown in the diagram: A and C both lead into the node from which D and E start; B starts the path through C and F; D leads into G, G into H, and E, F and H all end at the finish.

The duration of E is 13 weeks, so the critical paths are $B-C-D-G-H$ and $B-C-E$ (21 weeks). It is possible to reduce the duration of certain activities, but doing so will incur additional costs. The cost per week to reduce the duration of four activities is:

| Activity | A | C | E | H |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cost per week | \$30 000 | \$40 000 | \$90 000 | \$120 000 |

For example, to reduce the duration of activity A by two weeks will cost \$60 000. The duration of each of these activities can be reduced by a maximum of three weeks.

What will be the minimum cost to reduce the total duration of the roadworks to 18 weeks? In your answer state the activities that need to be reduced and the new durations of these activities.
questions.answer:
The paths and their lengths are: $B-C-D-G-H=21$, $B-C-E=21$, $A-E=6+13=19$, $A-D-G-H=6+3+4+6=19$ and $B-F=11$.

Both critical paths pass through $C$, so reducing C by the maximum of $3$ weeks (the cheapest activity common to both) reduces both of them to $18$ weeks, at a cost of $3\times\$40\,000=\$120\,000$. The paths $A-E$ and $A-D-G-H$ are then the longest at $19$ weeks, and both contain A, so A must be reduced by $1$ week at a cost of \$30 000. All paths are then $18$ weeks or less.

Minimum cost $=120\,000+30\,000=\$150\,000$: reduce C by $3$ weeks (new duration $2$ weeks) and A by $1$ week (new duration $5$ weeks). (Reducing E by $3$ weeks and H by $3$ weeks instead would cost \$630 000.)

questions.question: Jordan was investigating the capacities of different glass tumblers. She used two tumblers, one in the shape of a cone with radius 5 cm and height 8 cm, and another in the shape of a cylinder with radius 2.5 cm and height $h$. When Jordan completely filled the conical tumbler with water then poured it into the cylindrical tumbler, she found it only half filled the cylinder. What is the height ($h$) of the cylindrical tumbler, correct to two decimal places?
questions.answer: Volume of the cone $=\tfrac13\pi r^2h=\tfrac13\pi(5)^2(8)=209.44\ \text{cm}^3$. This fills half of the cylinder, so $\tfrac12\pi(2.5)^2h=\tfrac13\pi(5)^2(8)$. Then $h=\dfrac{2\times\tfrac13\times25\times8}{2.5^2}=\dfrac{400/3}{6.25}=21.33$ cm.

questions.question: Which of the data sets graphed below has the largest positive correlation coefficient value?
questions.answer: The largest positive correlation coefficient belongs to the data with the strongest positive linear association: the points in D lie closest to an upward-sloping line (D).

questions.question: Which of the following expressions would give the height ($h$) of the tree in the diagram?
questions.answer:
$h$ is opposite the $35^\circ$ angle and $41$ m is adjacent, so $\tan35^\circ=\dfrac h{41}\Rightarrow h=41\tan35^\circ$ (A).
*(The question paper prints option D as $41/\cos35^\circ$, the same as B; the answer is unaffected.)*

questions.question: The female and male smoking rates, expressed as percentages, are shown in the back-to-back stem-and-leaf plot. What is the lowest female smoking rate?
questions.answer: The stem is the tens digit. Reading the female side (left) of the row with stem 1, the smallest leaf is 6, so the lowest rate is $16\%$ (C).

questions.question: In a survey of $250$ randomly selected Year 12 students it was found that $65$ use a bicycle to travel to school. Based on this survey, approximately how many of $72\,000$ Year 12 students would be expected to use a bicycle to school?
The network shows the distances, in kilometres, along roads that connect Town A and Town B. The shortest distance, in kilometres, from Town A to Town B is:
questions.answer: The shortest path (highlighted in the marking guide) is $2+1+2+5=10$ km (B).

questions.question: Terrence boards a plane in London at 8 pm on Thursday 12th September and flies for 22 hours before arriving in Sydney. Given that Sydney's time zone is ten hours ahead of London's, what is the local time when he arrives in Sydney?
questions.answer: 8 pm Thursday $+22$ h $=6$ pm Friday London time. Adding $10$ h for Sydney gives $4$ am Saturday 14th September (C).

questions.question:
A group of students sat two different exams, Mathematics and Science.

| Student | A | B | C | D | E | F | G | H |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Maths ($x$) | 68 | 70 | 45 | 51 | 86 | 61 | 72 | 78 |
| Science ($y$) | 80 | 85 | 63 | 71 | 93 | 79 | 86 | 92 |

Use your calculator to find the equation of the least-squares regression line for the scores. (Answers have been rounded.)
questions.answer: Entering the data in the statistics mode of a calculator gives gradient $0.7393$ and intercept $32.053$, so $y=0.739x+32.05$ (A).

questions.question: An asset depreciates to half its original value after 5 years using the declining balance method. What is the approximate annual rate of depreciation?
Amanda received her natural gas account. She is charged 3.892 cents per MJ for the first 5000 MJ and 2.354 cents per MJ for any other usage. What is the cost if she used 8450 MJ of natural gas?
Which is the correct expression to make $t$ the subject of the formula $x=ab+yt^2$?
questions.answer: $x-ab=yt^2\Rightarrow t^2=\dfrac{x-ab}{y}\Rightarrow t=\pm\sqrt{\dfrac{x-ab}{y}}$ (B).

questions.question: Peter has completed four Geography tests. His mean mark is 72%. What percentage mark does he have to get in his next test to increase the mean to 73%?
questions.answer: Sum of four tests $=4\times72=288$. Need $\dfrac{288+x}{5}=73\Rightarrow x=365-288=77$ (C).

questions.question: Ravi owns 1782 shares with a market value of \$8.25 per share. The dividend received for these shares is \$1372.50. The percentage dividend yield is:

In 2008 the population in Country ABC was 15.5 million people. The number of people in the same country increased at a rate of 2.5% per year. Which expression represents the number (in millions) of people in Country ABC if $y$ represents the number of years after 2008?
questions.answer: A $2.5\%$ yearly increase multiplies by $1.025$ each year: $15.5\times1.025^y$ (A).

questions.question: Which of the following graphs represents $y=-3^{-x}$?
questions.answer: $y=3^{-x}$ passes through $(0,1)$ and decays towards $0$ as $x\to\infty$. The negative sign reflects it in the $x$-axis, so the graph is below the axis, passes through $(0,-1)$, tends to $0$ from below as $x\to\infty$, and falls steeply as $x\to-\infty$ (e.g. $y=-3$ at $x=-1$). This is graph D.

questions.question: In a raffle, the total prize money is shared among the first two tickets drawn in the ratio $7:3$. The prize for the first ticket drawn is $\$560$. What is the total prize money?
questions.answer: $7$ parts $=\$560$, so $1$ part $=\$80$ and the total ($10$ parts) is $\$800$.

questions.question: Roger purchases a car to travel to work and back home. The fuel consumption of the car is $8.1$ L/100 km and the fuel tank capacity is $50$ L. If Roger drives $850$ km in total each week, how many full tanks of petrol will he need?
questions.answer: Fuel used $=\dfrac{850}{100}\times8.1=68.85$ L. Tanks $=\dfrac{68.85}{50}=1.377$, so he needs $2$ full tanks (rounding up, since one tank is not enough).

questions.question: In 2017, Jasmine bought a home for $\$625\,000$. The house appreciated by $6.3\%$ p.a. over the next 5 years. Determine how much the value of the house had increased by over the 5 years, correct to the nearest $\$1000$.

A rocket is launched into the air. Its height is modelled by $h=-40t^2+800t$, where $h$ is the height in metres and $t$ the time in seconds (graph shown). State the maximum height that the rocket reaches.
questions.answer: From the graph the maximum height is $4000$ m (at $t=10$ s).

questions.question: (Rocket model $h=-40t^2+800t$.) Explain why there are two times, namely 5 seconds and 15 seconds, when the rocket is 3000 metres above the ground.
questions.answer: The rocket reaches $3000$ m on the way up ($t=5$ s) and passes through the same height again on the way down ($t=15$ s); the parabola is symmetric about $t=10$.

questions.question: (Rocket model $h=-40t^2+800t$.) When does the rocket return back to the ground?
questions.answer: $h=0\Rightarrow-40t(t-20)=0$, so $t=20$ seconds.

questions.question: The network diagram shows the travel times in minutes along roads connecting Towns A, B, C, D, E, F, G and H. Draw a minimum spanning tree for this network and determine its length.
questions.answer:
Choosing the smallest edges that do not form a cycle (Kruskal's algorithm): CE $15$, EF $20$, CD $25$, EG $25$, BC $30$, AB $35$, FH $45$ (see diagram).
Length $=15+20+25+25+30+35+45=195$ minutes.

questions.question: (Network of travel times as above.) How long does it take to travel from Town A to Town F using the fastest route?
questions.answer: The routes are: ABDF $=140$, ABDEF $=170$, ABCDF $=125$, ACEF $=50+15+20=85$. The fastest route is A–C–E–F, taking $85$ minutes.

questions.question: This table shows the tax rates for the 2023–2024 financial year. Jonathan is an electrician and receives a yearly salary of $\$92\,500$. He also receives an income of $\$750$ per month from his part-time work at the local gym. Jonathan purchased an electrician's toolbox for $\$2075$ which is an allowed tax deduction. He made a PAYG contribution from both sources of income of $\$2140$ per month. He must also pay the Medicare levy, which is $2\%$ of his taxable income. Find Jonathan's taxable income.
(Jonathan: taxable income $\$99\,425$; tax table as above.) Using the tax table, find the income tax payable.
(Jonathan: taxable income $\$99\,425$.) Calculate the Medicare levy that Jonathan needs to pay.
(Jonathan: tax payable $\$22\,780.13$, Medicare levy $\$1988.50$, PAYG $\$2140$ per month.) Will he have a tax liability or a tax refund? Justify your answer with calculations.
questions.answer: Total payable $=22\,780.13+1988.50=\$24\,768.63$. PAYG paid $=2140\times12=\$25\,680$. Since he has paid more than he owes, he receives a **refund** of $25\,680-24\,768.63=\$911.37$.

questions.question: The table shows the future value of $\$1$ invested at the end of each time period at the rate indicated. Use the table to find the future value of an annuity of $\$900$ invested at the end of each year for $11$ years at an interest rate of $4.5\%$ p.a.
questions.answer: From the table, the factor for $4.5\%$ and $11$ periods is $13.8412$. $FV=900\times13.8412=\$12\,457.08$.

questions.question: (Annuity of $\$900$ per year for $11$ years at $4.5\%$ p.a., future value $\$12\,457.08$.) Calculate the amount of interest earned on the investment.
questions.answer: Total contributions $=11\times900=\$9900$. Interest $=12\,457.08-9900=\$2557.08$.

questions.question: The table shows the present value of an annuity of $\$1$ invested at the end of each time period at the rate indicated. $\$3500$ is deposited at the end of each year for $5$ years into an annuity account. The interest rate is $5.5\%$ p.a. Find the present value of the annuity.
questions.answer: From the table, the factor for $5.5\%$ and $5$ periods is $4.2703$. $PV=3500\times4.2703=\$14\,946.05$.

questions.question: The formula below is used to calculate an estimate of blood alcohol content (BAC) for males: $BAC_{\text{male}}=\dfrac{10N-7.5H}{6.8M}$, where $N$ is the number of standard drinks, $H$ the number of hours of drinking and $M$ the mass in kg. The number of hours required for a person to reach zero BAC after they stop consuming alcohol is $\text{Time}=\dfrac{BAC}{0.015}$. A glass of wine is $1.2$ standard drinks and a glass of spirits is $1$ standard drink. John weighs $69.54$ kg. He consumed 4 glasses of wine and 3 glasses of spirits between 7:00 pm and 12:45 am the following day. He then stopped drinking alcohol. Calculate the time in the morning when John's BAC should reach zero, to the nearest minute.

Rita would like to save $\$35\,000$ for her first home deposit in 5 years' time. Option 1: she invests in an annuity that pays $14\%$ p.a. compounding quarterly. Using the table of future values of $\$1$ below, how much does she need to deposit at the end of each quarter?
questions.answer: $n=5\times4=20$ periods, $r=\dfrac{14}4=3.5\%$ per quarter. The table factor is $28.2797$. Contribution $=\dfrac{35\,000}{28.2797}=\$1237.64$ per quarter.

questions.question: Option 2: Rita's friend advises her to invest $\$21\,000$ at $9\%$ p.a. interest, compounding monthly, for 5 years. How much will Rita have at the end of 5 years?

(Option 1: $\$1237.64$ per quarter gives $\$35\,000$; option 2: $\$32\,879.30$.) Which option will result in her saving enough for her first home deposit? Justify your answer by determining how much more or less than the required amount she will have with each option.
questions.answer: Option 1 gives exactly $\$35\,000$ (the required amount). Option 2 gives $\$32\,879.30$, which is $\$2120.70$ less than required. So Option 1 achieves the deposit.

questions.question: A bag contains 9 red balls and 7 white balls. Two balls are selected at random without replacement. Complete the tree diagram.
questions.answer: First draw: $P(R)=\dfrac9{16}$, $P(W)=\dfrac7{16}$. After a red: $P(R)=\dfrac8{15}$, $P(W)=\dfrac7{15}$. After a white: $P(R)=\dfrac9{15}$, $P(W)=\dfrac6{15}$ (see diagram).

questions.question: (9 red and 7 white balls; two drawn without replacement.) Calculate the probability of selecting two balls of different colours.
questions.answer: $P(RW)+P(WR)=\dfrac9{16}\cdot\dfrac7{15}+\dfrac7{16}\cdot\dfrac9{15}=\dfrac{21}{80}+\dfrac{21}{80}=\dfrac{21}{40}$.

questions.question: (9 red and 7 white balls; two drawn without replacement.) Calculate the probability of picking at least one red ball.

This scatterplot shows the age and value for a sample of cars of a particular model. A line of best fit has been drawn, passing through $(5,40\,000)$ and $(10,20\,000)$. Determine the gradient of the line of best fit.
(Line of best fit for value $V$ against age $A$, through $(5,40\,000)$ with gradient $-4000$.) Determine the equation of the line of best fit.
(Line of best fit $V=-4000A+60\,000$.) Use the equation to predict the value of a car of this model aged 5 years.
(Line of best fit $V=-4000A+60\,000$.) Use the equation to predict the age of a car of this model with a value of $\$48\,000$.
(Line of best fit $V=-4000A+60\,000$.) Would this model be good to predict the value of a car that is 16 years old? Justify with reason.
questions.answer: No. At $A=16$, $V=-4000(16)+60\,000=-\$4000$, a negative value, which is unrealistic. The age is also well outside the data (about $1$–$11$ years), so this extrapolation is unreliable.

questions.question: Solve $\dfrac{x+5}5-\dfrac{2x-2}3=-3$.
questions.answer:
Multiply by $15$: $3(x+5)-5(2x-2)=-45\Rightarrow3x+15-10x+10=-45\Rightarrow-7x=-70\Rightarrow x=10$.
Check: $\dfrac{15}5-\dfrac{18}3=3-6=-3$ ✓.

questions.question: A student believes that the time it takes for an ice cube to melt ($M$ minutes) varies inversely with the room temperature ($T^\circ$C). The student observes that at a room temperature of $9^\circ$C it takes $20$ minutes for an ice cube to melt. Write an equation relating $M$ and $T$ to model this situation.
questions.answer: $M=\dfrac kT$. With $M=20$, $T=9$: $k=180$, so $M=\dfrac{180}T$.

questions.question: (Model $M=\dfrac{180}T$.) How many minutes would it take for an ice cube to melt when the room temperature is $30^\circ$C?
questions.answer:
$M=\dfrac{180}{30}=6$ minutes.
*(The school's solution wrote '6 hours'; the units of $M$ are minutes, so the answer is $6$ minutes.)*

questions.question: Consider the dataset $3,7,11,12,17$. A new value $x$ is added, giving $3,7,11,12,17,x$. It is known that $x$ is greater than $17$, and that the difference between the means of the two datasets is equal to ten times the difference between the medians. Calculate the value of $x$.
questions.answer:
Original: median $=11$, mean $=\dfrac{50}5=10$. New (six values, $x>17$): median $=\dfrac{11+12}2=11.5$, mean $=\dfrac{50+x}6$.
$$\frac{50+x}6-10=10(11.5-11)=5\Rightarrow\frac{50+x}6=15\Rightarrow x=40.$$

questions.question: A tunnel is excavated with a cross-section as shown (four strips each of width $h$, with offsets $0$, $a$, $b$, $a$, $0$). Find an expression in simplest form for the area of the cross-section using the Trapezoidal rule.
questions.answer: $$A\approx\frac h2\big[(0+a)+(a+b)+(b+a)+(a+0)\big]=\frac h2(4a+2b)=h(2a+b)$$

questions.question: (Cross-section area $A=h(2a+b)$, four strips of width $h$.) The area must be $810\ \text{m}^2$. The tunnel is $108$ m wide. If the value of $b$ increases by $4$ metres, by how much will $a$ change?
questions.answer: $4h=108\Rightarrow h=27$. $810=27(2a+b)\Rightarrow2a+b=30\Rightarrow a=15-\dfrac b2$. If $b$ increases by $4$, $a$ becomes $15-\dfrac{b+4}2=\left(15-\dfrac b2\right)-2$. So $a$ decreases by $2$ metres.

questions.question:
Calculate the balance on this credit card at the end of April given that the annual percentage rate is $19.8\%$. Assume that there is no interest-free period on these purchases.

| Date | Details | Amount (\$) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 April | Opening balance | 37 |
| 7 April | Purchase (Kettle) | 65 |
| 16 April | Purchase (Toaster) | 43 |
| 23 April | Payment | −80 |
questions.answer:
Daily rate $=\dfrac{0.198}{365}$; interest is compounded daily on each balance.
- 1–6 April (6 days): $37\left(1+\tfrac{0.198}{365}\right)^6=37.1206$
- 7–15 April (9 days): $(37.1206+65)(1+r)^9=102.6202$
- 16–22 April (7 days): $(102.6202+43)(1+r)^7=146.1740$
- 23–30 April (8 days): $(146.1740-80)(1+r)^8=66.4618$

The balance at the end of April is about $\$66.46$.

questions.question: Linda is driving her car on the motorway where the legal speed limit is $110$ km/h. She notices that an animal is suddenly attempting to cross the road and immediately reacts to apply the brakes. If Linda's reaction time is $1.7$ seconds and she travels $65$ metres in that time, was she travelling within the legal speed limit? Justify your answer using appropriate mathematical calculations.
questions.answer: Speed $=\dfrac{65}{1.7}=38.2$ m/s $=38.2\times3.6=137.65$ km/h. This is greater than $110$ km/h, so she was not within the speed limit (about $27.65$ km/h over).

questions.question: Xian produces small toys at his business. He spent $\$100$ on equipment and ascertained that it will cost $\$2$ to manufacture each toy. Xian plans to sell each toy for $\$4$. If $C$ is the total cost and $R$ the total revenue, in dollars, set up the cost and revenue equations for the sale of $x$ items.
(Cost $C=2x+100$ and revenue $R=4x$.) Plot the graph of the two equations on the grid and determine the break-even point.
questions.answer: Plot $C$ through $(0,100)$ and $(300,700)$, and $R$ through $(0,0)$ and $(300,1200)$. The lines meet where $4x=2x+100\Rightarrow x=50$, $R=C=200$. The break-even point is $(50,\ \$200)$: $50$ toys (see graph).

questions.question: (Cost $C=2x+100$, revenue $R=4x$.) Will Xian make a profit or loss if he produces and sells 100 toys? Determine the amount of the profit or loss.
questions.answer: At $x=100$: $R=\$400$ and $C=\$300$. Revenue exceeds cost, so he makes a profit of $\$100$.

questions.question: Thomas will travel from Melbourne ($38^\circ$S, $145^\circ$E) to Tokyo ($36^\circ$N, $140^\circ$E) on Thursday 21 December. The flight will leave Melbourne at 6.20 pm and will take 10 hours and 30 minutes to reach Tokyo. The time difference between Melbourne and Tokyo is two hours at that time of year. On what day and at what time will Thomas arrive in Tokyo?
questions.answer: Arrival in Melbourne time: $6{:}20$ pm $+10$ h $30$ min $=4{:}50$ am Friday 22 December. Tokyo is $2$ hours behind Melbourne, so he arrives at $2{:}50$ am on Friday 22 December (Tokyo time).

questions.question: Shaun travelled by train to his school and walked from the train station to his school. The school is located $196$ m north and $60$ m west of the train station. What distance will Shaun walk in a straight line from the station to the school? Round to two decimal places.
(School $196$ m north and $60$ m west of the station.) What is the three-figure bearing of the school from the train station, to the nearest degree?
questions.answer: The angle west of north is $\tan^{-1}\dfrac{60}{196}=17^\circ$, so the bearing is $360^\circ-17^\circ=343^\circ$T.

questions.question: Tennis balls are packaged in cylindrical containers. Tim purchases a container that holds three standard tennis balls stacked one on top of the other. The container has a radius of $3.6$ cm and a height of $21.6$ cm. What is the total outside surface area of this container, including both ends? Give your answer in cm$^2$ to one decimal place.
A standard tennis ball is spherical with a radius of $3.6$ cm. Write a calculation that shows that the volume, rounded to one decimal place, of one standard tennis ball is $195.4\ \text{cm}^3$.
Calculate the volume, rounded to one decimal place, of three standard tennis balls.
questions.answer: $3\times195.4=586.2\ \text{cm}^3$ (using the rounded volume; using the unrounded $195.43$ gives $586.3$).

prev.question: A standard tennis ball is spherical with a radius of $3.6$ cm. Write a calculation that shows that the volume, rounded to one decimal place, of one standard tennis ball is $195.4\ \text{cm}^3$.

questions.question: How much unused volume, in cm$^3$, surrounds the tennis balls in this container? Round to one decimal place.
questions.answer: Container volume $=\pi(3.6)^2(21.6)=879.4\ \text{cm}^3$. Unused volume $=879.4-586.2\approx293.2\ \text{cm}^3$.

prev.question: A standard tennis ball is spherical with a radius of $3.6$ cm. Write a calculation that shows that the volume, rounded to one decimal place, of one standard tennis ball is $195.4\ \text{cm}^3$.
Calculate the volume, rounded to one decimal place, of three standard tennis balls.
prev.answer: $3\times195.4=586.2\ \text{cm}^3$ (using the rounded volume; using the unrounded $195.43$ gives $586.3$).

questions.question: The diagram shows two triangles $ABC$ and $ABD$, where $AC=37$ cm, $BD=95$ cm, $\angle ACB=41^\circ$ and $\angle ADB=\theta$. Calculate the size of angle $\theta$, to the nearest minute.
questions.answer: In $\triangle ABC$: $\tan41^\circ=\dfrac{AB}{37}\Rightarrow AB=32.16$ cm. In $\triangle ABD$: $\sin\theta=\dfrac{AB}{95}=0.3385\Rightarrow\theta=19.79^\circ=19^\circ47'$.

questions.question: The information from a compass radial survey of a field is shown in the diagram (distances from $O$: $49$ m on bearing $319^\circ$, $55$ m on $069^\circ$, $37$ m on $145^\circ$, $43$ m on $221^\circ$). Find the perimeter of the field, to the nearest metre.
questions.answer: The angles at $O$: $41^\circ+69^\circ=110^\circ$, $145-69=76^\circ$, $221-145=76^\circ$, $319-221=98^\circ$. By the cosine rule the sides are $85.26$, $58.39$, $49.48$ and $69.54$ m, so the perimeter is $\approx263$ m.

questions.question: (Radial survey: $OA=49$, $OB=55$, $OC=37$, $OD=43$ m; angles at $O$ of $110^\circ$, $76^\circ$, $76^\circ$, $98^\circ$.) Find the area of the field, to the nearest square metre.
questions.answer: $A=\tfrac12(49)(55)\sin110^\circ+\tfrac12(55)(37)\sin76^\circ+\tfrac12(37)(43)\sin76^\circ+\tfrac12(43)(49)\sin98^\circ=4068.6\approx4069\ \text{m}^2$.

questions.question: What is 34 827 368.12 expressed in standard form with two significant figures?
questions.answer: $34\,827\,368.12=3.4827\ldots\times10^7\approx3.5\times10^7$ to 2 significant figures (C).

questions.question: Amie was studying the butterfly population at a park. She caught and marked 20 butterflies and released them back into the park. Later, she caught 40 butterflies, of which 5 were already marked. Based on the number of butterflies Amie has caught and marked, what is the most likely estimate for the butterfly population in the park?
questions.answer: Capture–recapture: $\dfrac{5}{40}=\dfrac{20}{N}$, so $N=\dfrac{20\times40}{5}=160$ (A).

questions.question: Deborah needs to share 140 grams of birdseed equally between five canaries. One of Deborah's birdcages has two canaries in it. How much birdseed should she place in the feeder in that birdcage?
questions.answer: Each canary gets $140\div5=28$ g, so two canaries need $2\times28=56$ g (B).

questions.question: Kabir earns an hourly rate of \$32.46, before he gets a 3.2% pay rise. What is Kabir's new hourly rate?
The weather forecast for a particular week states that each day has a 45% chance of rain one day that week. What is the probability that it does NOT rain over the weekend?
questions.answer: $P(\text{no rain on a day})=1-0.45=0.55$. For both weekend days (independent): $0.55^2=0.3025$ (C).

questions.question: An electrician charges a call-out fee of \$120, as well as \$1.50 per minute while working. Suppose the electrician works for $t$ hours. Which equation expresses the amount the electrician charges, \$$C$, as a function of time, $t$, hours?
questions.answer: \$1.50 per minute is $1.50\times60=\$90$ per hour, so $C=90t+120$ (C).

questions.question: Anna bought a car for \$44 000 in 2013 and sold it after 10 years in 2023. It was depreciated using the declining-balance method, at a rate of 7% per annum. By how much had the car depreciated when Anna sold it?
Joe bought 430 shares in a biomedical company at a total cost of \$5600. The dividend yield was 8.7%. What was the value of the dividend per share?
questions.answer: Dividend yield $=\dfrac{\text{dividend per share}}{\text{market value per share}}\times100$. Market value per share $=\dfrac{5600}{430}$, so dividend per share $=\dfrac{5600}{430}\times0.087=\$1.13$ (B).

questions.question: Which of the following could represent the graph of $y=k(a^x)$, where $k$ is greater than 1, and $a$ is between 0 and 1?
questions.answer: With $0<a<1$ the function is an exponential decay (decreasing), and the $y$-intercept is $k>1$ (here $1.5$). Only graph D decreases and has a $y$-intercept greater than $1$ (D).

questions.question: The network shows the distances, in kilometres, along roads that connect the cities of Austin and Boyle. The shortest distance, in kilometres, from Austin to Boyle is:
questions.answer: The shortest path is along the top: $2+4+1+1=8$ km (A).

questions.question: Nadia is watching a bird at the top of a tree. Nadia is 1.6 m tall and is standing 8 metres away from the tree, as shown in the diagram. If the angle of depression of Nadia from the bird is 73°, what is the height of the tree?
questions.answer: The angle of elevation of the bird from Nadia's eye is $73^\circ$. The height of the bird above eye level is $8\tan73^\circ=26.17$ m, so the tree's height is $26.17+1.6=27.77$ m (D).

questions.question: A teacher is interested in the relationship between the age of students and the size of the groups they choose to sit in at lunch time in the playground. The teacher gathers data and plots the average age of students sitting in a group, $x$, and the number of students in that group, $y$. They construct a scatterplot and draw a line of best fit by eye. The equation of the line of best fit is $y=2.4+0.3x$. Which of the following statements is FALSE?
questions.answer: A: $y=2.4+0.3(12)=6$ ✓. B: $7=2.4+0.3x\Rightarrow x=15.3$ ✓. C: the gradient is positive ✓. D is false: $0.3$ is the gradient of the line, not the correlation coefficient $r$ (D).
options: If the average age of a group is 12, then the line of best fit predicts the group size will be 6 students.
If there is a group with 7 students, then the line of best fit predicts the group will have an average age of 15.3 years.
The students in smaller groups tend to be younger than those in larger groups.
The equation for the line of best fit shows that the correlation coefficient is 0.3, which indicates a weak positive linear relationship.

questions.question: The graph shows the income, in dollars, for a small business that makes and sells picture frames. The cost to make the picture frames is given by the formula $C=10n+20$, where $C$ is the cost and $n$ is the number of picture frames sold. If 6 picture frames are made and sold, which of the following statements is CORRECT?
questions.answer: The income line passes through $(0,0)$ and $(6.67,100)$, so $I=15n$. At $n=6$: income $=\$90$; cost $=10(6)+20=\$80$. Profit $=90-80=\$10$ (A).

questions.question: Macy and Kassidy share a sum of money. Kassidy receives 60% more money than Macy. If Kassidy receives \$176, what is the total amount of money that they share between them?
questions.answer: Kassidy has $160\%$ of Macy's amount: $1.6M=176\Rightarrow M=\$110$. Total $=176+110=\$286$ (B).

questions.question: A sports store sells jerseys priced at \$169.95, including 10% goods and services tax (GST). What is the amount of GST included in the price?
questions.answer: The price is $110\%$ of the pre-GST price: $\dfrac{169.95}{11}=\$15.45$ is the GST (A).

questions.question: A new dryer is being sold for \$599. The dryer uses 315 kWh of electricity per year, and electricity is charged at 28.66 cents per kWh. How much will it cost to purchase and then run the dryer for three years?

The map of Australia shows the six states, the Northern Territory and the Australian Capital Territory (ACT). In the network diagram, each of the vertices A to H represents one of the states or territories. The edges represent a border shared between two states or between a state and a territory. In the network diagram, what is the order (degree) of the vertex that represents the ACT?
questions.answer: The ACT borders only NSW, so its vertex has one edge: the order (degree) is $1$ (it is vertex $D$).

questions.question: The map of Australia shows the six states, the Northern Territory and the ACT. In the network diagram, each of the vertices A to H represents one of these, and the edges represent shared borders. In the network diagram, Queensland is represented by which letter? Explain why.
questions.answer: Queensland is vertex $A$. The ACT (degree 1) is $D$, joined to NSW, the only state it borders, so NSW is $B$ (degree 4: QLD, SA, VIC, ACT). Vertex $A$ has degree 3 and is joined to $B$ (NSW), as Queensland borders NSW. Tasmania ($G$) has no borders, Victoria is $C$ (degree 2), and the other degree-3 vertex $E$ is the NT, which does not border NSW.

questions.question: The following information is known about three towns, $A$, $B$ and $C$, shown on the diagram. Town $A$ is due west of town $B$. Town $C$ is 150 kilometres from town $A$, and 200 kilometres from town $B$. The bearing of town $C$ from town $B$ is $302^\circ$. What is the bearing, $\theta$, of town $C$ from town $A$, correct to the nearest minute?
questions.answer:
$\angle CBA=302^\circ-270^\circ=32^\circ$. By the sine rule in $\triangle ABC$:
$$\frac{\sin\angle CAB}{200}=\frac{\sin32^\circ}{150}\Rightarrow\angle CAB=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{200\sin32^\circ}{150}\right)=44^\circ57'$$
$\theta=90^\circ-44^\circ57'=45^\circ3'$ (i.e. $045^\circ03'$).

questions.question: The child dosage of a particular pain medicine can be calculated using the formula $C=\dfrac{aD}{a+12}$, where $C$ is the child dosage in mL, $a$ is the age of the child in years and $D$ is the adult dosage in mL. For this particular pain medicine, the adult dosage is 15 mL. What is the dosage for a five-year-old child? Give your answer correct to the nearest mL.
questions.answer: $C=\dfrac{5\times15}{5+12}=4.41\ldots\approx4$ mL.

questions.question: The child dosage of a medicine is $C=\dfrac{aD}{a+12}$, where $C$ is the child dosage in mL, $a$ is the age in years and $D$ is the adult dosage, which is 15 mL. At what age will the child dosage be exactly half the adult dosage?
questions.answer: Half the adult dosage is $7.5$ mL: $7.5=\dfrac{15a}{a+12}\Rightarrow7.5(a+12)=15a\Rightarrow90=7.5a\Rightarrow a=12$ years.

questions.question: Ariel purchased a printer for her office three years ago. It depreciated by \$260 each year based on the straight-line method of depreciation. The salvage value of the printer is now \$120. Find the initial value of the printer.
The nutrition information for a box of cupcakes is shown. If 1 calorie is equal to 4.184 joules, what is the total number of kilojoules in the box of cupcakes?
questions.answer:
Total calories $=12\times80=960$. Energy $=960\times4.184=4016.64$ J $=\dfrac{4016.64}{1000}=4.01664$ kJ $\approx4.02$ kJ.

(Note: on real food labels 'Calories' means kilocalories, which would give about $4017$ kJ; the working above follows the conversion given in the question.)

questions.question: A ball is shot vertically into the air from the ground. The height of the ball above the ground, $h$ metres, can be modelled by $h=40t-5t^2$, where $t$ is measured in seconds. The first half of the graph is shown. Based on the graph, or otherwise, at what time does the ball return to the ground?
questions.answer: The graph is symmetric about its vertex at $t=4$, so the ball returns to the ground at $t=8$ s. (Or solve $40t-5t^2=0\Rightarrow5t(8-t)=0$.)

questions.question: The height of a ball above the ground, $h$ metres, is modelled by $h=40t-5t^2$, where $t$ is in seconds. How high is the ball above the ground after 1 second?

The height of a ball above the ground is $h=40t-5t^2$ ($t$ in seconds; it lands at $t=8$). Ben is looking out his window and sees the ball pass the window on its way up, then four seconds later sees it pass the window again on its way down. How high is Ben's window above the ground? Justify your answer.
questions.answer: The graph is symmetric about $t=4$, so the two times are $4$ s apart and equally spaced about $t=4$: $t=2$ and $t=6$. At $t=2$: $h=40(2)-5(4)=60$ m. So the window is $60$ m above the ground.

questions.question: A bag contains 5 white, 8 red and 4 purple marbles. Sarah takes two marbles from the bag (without replacement) and records the outcomes in the tree diagram, as shown. Complete the tree diagram. Include all appropriate outcomes and probabilities.
questions.answer:
There are $17$ marbles.

| First | Second | Probability |
|---|---|---|
| red $\frac{8}{17}$ | red $\frac{7}{16}$ | $\frac{8}{17}\times\frac{7}{16}$ |
| red $\frac{8}{17}$ | not red $\frac{9}{16}$ | $\frac{8}{17}\times\frac{9}{16}$ |
| not red $\frac{9}{17}$ | red $\frac{8}{16}=\frac12$ | $\frac{9}{17}\times\frac12$ |
| not red $\frac{9}{17}$ | not red $\frac{8}{16}=\frac12$ | $\frac{9}{17}\times\frac12$ |

questions.question: A bag contains 5 white, 8 red and 4 purple marbles. Sarah takes two marbles from the bag without replacement. Find the probability that at least ONE of the marbles is RED.
questions.answer: $P(\text{at least one red})=1-P(\text{no red})=1-\dfrac{9}{17}\times\dfrac{8}{16}=1-\dfrac{9}{34}=\dfrac{25}{34}$.

questions.question: The diagram shows the cross-section of the bed of a river as it flows under a bridge. Use two applications of the trapezoidal rule to estimate the area of the cross-section of the river, correct to the nearest square metre.
questions.answer:
The width $38.2$ m is split into two strips of width $h=19.1$ m, with depths $1.2$, $3.5$ and $2.3$ m.
$$A\approx\frac{19.1}{2}(1.2+3.5)+\frac{19.1}{2}(3.5+2.3)=44.885+55.39=100.275\approx100\ \text{m}^2$$

questions.question: The cross-sectional area of a river under a bridge is about 100 m². The water in the river is moving at a rate of 0.4 metres per second. What is the volume of water that flows under the bridge in an hour?
questions.answer: In one hour ($3600$ s) the water travels $0.4\times3600=1440$ m. Volume $=100\times1440=144\,000\ \text{m}^3$ ($\approx144\,396\ \text{m}^3$ using the unrounded area $100.275$ m²).

questions.question: Andrew spent a total of \$131.98 at the supermarket, which included 10% GST on some of the items he bought. The total value of the items which did NOT have GST added was \$40.35. What was the amount Andrew paid at the supermarket excluding GST?
questions.answer: Items with GST (including GST): $131.98-40.35=\$91.63$. GST $=\dfrac{91.63}{11}=\$8.33$. Amount paid excluding GST $=131.98-8.33=\$123.65$.

questions.question:
The table shows the individual tax rates for the 2023–24 financial year.

| Taxable income | Tax payable |
|---|---|
| \$0–\$18 200 | Nil |
| \$18 201–\$45 000 | 19 cents for each \$1 over \$18 200 |
| \$45 001–\$120 000 | \$5092 plus 32.5 cents for each \$1 over \$45 000 |
| \$120 001–\$180 000 | \$29 467 plus 37 cents for each \$1 over \$120 000 |
| \$180 001 and over | \$51 667 plus 45 cents for each \$1 over \$180 000 |

Georgina has a gross annual salary of \$113 700. She is able to claim \$3050 in tax deductions for work-related expenses. She is required to pay the Medicare levy, which is 2% of her taxable income. Calculate Georgina's tax payable, including the Medicare levy. Give your answer correct to the nearest dollar.

Hunter bought 20 000 shares in KSH Mining for \$0.31 each, and 100 000 shares in PSK Mining for 0.2 cents each. While he owned the shares, Hunter received total dividends from the two companies of \$590. When Hunter sold all of the shares, he received \$0.26 per share for the KSH Mining shares and 1.1 cents per share for the PSK Mining shares. Hunter did not have to pay any other fees when he bought or sold the shares. What percentage profit or loss did Hunter make from owning the shares? Answer as a percentage correct to 2 decimal places.

Mackenzie has a credit card with the following conditions: there is no interest-free period; interest is charged at the end of each month at 19.5% per annum, compounded daily, from the purchase date (included) to the last day of the month (included). Mackenzie's credit card statement for October is shown, with some figures missing.

| Date | Details | Amount (\$) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 October | Opening balance | 245.62 |
| 21 October | Monitor | 699.00 |
| 31 October | Interest charged | *** |
| 31 October | Closing balance | *** |

What is Mackenzie's closing balance?
questions.answer:
Daily rate $=\dfrac{0.195}{365}$. The opening balance accrues interest for $31$ days; the monitor for $31-21+1=11$ days.
Interest on opening balance $=245.62\left[\left(1+\frac{0.195}{365}\right)^{31}-1\right]=\$4.10$.
Interest on monitor $=699\left[\left(1+\frac{0.195}{365}\right)^{11}-1\right]=\$4.12$.
Total interest $=\$8.22$. Closing balance $=245.62+699+8.22=\$952.84$.

questions.question: An object is thrown upwards from a cliff that overlooks the sea. The object's motion can be modelled by $h=32+12t-5t^2$, where $h$ is the object's height above the sea in metres and $t$ is the time in seconds. The graph of the function is shown. Find the height of the cliff.
questions.answer: The object starts at $t=0$: $h=32$, so the cliff is $32$ m high.

questions.question: An object is thrown upwards from a cliff: $h=32+12t-5t^2$ ($h$ metres above the sea, $t$ seconds). The graph is shown. State the time it takes for the object to land in the sea.
questions.answer: It lands when $h=0$, at the positive $t$-intercept: $t=4$ s. (Check: $32+48-80=0$.)

questions.question: An object is thrown upwards from a cliff: $h=32+12t-5t^2$. Given that the axis of symmetry of the parabola shown is at $t=1.2$ s, find the maximum height that the object reaches after being thrown.

A closed mailbox, composed of half a cylinder on top of a rectangular prism, is shown (width $17$ cm, length $52$ cm, prism height $15.5$ cm). What is the surface area, in cm², of the closed mailbox? Give your answer to the nearest whole number.
questions.answer:
Half-cylinder: $r=8.5$ cm, length $52$ cm. Curved surface plus two half-circle ends:
$\tfrac12(2\pi r^2+2\pi rh)=\pi(8.5)^2+\pi(8.5)(52)=1615.56$ cm².
Prism (no top, as the cylinder sits on it): $2(17\times15.5)+2(52\times15.5)+17\times52=527+1612+884=3023$ cm².
Total $=1615.56+3023=4638.56\approx4639$ cm².

questions.question:
A random variable is normally distributed with a mean of 0 and a standard deviation of 1. The table gives the probability that this random variable lies below $z$ for some positive values of $z$.

| $z$ | 2.20 | 2.21 | 2.22 | 2.23 | 2.24 | 2.25 | 2.26 | 2.27 | 2.28 | 2.29 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Probability | 0.9861 | 0.9864 | 0.9868 | 0.9871 | 0.9875 | 0.9878 | 0.9881 | 0.9884 | 0.9887 | 0.9890 |

The heights of fourteen-year-old girls in Australia are normally distributed with a mean of 151.2 centimetres and a standard deviation of 7.4 centimetres. In a group of 1000 fourteen-year-old Australian girls, how many would be expected to be over 168 centimetres in height?

The heights of fourteen-year-old girls in Australia are normally distributed with a mean of 151.2 centimetres and a standard deviation of 7.4 centimetres. About 11.6 in 1000 girls are taller than 168 cm ($z=2.27$). In the same group of 1000 girls, how many would be expected to be less than 134.4 centimetres in height?
questions.answer: $z=\dfrac{134.4-151.2}{7.4}=-2.27$. By symmetry of the normal distribution this is the same tail probability, $0.0116$, so about $12$ girls (11.6).

questions.question: A block of land is represented by the shaded region on the number plane. All measurements are in metres. The owner needs to cover the block of land with 50 g of fertiliser per square metre. How many tonnes of fertiliser will they need?

The time taken for a student to ride between their home and school at a constant speed varies inversely with their speed. It takes the student 36 minutes to travel from home to school if they are travelling at 20 kilometres per hour. Calculate the distance between the student's home and school.
questions.answer: Time (hours) $t=\dfrac ks$: $\dfrac{36}{60}=\dfrac{k}{20}\Rightarrow k=12$. The distance is $12$ km.

questions.question: The time taken for a student to ride between their home and school varies inversely with their speed (the home–school distance is 12 km). The student can ride to school at average speeds varying from 6 kilometres per hour to 24 kilometres per hour. By first plotting at least four relevant points, draw the curve that shows the time taken to travel from home to school at different average speeds.
questions.answer: Time in minutes $t=\dfrac{12}{s}\times60=\dfrac{720}{s}$. Points: $(6,120)$, $(8,90)$, $(12,60)$, $(24,30)$. Plot them and join with a smooth decreasing curve (hyperbola).

questions.question:
Businesses often collect data on the total amount of money spent on advertising and total revenue. The table shows information about six consecutive sales quarters for a particular business.

| Sales quarter | Money spent on advertising (\$) | Total revenue (\$) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 15 500 | 61 000 |
| 2 | 18 000 | 62 000 |
| 3 | 23 400 | 81 000 |
| 4 | 32 000 | 94 000 |
| 5 | 32 000 | 102 000 |
| 6 | 40 000 | 150 000 |

Find the equation of the least-squares regression line by calculating the gradient and $y$-intercept. Give these values correct to two decimal places.
questions.answer:
Using the statistics mode on a calculator with $x$ = advertising and $y$ = revenue: gradient $m=3.33$ and $y$-intercept $c=2496.39$.
$$y=2496.39+3.33x$$

questions.question: The manager of a business believes that the data on advertising spend and total revenue over six quarters shows a strong and positive correlation. (Least-squares line: $y=2496.39+3.33x$.) Is the manager correct? Justify your answer using appropriate statistical measure(s) and mathematical reasoning.
questions.answer: Pearson's correlation coefficient is $r=0.95$. This is positive and close to $1$, so there is a strong positive linear correlation. The manager is correct.

questions.question: The diagram shows triangle $ABC$. The triangle has an area of $105.67\ \text{m}^2$, $AC=14$ m and $\angle ACB=57^\circ$. Find the length of $AB$, correct to 2 decimal places.
questions.answer:
Area $=\tfrac12(AC)(BC)\sin C$: $105.67=\tfrac12(14)(BC)\sin57^\circ\Rightarrow BC=\dfrac{105.67}{7\sin57^\circ}=18$ m.
Cosine rule: $AB^2=14^2+18^2-2(14)(18)\cos57^\circ=245.5\ldots$, so $AB=15.67$ m.

questions.question: Jordan wanted to investigate the capacities of different three-dimensional objects. She used two containers: a cone (radius 5 cm, height 8 cm) and a cylinder (radius 2.5 cm, height $h$). When Jordan completely filled the conical container with water and then poured the water into the cylindrical container, she found that the containers had equal volumes. What is the height ($h$) of the cylindrical container, correct to two decimal places?
questions.answer:
$V_{\text{cone}}=\tfrac13\pi(5)^2(8)=209.44\ \text{cm}^3$.
$V_{\text{cylinder}}=\pi(2.5)^2h=209.44\Rightarrow h=\dfrac{209.44}{\pi(6.25)}=10.67$ cm.

questions.question:
The table below shows the monthly repayments on loans of various amounts over a number of different loan periods.

| Principal | 2 years | 5 years | 7 years |
|---|---|---|---|
| \$10 000 | \$480 | \$228 | \$187 |
| \$20 000 | \$960 | \$455 | \$374 |
| \$30 000 | \$1439 | \$683 | \$561 |

Spiro is borrowing \$30 000, to be repaid with monthly repayments over 5 years. How much interest will be paid on the loan?
Spiro borrows \$30 000 and repays \$683 per month for 5 years, so the total interest paid is \$10 980. Calculate the percentage flat rate of interest per annum on this loan.

The compass radial survey shows the position of four towns: $A$, $B$, $C$ and $X$. Towns $A$ and $B$ lie at true bearings of $328^\circ$ and $110^\circ$ from town $X$, respectively. All distances between the towns are given in metres. Find the distance between towns $A$ and $B$, correct to the nearest metre.
questions.answer:
$\angle AXB=(360^\circ-328^\circ)+110^\circ=142^\circ$. Cosine rule with $XA=25$, $XB=28$:
$AB^2=25^2+28^2-2(25)(28)\cos142^\circ\Rightarrow AB=50$ m.

questions.question: In a compass radial survey, towns $B$ and $C$ are at distances $28$ m and $19$ m from town $X$, and $B$ lies at a true bearing of $110^\circ$ from $X$. If the area of triangle $XCB$ is $265\ \text{m}^2$, find the true bearing of town $C$ from town $X$. Give your answer correct to the nearest degree.
questions.answer:
$265=\tfrac12(19)(28)\sin\angle CXB\Rightarrow\sin\angle CXB=\dfrac{265}{266}\Rightarrow\angle CXB=85^\circ$ (taking the acute angle).
True bearing of $C$ from $X=110^\circ+85^\circ=195^\circ$.

questions.question:
Elena takes out a loan of \$150 000 with Westpac bank, which has an interest rate of 6.14% per annum. She makes regular monthly repayments of \$1000. Elena uses the table shown to calculate her interest. In the table, $n$ is the number of months, $P$ is the outstanding balance of the loan, $I$ is the monthly interest charged, and $R$ is the monthly repayment.

| $n$ | $P$ | $I$ | $P+I$ | $P+I-R$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | \$150 000 | \$767.50 | \$150 767.50 | \$149 767.50 |
| 2 | | | | $A_2$ |

Complete the table to find the value of $A_2$.

Elena takes out a loan of \$150 000 at 6.14% per annum, making monthly repayments of \$1000. Let $A_n$ be the value of Elena's loan after $n$ months. Complete the recurrence relation $A_0=\_\_\_$, $A_{n+1}=\_\_\_\times A_n-\_\_\_$ to model the value of this loan over time. Give your answers correct to three decimal places.
questions.answer:
Monthly interest rate $=\dfrac{0.0614}{12}=0.005117\approx0.005$, so the multiplier is $1.005$.
$$A_0=150\,000,\qquad A_{n+1}=1.005\,A_n-1000$$

questions.question:
After the second month, Elena realises that the interest she pays is very high ($A_2=\$149\,533.81$). She decides to switch her loan and repayments to Commonwealth Bank for the remaining 142 months, which offers an interest rate of 6% per annum. The table shows the present value for an annuity of \$1 (excerpt):

| Period | 0.5% |
|---|---|
| 132 | 96.460 |
| 142 | 101.497 |
| 144 | 102.475 |

Using the table, calculate the total interest that Elena will pay to Commonwealth Bank if she repays the loan in full after 12 years.
questions.answer:
The rate is $\dfrac{6\%}{12}=0.5\%$ per month for $142$ periods, so the annuity factor is $101.497$.
Monthly repayment $=\dfrac{149\,533.81}{101.497}=\$1473.28$.
Total interest $=1473.28\times142+1000\times2-150\,000=\$61\,206.19$ (using the unrounded repayment; $\approx\$61\,206$).

questions.question: Consider the network diagram. What is the sum of the degrees of all the vertices in this network?
questions.answer: Degrees: $A=2$, $B=4$ (including the curved edge to $C$), $C=3$, $D=3$, $E=2$. Sum $=14$, which is twice the 7 edges (D).

questions.question: A new mountain bike was purchased for \$1386, including 10% GST. What was the price of the bike before GST, correct to the nearest dollar?
questions.answer: The price including GST is $110\%$ of the original price: $1386\div1.1=\$1260$ (B).

questions.question: Most cars use fuel that is a blend of 90% petrol and 10% ethanol. What is the ratio of petrol to ethanol in this blend?
Consider the line below. What is the equation of the line?
questions.answer: The $y$-intercept is 4 and the line falls 2 units for every 1 unit to the right (through $(2,0)$), so the gradient is $-2$: $y=-2x+4$ (D).

questions.question: What is the correct expression for the value of $x$ in this triangle?
questions.answer: The side of length 4 is adjacent to the $65^\circ$ angle and $x$ is the hypotenuse, so $\cos65^\circ=\dfrac4x$ and $x=\dfrac{4}{\cos65^\circ}$ (A).

questions.question: Young's formula is used to calculate the required dosages of medicine for children aged 1–12 years: $\text{Dosage}=\dfrac{\text{age of child (in years)}\times\text{adult dosage}}{\text{age of child (in years)}+12}$. The adult dosage is 45 mL. How much medicine should be given to an 18-month-old child in a 24-hour period if the child has a dose of medicine every 6 hours?
questions.answer: Age $=1.5$ years: dose $=\dfrac{1.5\times45}{1.5+12}=5$ mL. There are $24\div6=4$ doses in 24 hours, so the total is $4\times5=20$ mL (B).

questions.question: A table of future value interest factors for an annuity of \$1 is shown. Peta made equal contributions of \$2500 into an account at the end of every 6 months for 2 years at an interest rate of 4% per annum. What is the future value of this annuity?
questions.answer: There are $4$ periods and the rate is $2\%$ per period, so the factor is $4.1216$. $FV=2500\times4.1216=\$10\,304.00$ (A).

questions.question: The costs of two mobile phone plans are Plan A: $y=0.1x+15$ and Plan B: $y=0.2x+10$, where $y$ is the total monthly cost in dollars and $x$ is the number of call minutes used. The equations are graphed on the same axes below. At what number of call minutes do both plans cost the same?
questions.answer: The lines intersect at $x=50$ (algebraically $0.1x+15=0.2x+10\Rightarrow x=50$), where both plans cost \$20 (D).

questions.question: A map has a scale of 1:20 000. Two towns are 12 km apart in real life. How far apart are the two towns on the map, in centimetres?
The daily production costs and revenue from the sale of a particular item are shown on the graph. Which statement is incorrect?
questions.answer: The lines intersect at 5 items (\$10), the break-even point, so no profit is made at 5 items and statement C is incorrect. At 10 items revenue is \$20 and cost is \$15 (profit \$5), and at 15 items revenue is \$30 and cost is \$20 (profit \$10).
options: If 5 items are sold, no profit is made.
If 10 items are sold a profit of \$5 is made.
If 5 items are sold, a profit of \$10 is made.
If 15 items are sold a profit of \$10 is made.

questions.question: A factory has a large juice tank that holds 16 kL of freshly squeezed orange juice. If each bottle holds 750 mL, approximately how many bottles can be filled?
The diagram shows a radial survey of a field $ABCD$. What is the distance between $A$ and $B$, correct to the nearest metre?
questions.answer: $A$ is on a bearing of $308^\circ$ and $B$ on $060^\circ$ from $O$, so $\angle AOB=360^\circ-308^\circ+60^\circ=112^\circ$. By the cosine rule $AB^2=100^2+30^2-2(100)(30)\cos112^\circ\approx13\,147.6$, so $AB\approx114.7\approx115$ m (B).

questions.question: A coin is biased so it shows heads to tails in the ratio of 2:3 when it is tossed. Find the number of heads expected if the coin is tossed 100 times.
questions.answer: $P(\text{head})=\dfrac25$, so the expected number of heads is $\dfrac25\times100=40$ (B).

questions.question: Two identical spheres fit exactly inside a cylindrical container, as shown. The diameter of each sphere is 10 cm. What is the volume of the cylindrical container, to the nearest cubic centimetre?
questions.answer: The cylinder has radius 5 cm and height $2\times10=20$ cm: $V=\pi r^2h=\pi(5)^2(20)\approx1571$ cm$^3$ (B).

questions.question: A random variable is normally distributed with a mean of 0 and a standard deviation of 1. The probability that this random variable lies below $a$, for some positive value of $a$, is represented by the shaded area. Which of the following statements is false?
questions.answer: By symmetry $P(z<-a)=P(z>a)$ (A) and $P(z>-a)=P(z<a)=1-P(z>a)$ (B). The central area is $P(z<a)-P(z<-a)=P(z<a)-(1-P(z<a))=2P(z<a)-1$ (C is true), so D, which has the opposite sign, is false. For example if $P(z<a)=0.9$ then $P(-a<z<a)=0.8$, but $1-2(0.9)=-0.8$.

questions.question: The number of points per game scored by a basketball team in a season is normally distributed with a mean of 116 points per game and a standard deviation of 2. What percentage of games will have between 112 and 118 points scored?
questions.answer: $112$ is 2 standard deviations below the mean ($z=-2$) and $118$ is 1 standard deviation above the mean ($z=1$). By the empirical rule, $\dfrac12(95\%)+\dfrac12(68\%)=47.5\%+34\%=81.5\%$.

questions.question: Solve $2x=\dfrac{x}{2}+6$.
questions.answer: Multiply both sides by 2: $4x=x+12$, so $3x=12$ and $x=4$.

questions.question: Use the trapezoidal rule to approximate the shaded area on the diagram (the parallel sides are 12 m and 8 m, and the distance between them is 8 m).
questions.answer: $A\approx\dfrac h2(d_f+d_l)=\dfrac82(12+8)=80\text{ m}^2$.

questions.question: Express 0.0009028 in scientific (standard) form. Give your answer correct to three significant figures.
Mona's heart beats 72 times per minute. How many times will it beat in 24 hours?
questions.answer: $72\times60\times24=103\,680$ beats.

questions.question: Make $y$ the subject of the equation $a=\sqrt{by-1}$.
questions.answer: Square both sides: $a^2=by-1$, so $by=a^2+1$ and $y=\dfrac{a^2+1}{b}$.

questions.question: Ray owns 1800 shares in a company. The total market price for the portfolio is \$27 000. Ray's dividend for each share is \$1.20. Calculate the dividend yield for his shares.
questions.answer: Share price $=\dfrac{27\,000}{1800}=\$15$. Dividend yield $=\dfrac{1.20}{15}=0.08=8\%$.

questions.question:
Jack and Judy are planning a fund-raising dance. They hire a hall for \$400 and a band for \$300. Refreshments will cost \$12 per person. The graph shows planned income and cost with the ticket price set at \$20 per person.

Write a formula for the cost (\$$C$) of running the dance for $x$ people.
questions.answer: Fixed costs are $400+300=\$700$ and refreshments are \$12 per person: $C=12x+700$.

questions.question:
Jack and Judy are planning a fund-raising dance. They hire a hall for \$400 and a band for \$300. Refreshments will cost \$12 per person. The graph shows planned income and cost with the ticket price set at \$20 per person.

Estimate the minimum number of people needed at the dance to cover the cost.
questions.answer: The income and cost lines intersect at about 88 people (the school's answer: about 90). Algebraically $20x=12x+700$ gives $x=87.5$, so at least 88 people are needed.

questions.question:
Jack and Judy are planning a fund-raising dance. They hire a hall for \$400 and a band for \$300. Refreshments will cost \$12 per person. The graph shows planned income and cost with the ticket price set at \$20 per person.

How much profit will be made if 150 people attend the dance?

Jack and Judy hire a hall for \$400 and a band for \$300, and refreshments cost \$12 per person. They plan to sell 200 tickets and want to make a profit of \$1500. What should be the price of a ticket, assuming all 200 tickets will be sold?
questions.answer: Cost for 200 people $=12(200)+700=\$3100$. Let the ticket price be $p$: income $=200p$. Profit $=$ income $-$ cost, so $1500=200p-3100$, giving $200p=4600$ and $p=\$23$.

questions.question: A bag contains 7 red balls and 13 blue balls. Two balls are selected at random without replacement. Draw a probability tree and calculate the probability of selecting two balls of the same colour.
questions.answer:
First draw: $P(R)=\dfrac7{20}$, $P(B)=\dfrac{13}{20}$. Second draw (no replacement): after a red, $P(R)=\dfrac6{19}$ and $P(B)=\dfrac{13}{19}$; after a blue, $P(R)=\dfrac7{19}$ and $P(B)=\dfrac{12}{19}$.

$P(\text{same colour})=P(RR)+P(BB)=\dfrac7{20}\times\dfrac6{19}+\dfrac{13}{20}\times\dfrac{12}{19}=\dfrac{42+156}{380}=\dfrac{99}{190}$.

questions.question: The school librarian records the reasons students visited the help desk during Term 1: Research Help 24 (cumulative frequency 24, cumulative percentage 48); Wifi Issues A (cumulative frequency 28, 56%); Find Book 12 (cumulative frequency 40, 80%); Printing Issues 5 (cumulative frequency B, 90%); New Card 3 (cumulative frequency 48, 99%); Forgotten Password 2 (cumulative frequency 50, 100%). The total is 50. What are the values of $A$ and $B$?
The box plot for a dataset is given. Is 10 an outlier? Justify your answer with calculations.
questions.answer: From the box plot $Q_1=3$ and $Q_3=7$, so $\text{IQR}=7-3=4$. The upper fence is $Q_3+1.5\times\text{IQR}=7+1.5\times4=13$. Since $10<13$, 10 is not an outlier.

questions.question: Charles's taxable income is \$88 225. Tax payable: \$0–\$18 200 nil; \$18 201–\$45 000: 16c for each \$1 over \$18 200; \$45 001–\$135 000: \$4288 plus 30c for each \$1 over \$45 000; \$135 001–\$190 000: \$31 288 plus 37c for each \$1 over \$135 000; \$190 001 and over: \$51 638 plus 45c for each \$1 over \$190 000. In addition he pays the Medicare levy, which is 2% of his taxable income. Calculate Charles's total tax payable.

The heights and weights of 8 preschoolers: heights $h$ (cm) 102, 100, 105, 98, 104, 99, 103, 101 with weights $w$ (kg) 16.5, 15.2, 17.8, 14.6, 17.2, 15, 16.1, 15.6 respectively.

Calculate the correlation coefficient, $r$. Give your answer correct to three significant figures.
questions.answer: Using a calculator's statistics mode: $r=0.9678\ldots\approx0.968$.

questions.question:
The heights and weights of 8 preschoolers: heights $h$ (cm) 102, 100, 105, 98, 104, 99, 103, 101 with weights $w$ (kg) 16.5, 15.2, 17.8, 14.6, 17.2, 15, 16.1, 15.6 respectively. The correlation coefficient is $r=0.968$.

Comment on the strength of the correlation.
questions.answer: $r=0.968$ is close to $+1$, so there is a very strong positive linear correlation between height and weight.

questions.question:
The heights and weights of 8 preschoolers: heights $h$ (cm) 102, 100, 105, 98, 104, 99, 103, 101 with weights $w$ (kg) 16.5, 15.2, 17.8, 14.6, 17.2, 15, 16.1, 15.6 respectively.

Find the equation of the least-squares regression line. Give the values in the equation correct to two decimal places.
questions.answer: From the calculator, the gradient is $0.4405\ldots\approx0.44$ and the intercept is $-28.7083\ldots\approx-28.71$, so $w=-28.71+0.44h$.

questions.question: The least-squares regression line for the heights ($h$ cm) and weights ($w$ kg) of preschoolers is $w=-28.71+0.44h$. Predict the weight of a preschooler who is 108 cm tall.
questions.answer: $w=-28.71+0.44(108)=18.81$ kg, so about 18.8 kg (using the unrounded line, 18.86 kg). Note that 108 cm is above the data range, so this is an extrapolation.

questions.question: Robert is buying a new car with a sale price of \$22 850. Stamp duty is calculated at \$3 for every \$100, or part thereof, of the sale price. Calculate the stamp duty payable.
questions.answer: $22\,850\div100=228.5$, so there are 229 lots of \$100 (including the part). Stamp duty $=229\times3=\$687$.

questions.question: Robert buys a new car for \$22 850. The total purchase costs include a \$79 registration fee, a \$55 number plate fee, stamp duty of \$687 and vehicle tax. Vehicle tax is based on the tare weight of the vehicle. The car has a tare weight of 1250 kg and is for private use. The private use fee is: up to 975 kg \$266; 976–1154 kg \$308; 1155–1504 kg \$374; 1505–2504 kg \$570; 2505–2794 kg \$822. Calculate the total amount Robert pays.
questions.answer: A tare weight of 1250 kg is in the 1155–1504 kg band, so the vehicle tax is \$374. Fees $=79+55+687+374=\$1195$. Total $=22\,850+1195=\$24\,045$.

questions.question: Robert has decided he will take out comprehensive car insurance in addition to the compulsory third party insurance. State ONE extra cover that is provided by the comprehensive car insurance.
questions.answer: Comprehensive insurance covers damage to Robert's own car (e.g. from an accident, theft, fire or storm); third-party insurance covers only injury to other people.

questions.question:
Jo has signed up for a premium gym membership. The upfront cost is \$3600, but the gym offers a payment plan allowing members to pay in equal quarterly instalments over 2 years, with an annual interest rate of 8% p.a. compounded quarterly. Present value interest factors for an annuity of \$1 include: 2% per period, 8 periods: 7.3255.

Find the value of each quarterly instalment Jo needs to make.
questions.answer: There are $N=8$ quarterly payments at $r=\dfrac8{4}=2\%$ per quarter, so the present value factor is 7.3255. $PV=\text{payment}\times\text{factor}$, so the payment $=\dfrac{3600}{7.3255}=\$491.43$.

questions.question: Jo pays 8 equal quarterly instalments of \$491.43. Find the total amount he will repay over the 2 years.
Jo's gym membership costs \$3600 upfront, or 8 quarterly instalments totalling \$3931.44. Find the total interest paid over the life of the payment plan.
Sue lives in New York ($40^\circ$ N, $74^\circ$ W). She plans to travel to Copenhagen, which is $15^\circ$ north and $86^\circ$ east of New York. What is the latitude and longitude of Copenhagen?
questions.answer: Latitude $=40^\circ+15^\circ=55^\circ$ N. Longitude: moving $86^\circ$ east from $74^\circ$ W gives $86-74=12^\circ$ E. Copenhagen is $55^\circ$ N, $12^\circ$ E.

questions.question: Copenhagen is in UTC+2 and New York is in UTC$-5$. Sue's plane leaves New York at 6:00 pm on Friday local time and flies non-stop to Copenhagen. The flight takes 9 hours and 50 minutes. What time and day is it in Copenhagen when the plane lands?
questions.answer: Copenhagen is $2-(-5)=7$ hours ahead of New York. Departure is 6:00 pm Friday in New York $=$ 1:00 am Saturday in Copenhagen. Adding the flight time of 9 h 50 min gives 10:50 am Saturday in Copenhagen.

questions.question:
A logistics company manages deliveries between a group of towns using one-way roads. The distances (km) are: Mapleton (M) to Brookvale (B) 8; M to Clearwater (C) 20; B to C 10; B to Riverton (R) 15; C to R 8; C to Stonebridge (S) 25; R to S 16.

Draw a weighted directed network diagram to represent the information.
questions.answer: The network has five vertices (M, B, C, R, S) and seven directed, weighted edges, one for each row of the table, as shown in the diagram.

questions.question: A logistics company manages deliveries between a group of towns using one-way roads. The distances (km) are: Mapleton (M) to Brookvale (B) 8; M to Clearwater (C) 20; B to C 10; B to Riverton (R) 15; C to R 8; C to Stonebridge (S) 25; R to S 16. A delivery needs to be made from Mapleton to Stonebridge and charges \$2.30 per km travelled. What is the lowest price the company could charge for this delivery?
questions.answer: Paths from M to S: M–B–R–S $=8+15+16=39$ km; M–B–C–S $=8+10+25=43$ km; M–B–C–R–S $=8+10+8+16=42$ km; M–C–R–S $=20+8+16=44$ km; M–C–S $=20+25=45$ km. The shortest path is M–B–R–S, 39 km. Lowest price $=39\times2.30=\$89.70$.

questions.question: The average daily step count of CodeNest staff is 8000 steps, with a standard deviation of 1200 steps. On a particular day, Oliver recorded 5600 steps. Calculate Oliver's $z$-score.

CodeNest has 280 employees, with an average daily step count of 8000 steps and a standard deviation of 1200 steps. Assuming the step counts are normally distributed, approximately how many employees recorded a higher step count than Oliver (5600 steps, $z=-2$) on that day?
questions.answer: By the empirical rule, $P(z<-2)\approx2.5\%$, so $P(z>-2)\approx50\%+47.5\%=97.5\%$. Number $\approx0.975\times280=273$ employees.

questions.question: Claudia has a credit card which has an interest rate of 16% per annum. The interest is compounded daily and is charged on the amount owing with no interest-free period. The period for which interest is charged includes the date of purchase and the date of payment. On 10th March, Claudia purchased tickets for \$620 using her credit card. No other purchases were made using this card for the remainder of the month. What amount was paid when the account was paid in full on 5th April?
questions.answer: Daily rate $=\dfrac{16\%}{365}=\dfrac{0.16}{365}$. Days from 10 March to 5 April inclusive: $22$ (10–31 March) $+5=27$ days. $FV=620\left(1+\dfrac{0.16}{365}\right)^{27}=\$627.38$.

questions.question: A random variable is normally distributed with mean 0 and standard deviation 1. The table gives the probability that this random variable lies below $z$. A manufacturer produces luxury scented candles. The mass of wax in each candle is normally distributed with a mean of 300 grams and a standard deviation of 4 grams. What percentage of candles would you expect to contain more than 302 grams of wax?
questions.answer: $z=\dfrac{302-300}{4}=0.5$. From the table $P(z<0.5)=0.691$, so $P(z>0.5)=1-0.691=0.309$. About 30.9% of candles contain more than 302 g.

questions.question: An outdoor adventurer uses a pedal-powered generator to recharge the battery of her satellite communication device while camping off-grid. While pedalling she burns energy at a rate of 720 kilocalories per hour. The generator converts this energy and stores it as electricity in the device's battery. Her device requires 1.8 kWh of electricity per day. How long must she pedal each day to generate enough energy to power the device? Give your answer in hours and minutes, correct to the nearest minute. (1 kcal = 4.184 kJ and 3600 kJ = 1 kWh.)
questions.answer: Energy needed $=1.8\times3600=6480$ kJ. Energy produced per hour $=720\times4.184=3012.48$ kJ. Time $=\dfrac{6480}{3012.48}=2.151$ h $=2$ h $9$ min (to the nearest minute).

questions.question:
The drama department at a school is planning a school musical. Activities (duration in weeks; predecessors): A Write script (5; none); B Audition cast (2; A); C Design set and costumes (4; A); D Cast rehearsals (6; B); E Build set and create costumes (3; C); F Rehearse with full staging (4; D, E); G Technical setup (1; E); H Final dress rehearsal (1; F, G).

Complete the network diagram for the school musical production (part of it is drawn).
questions.answer: Activity D ends at the node where F begins. E ends at the node where G begins. F needs both D and E, so a dummy activity (dashed) joins the end of E to the start of F. F and G both lead to the node where H begins.

questions.question:
The drama department at a school is planning a school musical. Activities (duration in weeks; predecessors): A Write script (5; none); B Audition cast (2; A); C Design set and costumes (4; A); D Cast rehearsals (6; B); E Build set and create costumes (3; C); F Rehearse with full staging (4; D, E); G Technical setup (1; E); H Final dress rehearsal (1; F, G).

Identify the critical path and determine the minimum time needed to complete the project.
questions.answer: Path lengths: A–B–D–F–H $=5+2+6+4+1=18$; A–C–E–F–H $=5+4+3+4+1=17$; A–C–E–G–H $=5+4+3+1+1=14$. The longest path is the critical path: A–B–D–F–H, so the minimum completion time is 18 weeks.

questions.question:
The drama department at a school is planning a school musical. Activities (duration in weeks; predecessors): A Write script (5; none); B Audition cast (2; A); C Design set and costumes (4; A); D Cast rehearsals (6; B); E Build set and create costumes (3; C); F Rehearse with full staging (4; D, E); G Technical setup (1; E); H Final dress rehearsal (1; F, G).

What is the float time for Activity E?
questions.answer: E has EST $=5+4=9$ and duration 3. It must finish before F can start at its LST. F's EST is $5+2+6=13$, so E's latest finish is 13 and its LST is $13-3=10$. Float $=\text{LST}-\text{EST}=10-9=1$ week.

questions.question:
The drama department at a school is planning a school musical. Activities (duration in weeks; predecessors): A Write script (5; none); B Audition cast (2; A); C Design set and costumes (4; A); D Cast rehearsals (6; B); E Build set and create costumes (3; C); F Rehearse with full staging (4; D, E); G Technical setup (1; E); H Final dress rehearsal (1; F, G).

Activity C is delayed by 3 weeks, causing a delay to the entire production. By how many weeks is the overall production delayed?
questions.answer: Path A–C–E–F–H has 1 week of float (it takes 17 weeks against the 18-week critical path). A 3-week delay on C makes this path 20 weeks, so the project finishes $20-18=2$ weeks late.

questions.question:
HydroCity relies on a network of water pipes to supply clean water from its main reservoir to three suburbs: Northview, Eastgate and Southbank. Each pipe has a maximum capacity in kilolitres per hour, shown on the diagram.

Calculate the capacity of the cut drawn on the network.
questions.answer: The cut separates the Main Reservoir and $B$ from the rest of the network. The pipes crossing it from the source side to the sink side are Main–$A$ (30), $B$–$C$ (8) and $B$–Southbank (15). Pipe $A$–$B$ flows back across the cut and is not counted. Capacity $=30+8+15=53$ kL/h.

questions.question:
HydroCity relies on a network of water pipes to supply clean water from its main reservoir to three suburbs: Northview, Eastgate and Southbank. Each pipe has a maximum capacity in kilolitres per hour, shown on the diagram.

Determine the maximum flow of the network.
questions.answer: The two pipes leaving the Main Reservoir have capacities 30 and 20, a cut of capacity $30+20=50$ kL/h. The flow can reach 50 (e.g. $A$–Northview 20, $A$–$C$ 10, $B$–Southbank 15, $B$–$C$ 5, $C$–Eastgate 15), so by the max-flow min-cut theorem the maximum flow is 50 kL/h.

questions.question:
HydroCity relies on a network of water pipes to supply clean water from its main reservoir to three suburbs: Northview, Eastgate and Southbank. Each pipe has a maximum capacity in kilolitres per hour, shown on the diagram.

Pipe $BC$ is due for repairs and will undergo a renovation that will increase its capacity. Will the increase in capacity in Pipe $BC$ change the maximum flow of the network? Justify your answer with mathematical reasoning or calculation.
questions.answer: No. The minimum cut is the two pipes leaving the source (capacity $30+20=50$ kL/h), which does not include $BC$. The flow out of the source is already at its maximum, so no extra water can pass through the network, and increasing the capacity of $BC$ does not change the maximum flow of 50 kL/h.

questions.question: A new leisure centre is designed with a running track on its perimeter. The track follows the entire outer edge of the shape shown, which comprises a rectangle and two semicircles. The straight sections are each 90 m. The length of the running track is 400 m. Find the length of the diameter of the semicircles, correct to the nearest whole metre.
questions.answer: The two semicircles form one circle of circumference $\pi d$. $90+90+\pi d=400$, so $\pi d=220$ and $d=\dfrac{220}{\pi}=70.03\approx70$ m.

questions.question: It takes Piper 2 minutes to run around a 400 m track. What was Piper's average speed in kilometres per hour?

The diagram shows the location of three landmarks in a national park: a Ranger Station $R$, a Waterfall $W$ and a Campsite $C$. The Ranger Station is due north of the Waterfall and $\angle RWC=130^\circ$. Isla and Gabriel go on solo hikes from the Waterfall, leaving at 2 pm. Isla arrives at the Ranger Station at 3 pm, travelling at 5 km/h. Gabriel travels directly to the Campsite and arrives at 4 pm, travelling at 7 km/h.

Show that the shortest distance between Isla and Gabriel when they have reached their destinations is 18 km, to the nearest kilometre.
questions.answer: $RW=5\times1=5$ km and $WC=7\times2=14$ km. By the cosine rule in $\triangle RWC$: $RC^2=5^2+14^2-2(5)(14)\cos130^\circ\approx311.0$, so $RC\approx17.6\approx18$ km.

questions.question:
The diagram shows the location of three landmarks in a national park: a Ranger Station $R$, a Waterfall $W$ and a Campsite $C$. The Ranger Station is due north of the Waterfall and $\angle RWC=130^\circ$. Isla and Gabriel go on solo hikes from the Waterfall, leaving at 2 pm. Isla arrives at the Ranger Station at 3 pm, travelling at 5 km/h. Gabriel travels directly to the Campsite and arrives at 4 pm, travelling at 7 km/h. Take $RC=18$ km.

Determine the bearing of the Ranger Station from the Campsite, correct to the nearest degree.
questions.answer: Let $\theta=\angle WRC$. By the sine rule, $\dfrac{\sin\theta}{14}=\dfrac{\sin130^\circ}{18}$, so $\sin\theta=\dfrac{14\sin130^\circ}{18}$ and $\theta\approx36.6^\circ\approx37^\circ$. Since $RW$ is a north–south line, the north line at $C$ is parallel to $RW$, and the alternate angle at $C$ is also $\theta$. The Ranger Station lies north-east of the Campsite, so the bearing is $037^\circ$. (The exact $RC=17.63$ gives $37.5^\circ$, which also rounds to $037^\circ$; using the rounded $RC=18$ with other methods can give slightly different values, e.g. $032^\circ$ or $038^\circ$.)

questions.question: Jenna is designing a logo using two circles with a diamond feature in the middle. The centre of each circle lies on the circumference of the other. Both circles have the same radius of 4 cm. The shaded area (everything inside either circle except the white diamond) needs glitter. Find the shaded area, correct to two decimal places.
questions.answer:
The diamond is made of two equilateral triangles of side 4 cm (the sides are all radii), so each circle has an angle of $60^\circ+60^\circ=120^\circ$ at its centre inside the diamond. Each circle's shaded part is therefore a sector of angle $360^\circ-60^\circ-60^\circ=240^\circ$ (this includes the part of the lens outside the diamond).

Shaded area $=2\times\dfrac{240}{360}\times\pi\times4^2=\dfrac{2\cdot2}{3}\cdot16\pi\approx67.02$ cm$^2$.

questions.question: The distance between Hillgrove and Riverpoint is 105 km. A driver travels from Hillgrove to Riverpoint at an average speed of 60 km/h. How long does it take the driver to complete the journey?
questions.answer: $t = \dfrac{105}{60} = 1.75$ hours $= 1$ hour $45$ minutes. **(C)**

questions.question: What is $0.0003641$ expressed in standard form with two significant figures?
Which of the following expresses $p$ as the subject of the formula $q = \dfrac{mp + n}{2}$?
questions.answer: $2q = mp + n \Rightarrow mp = 2q - n \Rightarrow p = \dfrac{2q - n}{m}$. **(A)**

questions.question: Which of the following could be the graph of $y = 5x - 5$?
questions.answer: The gradient is positive ($5$), the $y$-intercept is $-5$ and the $x$-intercept is $1$. Only graph B rises to the right, cuts the $y$-axis below the origin and cuts the $x$-axis to the right of the origin. **(B)**

questions.question: Alex invests \$800 for 18 months at a simple interest rate of 3% per annum in a fixed term deposit. What is the value of the investment after 18 months?

A doctor prescribes 900 grams of medication per day to be taken every 3 hours. The medication is provided in liquid form with a concentration of 60 grams per 6 millilitres. How many millilitres should the patient take per dose?
questions.answer: Doses per day $= 24 \div 3 = 8$, so each dose is $900 \div 8 = 112.5$ g. The concentration is $60\ \text{g} / 6\ \text{mL} = 10$ g per mL, so the volume is $112.5 \div 10 = 11.25$ mL. **(B)**

questions.question: A small business purchased a delivery van five years ago. Since its purchase, the van has depreciated in value by \$2300 per year under the straight-line method of depreciation. At the end of the five-year period, the current (salvage) value of the van is estimated to be \$7500. What was the original purchase price of the van?
