A fitness study recorded the time spent exercising each weekend by a group of Year 12 boys and girls. The results are displayed in the box plots. Which of the following best describes the patterns in exercise duration for boys and girls?
questions.answer: Boys: five-number summary $1, 2, 5, 6, 7$ (median 5). Girls: $0, 2, 3, 5, 6$ (median 3). The boys' median (5 h) is higher than the girls' median (3 h). The IQRs are $4$ (boys) and $3$ (girls), so B is false, and the boys' median is closer to $Q_3$ (negatively skewed), so A and C are false. **(D)**
options: The boys' exercise times are positively skewed, while the girls' times are symmetrical.
The girls' data is more variable, with a wider interquartile range than the boys.
The girls' distribution is positively skewed, while the boys' distribution is symmetrical.
The median exercise time for boys is higher than that for girls.

questions.question: Suppose $y = -4 + 3x$. When the value of $x$ increases by 4, the value of $y$ increases by:
questions.answer: The gradient is $3$, so $y$ increases by $3 \times 4 = 12$. **(C)**

questions.question: A group of 8 volunteers can pack food hampers in 12 hours. The time taken to complete the task varies inversely with the number of volunteers working at a constant rate. How long would it take a group of 7 volunteers to complete the same task?
questions.answer: $t = \dfrac{k}{n}$, so $12 = \dfrac{k}{8}$ and $k = 96$. For $n = 7$: $t = \dfrac{96}{7} \approx 13.7$ hours. **(B)**

questions.question: A homeowner received a written quotation of \$18 250 from a builder to complete renovation work. This amount includes 10% GST. The builder offers a cash payment option in which the GST is not charged. How much would the homeowner pay if they choose to pay in cash?
questions.answer: The quote is $110\%$ of the pre-GST price: $18\,250 \div 1.1 = \$16\,590.91$. **(C)**

questions.question: A koala is stranded on top of an 11 metre telegraph pole. From the top of the telegraph pole, the angle of depression of the rescue vehicle is $30^\circ$. How far from the base of the telegraph pole is the rescue vehicle, to the nearest metre?
questions.answer: The angle of depression equals the angle of elevation from the vehicle, so $\tan 30^\circ = \dfrac{11}{x}$ and $x = \dfrac{11}{\tan 30^\circ} = 19.05 \approx 19$ m. **(C)**

questions.question: A school is analysing the results of a recent Year 12 Mathematics assessment. The results indicate that many students scored poorly, likely due to poor time management and avoidable errors, while only a small number achieved high results. Four histograms have been produced to represent possible distributions of these scores. Which histogram represents the above scenario?
questions.answer: Many low scores and few high scores gives a positively skewed distribution (a tail to the right), which is histogram B. **(B)**

questions.question: The expected life of an Evercharge battery is normally distributed with a mean of 10 hours. What is the standard deviation if 95% of Evercharge batteries are expected to last between 8.8 and 11.2 hours?
questions.answer: 95% of scores lie within 2 standard deviations of the mean, so $2\sigma = 11.2 - 10 = 1.2$ and $\sigma = 0.6$ hours. **(A)**

questions.question: A local council is estimating the area of a section of land that borders a curved road. To do this, surveyors take three perpendicular measurements from the road to the opposite edge of the land, 20 m apart. The recorded distances are 23 m, 15 m and 19 m. Which of the following is the approximation for the area of this block of land, in square metres, using two applications of the trapezoidal rule?
Ali invests \$500 into a savings account that earns 4% per annum, compounded quarterly. What will be the value of Ali's investment after 2 years?

On 14 April 2025, Damien used his credit card to purchase a flight ticket valued at \$2150. He made no other purchases on his credit card during that month. He paid the outstanding amount in full on 6 May 2025. His credit card account does not offer an interest-free period, and interest is charged daily at an annual rate of 20.5%, including the date of purchase and the date of payment. How much interest did Damien pay on this transaction? Round your answer to the nearest cent.
questions.answer:
Daily rate $= \dfrac{20.5\%}{365} = 0.000561644\ldots$

Days: 14–30 April is $17$ days (including the 14th) and 1–6 May is $6$ days (including the 6th), so $n = 23$.

$$FV = 2150\left(1 + \dfrac{0.205}{365}\right)^{23} = \$2177.95$$

Interest $= 2177.95 - 2150 = \$27.95$.

*Note: the paper's solution gives \$38.98 (it evaluates $2150(1.000561\ldots)^{23}$ as \$2188.98, which is incorrect).*

questions.question: On Monday, 5 February, Liam boards a flight from Brisbane ($27^\circ$S, $153^\circ$E) to Seoul ($37^\circ$N, $127^\circ$E). His plane departs Brisbane at 9:45 pm and the journey takes 9 hours and 50 minutes. At that time of year, Seoul is 1 hour behind Brisbane. Determine the local day and time when Liam will land in Seoul.
questions.answer:
Arrival in Brisbane time: $9{:}45\ \text{pm} + 9\ \text{h}\ 50\ \text{min} = 7{:}35\ \text{am}$ on Tuesday.

Seoul is 1 hour behind Brisbane, so the local time in Seoul is $7{:}35 - 1\ \text{h} = 6{:}35\ \text{am}$ on **Tuesday**.

questions.question: Orlando has decided to move into a shared apartment. The floor plan is shown (not to scale). Orlando uses the Bathroom, Bedroom A, Hallway and the Kitchen regularly. The apartment rent is decided by the area of the rooms that Orlando uses regularly. He has to pay \$200 per square metre of those rooms per month. What is Orlando's rent per month?
questions.answer:
Reading the plan: the top row is $1.2$ m deep and the bottom row is $1.7$ m deep. The Kitchen is $2.2 + 1.0 = 3.2$ m wide, the Bathroom is $1.9$ m wide, Bedroom A is $1.9$ m wide and the Hallway is $1.0$ m wide.

- Bathroom: $1.9 \times 1.2 = 2.28\ \text{m}^2$
- Bedroom A: $1.9 \times 1.7 = 3.23\ \text{m}^2$
- Hallway: $1.0 \times 1.7 = 1.7\ \text{m}^2$
- Kitchen: $3.2 \times 1.2 = 3.84\ \text{m}^2$

Total area $= 11.05\ \text{m}^2$, so the rent is $200 \times 11.05 = \$2210$ per month.

questions.question: The kitchen floor of an apartment is $3.2$ m by $1.2$ m and needs to be retiled. Each tile measures $0.2$ m by $0.2$ m and is sold in boxes containing 15 tiles. Each box costs \$100. Only full boxes may be purchased. Calculate the total cost of the tiles required for the renovation.
questions.answer:
Number of tiles $= \dfrac{3.2 \times 1.2}{0.2 \times 0.2} = \dfrac{3.84}{0.04} = 96$.

Boxes needed $= 96 \div 15 = 6.4$, so $7$ boxes must be bought.

Cost $= 7 \times 100 = \$700$.

Calculate Pearson's correlation coefficient, correct to two significant figures.
questions.answer: Using the statistics mode of a calculator, $r = -0.4685\ldots \approx -0.47$.

questions.question:
Ten Year 11 students recorded their average daily screen time $x$ (hours) and study time $y$ (hours).

| Student | A | B | C | D | E | F | G | H | I | J |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Screen time $x$ | 5 | 6 | 4 | 7 | 3 | 6 | 8 | 5 | 4 | 7 |
| Study time $y$ | 2 | 1.5 | 2.5 | 1 | 3 | 1.5 | 0.5 | 2 | 2.5 | 4 |

The equation of the least-squares regression line of $y$ in terms of $x$ is $y = -0.3x + A$. Find $A$ and interpret the vertical intercept and the gradient in the context of the data.
questions.answer:
The line passes through $(\bar{x}, \bar{y}) = (5.5, 2.05)$, so $2.05 = -0.3(5.5) + A$ and $A = 3.7$. The line is $y = -0.3x + 3.7$.

- **Intercept:** with $0$ hours of screen time, the predicted study time is $3.7$ hours per day.
- **Gradient:** for each extra hour of screen time, the predicted study time decreases by $0.3$ hours (18 minutes).

questions.question:
Ethan takes the train to school on both Monday and Tuesday. Each day, the train can arrive in one of three ways:
- On time with a probability of $0.6$
- Slightly delayed with a probability of $0.3$
- Heavily delayed with a probability of $0.1$

Assume the outcome on each day is not affected by the previous day. Draw a probability tree diagram showing all possible outcomes over the two days, with the probability on each branch.
questions.answer:
Each day has three branches ($O$ = on time, $S$ = slightly delayed, $H$ = heavily delayed) with probabilities $0.6$, $0.3$, $0.1$. From each first-day branch the second day has the same three branches. The nine outcomes are:

| Outcome (Mon, Tue) | OO | OS | OH | SO | SS | SH | HO | HS | HH |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Probability | 0.36 | 0.18 | 0.06 | 0.18 | 0.09 | 0.03 | 0.06 | 0.03 | 0.01 |

questions.question: Each day Ethan's train is heavily delayed with probability $0.1$, independently of other days. Ethan claims that the probability of the train being heavily delayed on both Monday and Tuesday is $0.2$. Use an appropriate mathematical calculation to evaluate his claim and explain whether it is correct.
questions.answer:
$P(\text{heavily delayed both days}) = 0.1 \times 0.1 = 0.01$.

Ethan is incorrect: he added the probabilities ($0.1 + 0.1 = 0.2$) instead of multiplying them.

questions.question: Each day Ethan's train is heavily delayed with probability $0.1$, independently of other days. Calculate the probability that the train is not heavily delayed on either Monday or Tuesday.
questions.answer:
The train must not be heavily delayed on Monday and not heavily delayed on Tuesday:
$$P = 0.9 \times 0.9 = 0.81.$$

*Note: the paper's solution gives $1 - 0.01 = 0.99$, which is the probability that the train is *not* heavily delayed on both days, i.e. at least one day is not heavily delayed. "Not heavily delayed on either day" means neither day is heavily delayed, giving 0.81.*

questions.question: Nitin has a regular workweek of 40 hours and earns \$48 per hour. He is paid double time for any overtime hours. One week, he worked overtime and received a total pay of \$3072. How many overtime hours did Nitin work that week?
questions.answer:
Normal pay $= 40 \times 48 = \$1920$. Overtime pay $= 3072 - 1920 = \$1152$ at $2 \times 48 = \$96$ per hour.

Overtime hours $= \dfrac{1152}{96} = 12$ hours.

questions.question:
Electricity is charged at 29.85 cents per kWh. A household uses the following appliances:
- A 2.2 kW dryer for 1.5 hours, three times in one week
- A 900 W fridge running 24 hours a day

Calculate the total electricity cost to run both appliances for a full 7-day week.
questions.answer:
Dryer: $2.2 \times 1.5 \times 3 = 9.9$ kWh, costing $9.9 \times 0.2985 = \$2.96$.

Fridge: $900\ \text{W} = 0.9$ kW, so $0.9 \times 24 \times 7 = 151.2$ kWh, costing $151.2 \times 0.2985 = \$45.13$.

Total cost $= 2.96 + 45.13 \approx \$48.09$.

questions.question:

| White wine | 0.9 | 1.4 |
| Red wine | 1.0 | 1.5 |

Clara, who weighs 64 kg, consumed two large glasses of white wine and one small glass of red wine. Calculate how many standard drinks Clara consumed.
questions.answer: $N = 2 \times 1.4 + 1.0 = 3.8$ standard drinks.

questions.question:
Clara weighs 64 kg and consumed 3.8 standard drinks. At 10:00 pm her blood alcohol content (BAC) was measured at $0.045$. The BAC for females is estimated using
$$\text{BAC}_{\text{female}} = \frac{10N - 7.5H}{5.5M}$$
where $N$ is the number of standard drinks consumed, $H$ is the number of hours of drinking and $M$ is the person's weight in kilograms. Determine the number of hours $H$ that Clara had been drinking.
Clara had been drinking for $2$ hours $57$ minutes. What time did Clara start drinking if she finished drinking at 8:30 pm?
questions.answer: The drinking lasted $2$ h $57$ min and ended at 8:30 pm, so she started at $8{:}30\ \text{pm} - 2\ \text{h}\ 57\ \text{min} = 5{:}33\ \text{pm}$.

questions.question: Emma deposits \$30 000 into a new savings account. Each month she contributes an additional \$600 to the account before interest is applied. The account earns 0.7% interest per month, applied to the new total after the deposit. The amount in the account after the $n$th deposit is given by $A_n = (A_{n-1} + 600) \times 1.007$, where $n = 1, 2, 3, \dots$ and $A_0 = 30\,000$. Calculate the amount of money in the account after the third month.

Emma deposits \$30 000 into a new savings account and adds \$600 each month before interest. The account earns 0.7% interest per month, with $A_n = (A_{n-1} + 600) \times 1.007$ and $A_0 = 30\,000$. After three months the balance is \$32 459.74. Calculate the interest earned in the first three months.

The table shows future value interest factors for an annuity of \$1. Danny contributes \$600 every six months into an annuity that pays 8% p.a., compounded every six months. Use the table to determine how much he will have in 2 years' time.
questions.answer:
Rate per period $= 8\% \div 2 = 4\%$ and periods $= 2 \times 2 = 4$. The table factor is $4.2465$.

Future value $= 600 \times 4.2465 = \$2547.90$.

questions.question: The table shows future value interest factors for an annuity of \$1. James needs \$5000 in 2 years' time by contributing equal amounts every six months into an annuity that pays 8% p.a., compounded every six months. Danny contributes \$600 every six months. How much more than Danny does James need to contribute every six months?
questions.answer:
The factor for 4 periods at 4% is $4.2465$, so James's contribution is $\dfrac{5000}{4.2465} = \$1177.44$.

Difference $= 1177.44 - 600 = \$577.44$ more every six months.

questions.question: A coastal ferry departs from Dock $A$ at 6:00 am and travels 88 km on a bearing of $055^\circ$ to reach Buoy $B$. At $B$ the ferry changes direction and travels 62 km on a bearing of $140^\circ$ to reach Harbour $C$. Show that the size of $\angle ABC = 95^\circ$.
questions.answer:
The bearing of $A$ from $B$ is $055^\circ + 180^\circ = 235^\circ$ (back bearing). The bearing of $C$ from $B$ is $140^\circ$.

$\angle ABC = 235^\circ - 140^\circ = 95^\circ$.

questions.question: A ferry travels 88 km from Dock $A$ to Buoy $B$ and then 62 km from $B$ to Harbour $C$, where $\angle ABC = 95^\circ$. Using the cosine rule, find the distance from Dock $A$ to Harbour $C$. Give your answer correct to the nearest whole number.

A ferry travels 88 km from Dock $A$ on a bearing of $055^\circ$ to Buoy $B$ and then 62 km to Harbour $C$, where $\angle ABC = 95^\circ$ and $AC = 111.97$ km. Using the sine rule, calculate $\angle CAB$ to the nearest degree.
questions.answer: $$\frac{\sin \angle CAB}{62} = \frac{\sin 95^\circ}{111.97} \Rightarrow \sin \angle CAB = 0.5516\ldots \Rightarrow \angle CAB \approx 33^\circ.$$

questions.question: A ferry travels from Dock $A$ on a bearing of $055^\circ$ to Buoy $B$ and then on to Harbour $C$. The angle $\angle CAB$ between $AB$ and $AC$ is $33^\circ$ and $C$ lies clockwise from $B$ as seen from $A$. What is the bearing of Harbour $C$ from Dock $A$ to the nearest degree?
questions.answer: The ferry's second leg turns it to the right of the first, so $C$ lies clockwise of $B$ from $A$: bearing $= 55^\circ + 33^\circ = 088^\circ$.

questions.question: The daily water consumption (in litres) per household in a suburb is normally distributed with a mean of 900 L and a standard deviation of 100 L. The local council offers rebates to households that consume between 600 L and 1100 L per day. If there are 8000 households in the suburb, approximately how many are expected to qualify for the rebate?
questions.answer:
$600$ L is $3$ standard deviations below the mean and $1100$ L is $2$ standard deviations above the mean.

By the empirical rule: $\dfrac{99.7}{2} = 49.85\%$ lies between $-3$ and $0$ SD, and $\dfrac{95}{2} = 47.5\%$ lies between $0$ and $2$ SD.

Proportion qualifying $= 49.85 + 47.5 = 97.35\%$, so the expected number is $8000 \times 0.9735 \approx 7788$ households.

questions.question: A theme park is planning to install an emergency communication system. Each emergency station needs to be connected with cables. The network diagram shows all the possible cable connections and their lengths. The total length of cable used must be minimised. Draw a minimum spanning tree and find the length of the cable required.
questions.answer:
Using Kruskal's algorithm (add the shortest edges that do not form a cycle): $FG = 10$, $BC = 12$, $EG = 13$, $CE = 17$, $AB = 18$, $DF = 19$, $EH = 31$.

This gives 7 edges connecting all 8 vertices. The tree is $D - F - G - E - C - B - A$ with $H$ attached to $E$.

Total length $= 10 + 12 + 13 + 17 + 18 + 19 + 31 = 120$ units.

questions.question: Cables are to connect all stations of the network shown, using the least total length of cable. The minimum spanning tree has length 120 units and uses the edge $FG$ (length 10). Due to environmental restrictions, the cable connection between stations $F$ and $G$ cannot be used. Lee informs his team that this change will reduce the total cabling required by only 10 units. Is he correct? Justify your answer with mathematical calculations.
questions.answer:
Without $FG$, the shortest way to connect $F$ is the edge $FE$ (length $21$) instead of $FG$ (length $10$), giving a new spanning tree of length $120 - 10 + 21 = 131$.

Lee is incorrect: the total cable required **increases** by $11$ units (from 120 to 131); it does not decrease.

questions.question: The volume of water in a tank increases according to $V = 50(1.2)^t$, where $V$ is the volume in litres and $t$ is the time in hours. Using a graph or otherwise, estimate how long it will take for the tank to contain 150 litres.
questions.answer:
$150 = 50(1.2)^t \Rightarrow 1.2^t = 3 \Rightarrow t = \dfrac{\ln 3}{\ln 1.2} \approx 6.03$.

It will take approximately **6 hours** (found by trial: $50(1.2)^6 = 149.3$).

His total tax liability includes the Medicare levy (2% of taxable income). Over the course of the year, he paid \$2800 per month in Pay As You Go (PAYG) instalments. questions.answer: The factor for 25 years at 7.5% is $7.3899$ per \$1000, so the monthly repayment is $400 \times 7.3899 = \$2955.96$.

questions.question: A home loan of \$400 000 over 25 years has a monthly repayment of \$2955.96. Find the total amount to be repaid.
questions.answer: Total repaid $= 2955.96 \times 12 \times 25 = \$886\,788$.

questions.question: A home loan of \$400 000 over 25 years has a total amount to be repaid of \$886 788. Find the interest paid on the loan.

Darryl and Anna agree that they will take out a \$400 000 loan if the monthly repayments are no more than 25% of their gross salary. The monthly repayment is \$2955.96. Their combined gross salary is \$210 000 per year. Should they take out the loan? Justify your answer using mathematical calculations.
questions.answer:
Monthly gross salary $= 210\,000 \div 12 = \$17\,500$, and $25\%$ of this is $0.25 \times 17\,500 = \$4375$.

The repayment of \$2955.96 is less than \$4375, so they should take out the loan.

questions.question: Coastline Tours charges a fixed setup fee plus a cost per person. The total cost \$$C$ depends on the number of people $n$ and is shown on the graph. Find the gradient and the $y$-intercept of the Coastline Tours graph.
questions.answer:
The graph passes through $(0, 50)$ and, for example, $(20, 170)$ (rise $120$ for a run of $20$).

Gradient $= \dfrac{120}{20} = 6$ and $y$-intercept $= 50$. So $C = 6n + 50$.

questions.question: Coastline Tours' total cost is $C = 6n + 50$ (shown on the graph). Explore Away charges \$8 per person with no setup fee, so $C = 8n$. On the graph given, draw the line representing Explore Away's cost model.
questions.answer: Draw a straight line through the origin $(0, 0)$ and a second point such as $(25, 200)$ or $(40, 320)$.

questions.question: Coastline Tours charges $C = 6n + 50$ and Explore Away charges $C = 8n$, where $C$ is the cost in dollars and $n$ is the number of people. Determine the number of people for which the two companies charge the same total amount. Hence, state the corresponding cost.
questions.answer:
$6n + 50 = 8n \Rightarrow 50 = 2n \Rightarrow n = 25$.

The cost is $8 \times 25 = \$200$, i.e. the lines intersect at $(25, 200)$.

questions.question: Emily intends to purchase a new hybrid vehicle priced at \$38 000. She pays a 25% deposit and finances the remaining balance through a reducing balance loan. Calculate the amount that Emily needs to finance after paying the deposit.
questions.answer: Deposit $= 0.25 \times 38\,000 = \$9500$, so the amount financed is $38\,000 - 9500 = \$28\,500$.

questions.question: Emily finances \$28 500 through a reducing balance loan over 4 years. No repayments are required for the first 2 months. From the 3rd month onwards she makes equal monthly repayments until the end of the loan term (46 repayments). The lender charges 9% per annum, compounded monthly (0.75% per month). The table gives present value interest factors for an annuity of \$1; the factor for $N = 46$ and $r = 0.0075$ is $38.78231$. Calculate the monthly repayment, rounded to the nearest dollar.
questions.answer:
During the first two months interest accrues, so the amount owing when repayments begin is
$$28\,500 \times 1.0075^2 = \$28\,929.10.$$
Monthly repayment $= \dfrac{28\,929.10}{38.78231} = \$745.94 \approx \$746$.

*Note: the paper's solution ignores the interest charged during the 2 months with no repayments and gives \$735.*

questions.question: Emily finances \$28 500 and makes 46 monthly repayments of \$746. Calculate the total interest Emily will pay over the life of the loan.
questions.answer:
Total repaid $= 746 \times 46 = \$34\,316$, so interest $= 34\,316 - 28\,500 = \$5816$.

*(The paper's solution, using \$735, gives \$5304.07.)*

questions.question: A 6 L container contains a mixture of juice and water in the ratio $2:4$. After removing 2 L of the mixture, more water is added to refill the container. What is the final ratio of juice to water in the mixture?
questions.answer:
Original: juice $= \dfrac{2}{6} \times 6 = 2$ L and water $= 4$ L.

The 2 L removed contains juice $\dfrac{2}{6} \times 2 = \dfrac{2}{3}$ L and water $\dfrac{4}{3}$ L.

Remaining: juice $= 2 - \dfrac{2}{3} = \dfrac{4}{3}$ L and water $= 4 - \dfrac{4}{3} = \dfrac{8}{3}$ L.

After adding 2 L of water: water $= \dfrac{8}{3} + 2 = \dfrac{14}{3}$ L.

Final ratio juice : water $= \dfrac{4}{3} : \dfrac{14}{3} = 4 : 14 = 2 : 7$.

questions.question: A company designs a small decorative rocket made of a cone-shaped nose, a cylindrical body and a hemispherical base, as shown. The cylinder, the cone and the hemisphere all have diameter 6 cm. The cone is 5 cm long and the whole rocket is 16 cm long. The whole outer surface is to be painted (excluding the areas where the parts are joined). Calculate the total surface area to be painted, correct to two decimal places.
questions.answer:
Length of the cylinder $= 16 - 5 - 3 = 8$ cm. Radius $= 3$ cm.

- Hemisphere (curved): $2\pi r^2 = 2\pi(3)^2 = 18\pi$
- Cylinder (curved): $2\pi r h = 2\pi(3)(8) = 48\pi$
- Cone (curved): slant height $l = \sqrt{3^2 + 5^2} = \sqrt{34}$, so $\pi r l = 3\sqrt{34}\,\pi$

Total $= (18 + 48 + 3\sqrt{34})\pi \approx 262.30\ \text{cm}^2$.

*(The paper rounds the slant height to 5.83 and gets 262.29.)*

questions.question: A decorative rocket has a total surface area of $262.3\ \text{cm}^2$ to be painted. If 1 litre of paint covers $2\ \text{m}^2$, determine how many millilitres of paint are needed to paint one rocket. Give your answer correct to the nearest millilitre.

The delivery times (in hours) for packages sent by an online store are normally distributed with a mean of 48 and a standard deviation of 6 hours. Explain why the percentage of deliveries between 42 hours and 54 hours is double the percentage of deliveries between 48 hours and 54 hours.
questions.answer:
$42$ and $54$ are $1$ standard deviation below and above the mean, so about $68\%$ of deliveries lie between them. Between $48$ and $54$ is $0$ to $+1$ standard deviation, about $34\%$.

The normal distribution is symmetrical about the mean, so the area from $42$ to $48$ equals the area from $48$ to $54$, and the area from $42$ to $54$ is double the area from $48$ to $54$.

questions.question:
The delivery times (in hours) for packages sent by an online store are normally distributed with a mean of 48 and a standard deviation of 6 hours. The table gives the cumulative probability that a standard normal variable is less than a given $z$-score.

| $z$ | 0.6 | 0.7 | 0.8 | 0.9 | 1.0 | 1.1 | 1.2 | 1.3 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $P$ | 0.7257 | 0.7580 | 0.7881 | 0.8159 | 0.8413 | 0.8643 | 0.8849 | 0.9032 |

Using the values in the table, estimate the delivery time a customer could expect to fall within the fastest 15% of deliveries.
questions.answer:
The fastest 15% are the shortest times, so we need $P(Z < z) = 0.15$. By symmetry this is $z = -z_1$, where $P(Z < z_1) = 0.85$.

From the table, $0.8413$ at $z = 1.0$ and $0.8643$ at $z = 1.1$, so $z_1 \approx 1.0 + 0.1\left(\dfrac{0.85 - 0.8413}{0.8643 - 0.8413}\right) \approx 1.04$ (so $z \approx -1.04$).

$x = 48 - 1.04 \times 6 \approx 41.8$ hours. Deliveries of about **42 hours or less** are in the fastest 15%.

*Note: the paper's solution gives 54.6 hours, which is the cut-off for the slowest 13.6% of deliveries, not the fastest 15%.*

questions.question: On average, a courier delivers a parcel every three minutes. At that rate, how long will it take the courier to deliver 73 parcels?
questions.answer: $73 \times 3 = 219$ minutes $= 3$ hours $39$ minutes. **(B)**

questions.question: The diagram shows the graph of an equation. Which of the following equations does the graph best represent?
questions.answer: The curve has a positive $y$-intercept, is decreasing and approaches the $x$-axis (an exponential decay). $y = 2^{-x}$ has $y$-intercept $1$ and decreases towards $0$. The reciprocal graphs $y = \pm\frac{2}{x}$ have no $y$-intercept, and $y = 2^x$ is increasing. **(C)**

questions.question: A map of a particular city has a scale of $1 : 50\,000$. If the distance between Jesse's home and the airport is 4 centimetres on this map, what is the actual distance?
The diagram shows the locations of two towns, Alhambra and Brentwood. What is the bearing of Brentwood from Alhambra?
questions.answer: Alhambra is on a bearing of $120^\circ$ clockwise from north to the line AB... in the diagram, $120^\circ$ is the angle at Alhambra between north and the direction to Brentwood measured round through the south-west? The line to Brentwood is $60^\circ$ from the south direction, towards the west. So Brentwood is S$60^\circ$W from Alhambra. **(C)**

questions.question: Consider the linear equations $y = x + 2$ and $y = 2 - \dfrac{1}{2}x$. Which diagram could be used to find the solution to these simultaneous linear equations?
questions.answer: Both lines have $y$-intercept $2$. The first has gradient $+1$ (rising) and the second has gradient $-\frac{1}{2}$ (falling). Only diagram A shows one rising line and one falling line crossing at $(0, 2)$. **(A)**

questions.question: Consider the network diagram. What is the sum of the degrees of all the vertices shown on the network diagram?
questions.answer: The network has 6 edges and the sum of the degrees is twice the number of edges: $2 \times 6 = 12$. (Degrees: $A = 2$, $B = 2$, $C = 1$, $D = 3$, $E = 4$.) **(D)**

questions.question: A set of bivariate data has a Pearson's correlation coefficient of $-0.95$. Which expression best describes the association between the two variables?
questions.answer: $r = -0.95$ is close to $-1$, so the association is strong and negative. **(B)**
options: There is a weak negative association
There is a strong negative association
There is a weak positive association
There is a strong positive association

questions.question: A teacher asked fifty students to identify their favourite type of pet. A partially completed Pareto chart shows some of the data collected. How many students chose cats as their favourite pet?
questions.answer: The cumulative percentage rises from $40\%$ (dogs) to $68\%$ (dogs and cats), so cats are $68 - 40 = 28\%$ of the students. $28\% \times 50 = 14$ students. **(B)**

questions.question: Adam takes out a loan of \$10 000 to buy a new car. Simple interest is charged on the loan. To repay the loan and the interest charged, Adam makes payments of \$1200 every year over the next 10 years. What is the simple interest rate, per annum, that is charged on the loan?
questions.answer: Total repaid $= 1200 \times 10 = \$12\,000$, so the interest is $12\,000 - 10\,000 = \$2000$. $I = Prn$: $2000 = 10\,000 \times r \times 10 \Rightarrow r = 0.02 = 2\%$. **(A)**

questions.question:
Savannah competed in four throwing events at the district athletics carnival. In each event the distances recorded by the competitors were normally distributed.

| | Savannah's result | Event mean | Event standard deviation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Shot put | 15 m | 13 m | 2 m |
| Discus | 37 m | 43 m | 6 m |
| Javelin | 57 m | 47 m | 8 m |
| Hammer throw | 33 m | 48 m | 10 m |

Which was Savannah's weakest event compared with the other competitors?
questions.answer: Compare $z$-scores: shot put $\frac{15 - 13}{2} = 1$; discus $\frac{37 - 43}{6} = -1$; javelin $\frac{57 - 47}{8} = 1.25$; hammer throw $\frac{33 - 48}{10} = -1.5$. The lowest $z$-score is the hammer throw. **(D)**

questions.question: Tennis players are allowed to serve the ball to their opponent up to two consecutive times. If the first serve is successful, the ball goes into play and a second serve is not performed. If the first serve is unsuccessful, the player will serve the ball a second time. Nava is a tennis player. The probability that her first serve is successful is 50% and the probability that her second serve is successful is 90%. What is the probability that Nava serves the ball successfully?
questions.answer: $P(\text{success}) = P(\text{first serve in}) + P(\text{first fails and second in}) = 0.5 + 0.5 \times 0.9 = 0.95 = 95\%$. **(D)**

questions.question: Charlotte is thinking of a number. Let the number be $x$. When Charlotte subtracts 6 from this number and multiplies the result by 4, the answer is 3 more than $x$. Which equation can be used to find $x$?
questions.answer: Subtract 6 and then multiply by 4: $4(x - 6)$. This equals 3 more than $x$: $x + 3$. So $4(x - 6) = x + 3$. **(C)**

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a fee or charge associated with using a credit card?
questions.answer: Interest, cash advance fees and late payment fees are all charged on credit cards; there is no "repayment fee". **(D)**

questions.question: The graph shows the depth of water in a container over time, as it is being filled. Which of the containers shown could reflect the graph above?
questions.answer: Water is poured in at a steady rate. The depth rises quickly at first (narrow base), then slowly (wide middle section), then quickly again (narrow neck). That is the round flask with a narrow neck. **(B)**

questions.question: Two friends, Shay and Mika, left their respective homes one morning and cycled along the same road. The graph shows their journeys (distance from home against time). Which of the friends made a stop first?
questions.answer: Shay. Her graph is horizontal (she stops, at 30 km) from 12 noon to 1 pm, before Mika stops at 45 km from 1 pm to 2 pm.

questions.question: Two friends, Shay and Mika, cycled along the same road, as shown in the graph. When Mika began cycling home, how far had Shay travelled on her trip?
questions.answer: Mika begins cycling home at 2 pm. By then Shay has cycled out $30$ km and back $20$ km (she is $10$ km from home), so she has travelled $30 + 20 = 50$ km.

questions.question: Two friends, Shay and Mika, cycled along the same road, as shown in the graph. What was Mika's average speed, to the nearest km/h, on the cycling trip?
questions.answer: Mika cycled from 10 am to 5 pm, which is $7$ hours, and travelled $45 + 45 = 90$ km. Average speed $= \dfrac{90}{7} \approx 13$ km/h.

questions.question: The flight time from Sydney to Dubai is approximately 13 hours. The Universal Coordinated Time of Dubai is $+4$ and Sydney is $+10$. A plane departs Sydney local time at 11:00 PM Sunday for Dubai. At what local time in Dubai is the plane expected to land?
questions.answer:
Dubai is $10 - 4 = 6$ hours behind Sydney, so the departure is 5:00 PM Sunday Dubai time. Adding the flight time of 13 hours gives $5{:}00\ \text{PM} + 13\ \text{h} = 6{:}00$ AM **Monday** in Dubai.

(Equivalently: arrive 12:00 noon Monday Sydney time, which is 6:00 AM Monday in Dubai.)

questions.question: A manager oversees four teenage employees working in a fast-food restaurant. The number of weeks they have been working at the restaurant, $x$, and the number of times they need to ask the manager for assistance during a four-hour shift, $y$, are shown on the graph: $(2, 15)$, $(6, 10)$, $(10, 6)$, $(17, 3)$. Find the equation of the least-squares regression line for the data set, finding the gradient and $y$-intercept correct to 2 decimal places.
questions.answer:
Using the statistics mode of a calculator: gradient $= -0.79$ and $y$-intercept $= 15.38$.

$$y = 15.38 - 0.79x$$

questions.question: For four employees, the least-squares regression line for the number of times $y$ they need to ask for assistance during a four-hour shift against the number of weeks $x$ they have worked is $y = 15.38 - 0.79x$. Using this line as a guide, on average how many full weeks will an employee have to be working at the restaurant before they require assistance less than 8 times during a four-hour shift?
questions.answer:
$$15.38 - 0.79x < 8 \Rightarrow 0.79x > 7.38 \Rightarrow x > 9.34\ldots$$

(The paper's working uses $x > 9.38$ from the same rounded line.) So an employee needs to work $x > 9.3$ weeks, i.e. **10 full weeks**.

questions.question: The diagram shows a rectangular park that contains 3 triangular grass areas (shaded). There is a footpath (unshaded) around the edges of the park and between the grassed areas. The corners of the park are $A$, $B$, $C$, $E$ and $D$ is the point on the bottom edge where the two diagonal paths meet. Draw a network diagram to represent the possible walking paths through the park.
questions.answer: Vertices $A$, $B$, $C$, $D$, $E$ with edges $AB$, $BC$, $CD$, $DE$, $EA$ (the outside path) and $AD$, $BD$ (the two diagonal paths).

questions.question: A network has vertices $A$, $B$, $C$, $D$, $E$ and edges $AB$, $BC$, $CD$, $DE$, $EA$, $AD$, $BD$. Show that the sum of the degrees of the vertices is equal to twice the number of edges.
questions.answer:
| Vertex | $A$ | $B$ | $C$ | $D$ | $E$ | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Degree | 3 | 3 | 2 | 4 | 2 | 14 |

There are $7$ edges and $2 \times 7 = 14$, which equals the sum of the degrees.

questions.question:
A company purchases office furniture for \$10 000. The company accountant is considering two methods of depreciation:
- straight-line depreciation with the office furniture being depreciated by \$$D$ each year
- declining-balance depreciation at a rate of 15% per year

The accountant determines that after two years, the salvage value of the office furniture will be the same using either depreciation method. What is the value of $D$?
questions.answer:
Declining balance: $S = 10\,000(1 - 0.15)^2 = \$7225$. The depreciation after two years is $10\,000 - 7225 = \$2775$.

Straight line: $2D = 2775 \Rightarrow D = \$1387.50$.

questions.question: Two right-angled triangles, $ABD$ and $BCD$, are shown. In triangle $ABD$, $AB = 13$ cm and $AD = 12$ cm, and $\theta = \angle BAD$. Find the value of $\theta$, correct to the nearest degree.
questions.answer: $\cos\theta = \dfrac{12}{13} \Rightarrow \theta = \cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{12}{13}\right) = 22.6^\circ \approx 23^\circ$.

questions.question: Two right-angled triangles, $ABD$ and $BCD$, are shown. In triangle $ABD$, $AB = 13$ cm and $AD = 12$ cm. In triangle $BCD$, $\angle BCD = 50^\circ$ and $BC = x$. Find the value of $x$, correct to 1 decimal place.
questions.answer:
By Pythagoras in $\triangle ABD$: $BD^2 = 13^2 - 12^2 = 25 \Rightarrow BD = 5$ cm.

In $\triangle BCD$: $\sin 50^\circ = \dfrac{5}{x} \Rightarrow x = \dfrac{5}{\sin 50^\circ} = 6.5$ cm.

questions.question: A 44-gallon drum has a base but no lid. The drum is 88 cm in height and has a diameter of 58 cm. The inside of the drum and the curved surface of the outside of the drum are to be painted. Underneath the base of the drum is not to be painted as it is in contact with the ground. What is the surface area to be painted, in square centimetres, correct to 1 decimal place?
questions.answer:
Radius $= 29$ cm.

- Inside: curved surface $2\pi(29)(88)$ plus base $\pi(29)^2$
- Outside: curved surface $2\pi(29)(88)$

Total $= 4\pi(29)(88) + \pi(29)^2 = 32\,069.4 + 2642.1 = 34\,711.5\ \text{cm}^2$.

questions.question: The time it takes for a cupcake at a picnic to be eaten by ants ($t$ minutes) varies inversely with the number of ants eating the cupcake ($N$ ants). When there are 10 ants, the cupcake is eaten in 120 minutes. The equation relating $t$ and $N$ is $t = \dfrac{k}{N}$. What is the value of $k$?
questions.answer: $120 = \dfrac{k}{10} \Rightarrow k = 1200$.

questions.question: The time it takes for a cupcake at a picnic to be eaten by $N$ ants is $t = \dfrac{1200}{N}$ minutes. Calculate how long it will take 20 ants to eat one cupcake.
questions.answer: $t = \dfrac{1200}{20} = 60$ minutes (1 hour).

questions.question:
The table shows the fat and calorie content of 12 different burgers on a fast-food restaurant's menu. Two of the values are missing and are represented by the letters $A$ and $B$.

| Fat (g) | 9 | 12 | 15 | 18 | 23 | 24 | 26 | 27 | 29 | $A$ | 31 | 43 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Calories | 250 | $B$ | 320 | 380 | 420 | 420 | 515 | 530 | 545 | 600 | 620 | 750 |

The bivariate data is displayed in the scatter plot. Using the scatter plot, determine the values of $A$ and $B$.
questions.answer: The point with $600$ calories on the scatter plot is at $29$ g of fat, so $A = 29$. The point at $12$ g of fat has $300$ calories, so $B = 300$.

questions.question: A table and scatter plot show the fat content (g) and the calorie content of 12 different burgers. Identify the dependent variable.
questions.answer: Calories (the calorie content depends on the fat content).

questions.question: Anaya is paid \$38 per hour for the first 40 hours each week, with time-and-a-half for any overtime hours. In a particular week, Anaya earned \$285 in overtime. How many hours in total did she work that week?
questions.answer:
Overtime rate $= 1.5 \times 38 = \$57$ per hour, so the overtime hours are $\dfrac{285}{57} = 5$.

Total hours worked $= 40 + 5 = 45$ hours.

questions.question: Takeshi is considering two payment plans offered by an online music service. Plan A has a monthly subscription fee of \$3 and \$0.25 per song downloaded. Plan B has no monthly subscription fee and \$0.40 per song downloaded. Let $x$ be the number of songs downloaded and \$$C$ be the total cost per month. Write an equation that represents the monthly cost of Plan A.

Plan A costs $C = 0.25x + 3$ per month, where $x$ is the number of songs downloaded. The graph shows the line of the equation for the monthly cost of Plan B ($C = 0.40x$). On the graph, draw the line of the equation for Plan A.
questions.answer: Plot points such as $(0, 3)$, $(8, 5)$, $(20, 8)$ and $(28, 10)$, and join them with a straight line starting at $(0, 3)$ with gradient $0.25$. It crosses the Plan B line at $(20, 8)$.

questions.question: Plan A costs $C = 0.25x + 3$ and Plan B costs $C = 0.40x$ per month for $x$ songs. The two lines intersect at $(20, 8)$. Explain how Takeshi can decide which plan to select.
questions.answer: The lines intersect at $x = 20$ songs (cost \$8). If Takeshi downloads fewer than 20 songs a month, Plan B's line is lower, so Plan B is cheaper. If he downloads more than 20 songs, Plan A is cheaper. At exactly 20 songs the plans cost the same.

questions.question:
Roco has a credit card with the following conditions:
- There is no interest-free period.
- Interest is charged at the end of each month at 19.99% per annum, compounding daily, from the purchase date (included) to the last day of the month (included).

Roco's credit card statement for March (1 March to 31 March) shows: opening balance \$0.00; 19 March, car repairs, \$1200.00; 27 March, trailer hire, \$110.00; 31 March, interest charged, ***; 31 March, closing balance, ***. The minimum payment is calculated as 2.5% of the closing balance on 31 March. What will be the value of his minimum payment?
questions.answer:
Daily rate $= \dfrac{0.1999}{365}$.

The \$1200 purchase is charged from 19 to 31 March, which is $13$ days, and the \$110 purchase from 27 to 31 March, which is $5$ days.

Closing balance $= 1200\left(1 + \dfrac{0.1999}{365}\right)^{13} + 110\left(1 + \dfrac{0.1999}{365}\right)^{5} = \$1318.87$.

Minimum payment $= 2.5\% \times 1318.87 = \$32.97$.

questions.question: The diagram shows a wheel of cheese with a radius of 5 cm and a height of 3 cm. A wedge representing one eighth of the cheese has been cut and removed from the wheel. Find the volume of the remaining cheese wheel, correct to the nearest cubic centimetre.
questions.answer: $V = \dfrac{7}{8} \times \pi r^2 h = \dfrac{7}{8} \times \pi (5)^2 (3) = 206.2 \approx 206\ \text{cm}^3$.

questions.question: The diagram represents a network with weighted edges. Draw a minimum spanning tree for this network and determine its length.
questions.answer:
Add the shortest edges that do not form a cycle: $CD = 2$, $ED = 3$, $BC = 4$, $FE = 6$. Then $AB = 8$ (the next shortest edge, $BE = 7$, would form a cycle).

The tree has edges $AB$, $BC$, $CD$, $DE$, $EF$ and length $8 + 4 + 2 + 3 + 6 = 23$.

questions.question: The diagram represents a network with weighted edges. A new edge from $B$ to $F$ is added with a weight of $x$, where $x$ is a whole number. If the shortest path from $F$ to $D$ uses this new edge, what is the maximum value of $x$?
questions.answer:
The current shortest path from $F$ to $D$ is $F - E - D$ with length $6 + 3 = 9$.

Using the new edge, the shortest route is $F - B - C - D$ with length $x + 4 + 2 = x + 6$. For this to be the shortest path, $x + 6 < 9$, so $x < 3$.

The maximum whole-number value is $x = 2$.

questions.question: A spinner is divided into three sections $A$, $B$ and $C$. The sizes of the sections are $A$: $(7x + 10)^\circ$, $B$: $90^\circ$ and $C$: $3x^\circ$. Find the value of $x$.
questions.answer: The angles in a full turn sum to $360^\circ$: $7x + 10 + 90 + 3x = 360 \Rightarrow 10x = 260 \Rightarrow x = 26$.

questions.question: A spinner has three sections: $A$ with $(7x + 10)^\circ$, $B$ with $90^\circ$ and $C$ with $3x^\circ$, where $x = 26$. If the spinner is spun 60 times, how many times would it be expected to land on $C$?
questions.answer:
Section $C$ is $3 \times 26 = 78^\circ$, so $P(C) = \dfrac{78}{360}$.

Expected number $= 60 \times \dfrac{78}{360} = 13$ times.

questions.question: Shareen buys a car for \$29 000 and repays it over 4 years through equal monthly instalments. She pays a 10% deposit and interest is charged at 9% p.a. on the reducing balance loan. Using the table of present value interest factors, where $r$ represents the monthly interest rate and $N$ represents the number of payments, calculate the monthly repayment, \$$P$, that Shareen must pay to complete the loan after 4 years (to the nearest dollar).
questions.answer:
Deposit $= 0.10 \times 29\,000 = \$2900$, so the amount borrowed is $\$26\,100$.

$N = 4 \times 12 = 48$ and $r = \dfrac{9\%}{12} = 0.75\% = 0.0075$. The table factor is $40.18478$.

$P \times 40.18478 = 26\,100 \Rightarrow P = \dfrac{26\,100}{40.18478} = \$649$ (to the nearest dollar).

questions.question:
Gavin, a 72 kg male, consumes 4 bottles of beer at a party, each containing 1.4 standard drinks. Gavin started drinking his first beer at 8:20 PM and finished his 4th beer at 11:50 PM. The blood alcohol content (BAC) for males can be estimated by
$$\text{BAC}_{\text{male}} = \frac{10N - 7.5H}{6.8M}$$
where $N$ is the number of standard drinks, $H$ is the number of hours drinking and $M$ is the mass in kilograms. Calculate Gavin's BAC when he finished his fourth beer, correct to 3 decimal places.

A farmer has two flocks of chickens. The number of eggs they laid each day during the year was counted, with the data shown in a parallel box plot (Flock 1: minimum 4, $Q_1 = 7$, median 11, $Q_3 = 15$, maximum 18; Flock 2: minimum 6, $Q_1 = 8$, median 10, $Q_3 = 16$, maximum 20). Compare the two data sets, examining the skewness of the distributions, and any relevant measures of central tendency and spread.
questions.answer:
- **Centre:** Flock 1 has a higher median (11 eggs per day compared with 10).
- **Shape:** Flock 1 is approximately symmetrical (the median is in the middle of the box and the whiskers are about equal), while Flock 2 is positively skewed (the median is closer to $Q_1$ and the upper whisker is longer).
- **Spread:** The two flocks have the same range ($18 - 4 = 14$ and $20 - 6 = 14$) and the same interquartile range ($15 - 7 = 8$ and $16 - 8 = 8$).

questions.question: In the diagram, $\triangle PQR$ is similar to $\triangle STR$, $PQ = 45$ cm, $ST = 15$ cm, $QT = y$ and $TR = x$. Show that $y = 2x$.
questions.answer:
Corresponding sides of similar triangles are in the same ratio, so
$$\frac{QR}{TR} = \frac{PQ}{ST} \Rightarrow \frac{x + y}{x} = \frac{45}{15} = 3.$$
Then $x + y = 3x$, so $y = 2x$.

questions.question:
The table shows the income tax rates for the 2025–2026 financial year.

| Taxable income | Tax on this income |
|---|---|
| \$0 – \$18 200 | Nil |
| \$18 201 – \$45 000 | 16c for each \$1 over \$18 200 |
| \$45 001 – \$135 000 | \$4288 plus 30c for each \$1 over \$45 000 |
| \$135 001 – \$190 000 | \$31 288 plus 37c for each \$1 over \$135 000 |
| \$190 001 and over | \$51 638 plus 45c for each \$1 over \$190 000 |

For the 2025–2026 financial year, Amani has a taxable income of \$126 250. During the year she paid \$1130 per fortnight in Pay As You Go (PAYG) tax. Calculate Amani's tax refund, ignoring the Medicare levy.

120 people entered the first round of a crossword competition. The times taken to complete the crossword correctly were normally distributed with a mean of 10 minutes and a standard deviation of 2.1 minutes. Approximately how many of the 120 correctly completed their crosswords in more than 12.1 minutes?
questions.answer:
$12.1 = 10 + 2.1$, so $z = 1$. About $68\%$ lie within one standard deviation, leaving $16\%$ above $z = 1$.

$0.16 \times 120 = 19.2 \approx 19$ people.

questions.question: The times taken to complete a crossword were normally distributed with a mean of 10 minutes and a standard deviation of 2.1 minutes. If a competitor completed her crossword in 13.15 minutes, what was her $z$-score?

The table shows the future values of an annuity of \$1. At the end of each year, Albert deposits \$6000 into a bank account that earns interest at a rate of 4% per annum, compounding annually. He makes these contributions over a period of 20 years. How much interest will the account have earned after 20 years?
questions.answer:
From the table, 20 periods at 4% has a factor of $29.77808$.

$FV = 6000 \times 29.77808 = \$178\,668.48$.

Total contributions $= 6000 \times 20 = \$120\,000$, so the interest earned is $178\,668.48 - 120\,000 = \$58\,668.48$.

questions.question: Albert's account will have a future value of \$178 668.48 after 20 years. His bank has an account option that offers the same interest rate (4% p.a.), compounding quarterly rather than annually. Albert decides to open a new account and make quarterly contributions over a period of 10 years. How much would Albert need to contribute to the new account at the end of each quarter to achieve the same future value after 10 years? The table shows the future values of an annuity of \$1.
questions.answer:
Quarterly rate $= \dfrac{4\%}{4} = 1\%$ and the number of periods $= 10 \times 4 = 40$. From the table the factor is $48.88637$.

$$a \times 48.88637 = 178\,668.48 \Rightarrow a = \$3654.77.$$

questions.question:
The profit that a company makes in one month can be modelled by $P = 50n - 0.5n^2$, where $P$ is the profit (in thousands of dollars) and $n$ is the number of units produced (in thousands). Complete the table.

| Number of units produced (thousand) | 0 | 20 | 40 | 60 | 80 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Profit (thousand \$) | 0 | | | | |

The profit (in thousands of dollars) of a company is modelled by $P = 50n - 0.5n^2$, where $n$ is the number of units produced (in thousands). Graph the equation on the grid using the values $(0, 0)$, $(20, 800)$, $(40, 1200)$, $(60, 1200)$, $(80, 800)$.
questions.answer: Plot the five points and join them with a smooth, symmetrical, downwards-opening curve (a parabola) with its vertex at $(50, 1250)$.

questions.question: The profit of a company is modelled by $P = 50n - 0.5n^2$. State the name of this type of non-linear relationship.
questions.answer: A quadratic relationship (its graph is a parabola).

questions.question: The profit (in thousands of dollars) of a company is modelled by $P = 50n - 0.5n^2$, where $n$ is the number of units produced (in thousands). The profit is \$1200 thousand at both $n = 40$ and $n = 60$. Find how many units should be produced to maximise the company's monthly profits.
questions.answer: The maximum is on the axis of symmetry, which is midway between $n = 40$ and $n = 60$: $n = \dfrac{40 + 60}{2} = 50$. So $50\,000$ units should be produced.

questions.question: The profit (in thousands of dollars) of a company is modelled by $P = 50n - 0.5n^2$, where $n$ is the number of units produced (in thousands). What is the maximum profit that can be made per month?

The profit (in thousands of dollars) of a company is modelled by $P = 50n - 0.5n^2$, where $n$ is the number of units produced (in thousands). Explain why the company should not try to produce 100 000 units of their product, justifying your response with calculations.
questions.answer: At $n = 100$: $P = 50(100) - 0.5(100)^2 = 5000 - 5000 = 0$. The company would make no profit at 100 000 units, which is less than it makes at lower production levels (maximum \$1 250 000 at 50 000 units).

questions.question: The area of a paddock is to be estimated. Due to thick spiky weeds through parts of the paddock, the surveyors are only able to find the measurements shown (parallel sides 122 m, 99 m, 108 m and 141 m, spaced 83 m, 152 m and 116 m apart respectively). Use three applications of the trapezoidal rule to estimate the area of the paddock, in hectares, correct to 1 decimal place. (One hectare $= 10\,000\ \text{m}^2$.)

A paddock has an area of 3.9 hectares (3.93455 ha before rounding). A mixture of herbicide and fertiliser needs to be applied at a rate of 45 litres per hectare. How many litres of the mixture are needed for the paddock?
questions.answer: $3.9 \times 45 = 175.5$ L (or $3.93455 \times 45 \approx 177$ L using the unrounded area). Either answer is acceptable.

questions.question: A thunderstorm over a paddock of area $39\,345.5\ \text{m}^2$ sees the whole paddock receive 8 millimetres of rain. How much rain fell onto the paddock, correct to the nearest kilolitre?
questions.answer:
$V = Ah = 39\,345.5 \times 0.008 = 314.8\ \text{m}^3$.

Since $1\ \text{m}^3 = 1\ \text{kL}$, the rain was approximately $315$ kL.

questions.question: The time spent waiting for a taxi at a large international airport is normally distributed. The waiting time is less than 184 seconds 16% of the time and greater than 304 seconds 0.15% of the time. During the first three months of 2024, 4.16 million people visited the airport. If 30% of these people took a taxi from the airport, find the approximate number of people whose waiting time was greater than 184 seconds.
questions.answer:
$P(\text{wait} > 184) = 100\% - 16\% = 84\%$.

Number of people who took a taxi $= 0.30 \times 4\,160\,000 = 1\,248\,000$.

Number waiting more than 184 s $= 0.84 \times 1\,248\,000 = 1\,048\,320$ people.

questions.question: The time spent waiting for a taxi at a large international airport is normally distributed. The waiting time is less than 184 seconds 16% of the time and greater than 304 seconds 0.15% of the time. Determine the mean and standard deviation for the time spent waiting for a taxi at the airport.
questions.answer:
$16\%$ of the data lies below $z = -1$, so $184 = \mu - \sigma$. $0.15\%$ lies above $z = +3$, so $304 = \mu + 3\sigma$.

Subtracting: $304 - 184 = 4\sigma \Rightarrow \sigma = 30$ seconds. Then $\mu = 184 + 30 = 214$ seconds.

questions.question: The time spent waiting for a taxi at a large international airport is normally distributed with a mean of 214 seconds and a standard deviation of 30 seconds. Is it likely that the waiting time for a taxi will be two minutes or less? Justify your response with appropriate mathematical calculations.
questions.answer:
Two minutes is $120$ seconds, so $z = \dfrac{120 - 214}{30} = -3.13$.

A $z$-score below $-3$ occurs with a probability of less than $0.15\%$, so it is very unlikely that the waiting time will be two minutes or less.

questions.question: If $a = -3$, $b = 2$, what is the value of $\dfrac{b - a^2}{b - a}$?
Sanjoy purchased a laptop for \$3200 and depreciated it using a declining balance method at 10% per annum. How much is the laptop worth after 3 years?
Perth in Western Australia is 8 hours ahead of Greenwich in England. Cape Town in South Africa is 2 hours ahead of Greenwich. What is the time in Cape Town when it is 2 pm in Perth?
questions.answer: Cape Town is $8 - 2 = 6$ hours behind Perth, so the time is $2\ \text{pm} - 6\ \text{h} = 8$ am. **(B)**

questions.question: What is the equation of the line shown in the diagram?
questions.answer: The $y$-intercept is $-3$. The line passes through $(10, -7)$, so the gradient is $\dfrac{-7 - (-3)}{10 - 0} = -\dfrac{2}{5}$. So $y = -\dfrac{2}{5}x - 3$. **(A)**

questions.question: Consider the stem and leaf plot. The median and mode for the set of data are:
questions.answer: There are $1 + 4 + 5 + 5 + 2 = 17$ values, so the median is the 9th value, which is $35$. The mode is $47$ (it appears four times). **(B)**

questions.question: A bag contains 5 black and 7 white marbles. Two marbles are drawn from the bag one after the other without replacement. What is the probability of drawing a black marble first and then a white marble?
Corn flour is sold in four different sized packets. Which of the following is the best buy?
Which of the diagrams below best represents a relationship with a correlation coefficient of $r = -0.87$?
questions.answer:
$r = -0.87$ is a strong negative linear association with some scatter. A is positive, D has no linear trend (it is curved with $r$ near $0$), and C is an almost perfect straight line ($r$ very close to $-1$). B shows a decreasing trend with moderate scatter. **(B)**

(The school's answer key gives C, but C's points lie almost exactly on a line, which would give $r \approx -1$.)

questions.question: Tim scored 53 in a test for which the marks were normally distributed with a mean of 65 and a standard deviation of 12. What percentage of students scored higher marks than Tim?
questions.answer: $z = \dfrac{53 - 65}{12} = -1$. About $68\%$ of scores lie within one standard deviation, so $34\%$ lie between Tim's score and the mean and $50\%$ lie above the mean. Higher than Tim: $34 + 50 = 84\%$. **(D)**

questions.question: What is the length of the minimum spanning tree in the network below?
questions.answer: Add edges in order of increasing weight, skipping any that form a cycle: $2$, $3$, $4$, $5$, $5$, then $8$ and $8$ (the $6$, $7$ and the other $8$ would form cycles). That is 7 edges for 8 vertices: $2 + 3 + 4 + 5 + 5 + 8 + 8 = 35$. **(C)**

questions.question: A triangle has side lengths 2.1 cm, 3.7 cm and 1.9 cm, with angles of 55°, 78° and 47° as shown. Which of the following would give the area of this triangle?
questions.answer: $A = \frac{1}{2}ab\sin C$, where $C$ is the angle between sides $a$ and $b$. The $78^\circ$ angle is between the sides of length $2.1$ and $1.9$, so $A = \frac{1}{2} \times 2.1 \times 1.9 \times \sin 78^\circ$. **(B)**

questions.question: A function centre hosts events for up to 500 people. The cost $C$, in dollars, for the centre to host an event where $x$ people attend is given by $C = 10\,000 + 50x$. The centre charges \$100 per person. Its income $I$, in dollars, is given by $I = 100x$. The graph of each equation is shown. How much greater is the profit of the function centre when 500 people attend an event than its profit when 300 people attend?
A dividend of 4.65 cents per share is paid on shares with a market value of \$0.91. Which of the following is the dividend yield?
questions.answer: Dividend yield $= \dfrac{\text{dividend}}{\text{market value}} \times 100 = \dfrac{4.65}{91} \times 100 = 5.1\%$. **(D)**

questions.question:
Harry, a 78 kg male, goes to a party and drinks seven standard drinks over 4 hours. The blood alcohol content (BAC) for males can be estimated by
$$\text{BAC}_{\text{male}} = \frac{10N - 7.5H}{6.8M}$$
where $N$ is the number of standard drinks, $H$ is the number of hours drinking and $M$ is the mass in kilograms. Calculate Harry's BAC after 4 hours. Answer correct to 3 decimal places.

At a local football ground, the ratio of sausage rolls to beef pies sold was $3 : 4$. The ratio of beef pies to hot chips sold was $1 : 8$. If 640 hot chips were sold, how many sausage rolls were sold?
questions.answer:
Make the beef pie part equal: $4 : 32$. So sausage rolls : beef pies : hot chips $= 3 : 4 : 32$.

$32$ parts $= 640$, so $1$ part $= 20$ and $3$ parts $= 60$.

**60 sausage rolls.**

questions.question: The depreciation of a used car using both the straight-line and declining balance methods of depreciation is shown in the graph. After 2 years using the declining balance method, what is the salvage value of the used car?
questions.answer: Reading the curved (declining balance) graph at $2$ years gives **\$800**.

questions.question: The graph shows depreciation of a used car by both the straight-line and declining balance methods. Which method of depreciation would provide the largest depreciation for a tax deduction if the asset is to be kept for 5 years?
questions.answer: The straight-line method. After 5 years its value reaches \$0 (total depreciation \$2000), whereas the declining balance method still leaves the car with a value of about \$250, so its total depreciation is smaller.

questions.question: An object is projected vertically into the air. Its height, $h$ metres, above the ground after $t$ seconds is given by $h = -2t^2 + 10t$. A graph of this function is shown. By using the graph and showing calculations, find the maximum height of the object above the ground.
questions.answer:
The graph is symmetrical about its axis, which is midway between the $t$-intercepts $t = 0$ and $t = 5$, so the maximum occurs at $t = 2.5$.

$h = -2(2.5)^2 + 10(2.5) = -12.5 + 25 = 12.5$ m.

questions.question: Packets of sugar are filled and labelled as having a weight of 1 kg. The weight of these packets is normally distributed with a mean of 1.01 kg and a standard deviation of 0.01 kg. A packet of sugar is rejected if its weight is lower than 0.985 kg. What is the $z$-score of a packet of sugar with a weight of 0.985 kg?

The weight of packets of sugar is normally distributed with a mean of 1.01 kg and a standard deviation of 0.01 kg. A packet is rejected if its weight is lower than 0.985 kg ($z = -2.5$). Using the table of the standard normal distribution below (areas to the left of the $z$-score), calculate the probability that a randomly chosen packet of sugar is rejected.

| $z$ | 2.50 | 2.51 | 2.52 | 2.53 | 2.54 | 2.55 | 2.56 | 2.57 | 2.58 | 2.59 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Probability | 0.9937 | 0.9939 | 0.9941 | 0.9943 | 0.9944 | 0.9946 | 0.9947 | 0.9949 | 0.9950 | 0.9952 |
The probability that a packet of sugar is rejected is $0.0063$. From a batch of 1000 packets of sugar, how many would you expect to be rejected?
questions.answer: $0.0063 \times 1000 = 6.3 \approx 6$ packets.

questions.question: From the top of a 12 m tall building, the angles of depression of the top and foot of a lamp post are 30° and 60°, respectively. All measurements of length are in metres. Draw a diagram to show the given information.
questions.answer: Draw a vertical building of height $12$ and a vertical lamp post at some horizontal distance from it. From the top of the building draw a horizontal line; the line of sight to the top of the lamp post makes $30^\circ$ below the horizontal and the line of sight to the foot of the lamp post makes $60^\circ$ below the horizontal. Label the building $12$ and the lamp post height $h$.

questions.question: From the top of a 12 m tall building, the angles of depression of the top and foot of a lamp post are 30° and 60°, respectively. Find the height of the lamp post.
questions.answer:
Horizontal distance from the building to the lamp post: $\tan 60^\circ = \dfrac{12}{d} \Rightarrow d = \dfrac{12}{\tan 60^\circ} = 6.928$ m.

The top of the lamp post is below the top of the building by $x$, where $\tan 30^\circ = \dfrac{x}{d}$, so $x = 6.928 \times \tan 30^\circ = 4$ m.

Height of the lamp post $= 12 - 4 = 8$ m.

questions.question:
Data was gathered from eight students on the average number of hours ($h$) of sleep they get on school nights, and the number of times they got distracted in class ($d$).

| $h$ | 7.5 | 8 | 7 | 6 | 5 | 6.5 | 6 | 5.5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $d$ | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 8 | 12 | 15 | 17 |

Use a calculator to find Pearson's correlation coefficient ($r$) to two decimal places and describe the strength and direction of the relationship.
questions.answer:
$r = -0.629\ldots \approx -0.63$.

There is a moderate negative linear relationship: students who sleep more tend to be distracted fewer times.

questions.question: For the data on hours of sleep ($h$) and times distracted ($d$) for eight students (points $(7.5, 3)$, $(8, 4)$, $(7, 5)$, $(6, 6)$, $(5, 8)$, $(6.5, 12)$, $(6, 15)$, $(5.5, 17)$), use a calculator to find the equation of the least-squares line of best fit.

The data on hours of sleep ($h$) and times distracted ($d$) is plotted on the scatterplot below. The least-squares regression line is $d = -3.273h + 29.818$. Sketch the graph of the least-squares regression line on the scatterplot.
questions.answer: Plot two points on the line and join them. For example, at $h = 5$, $d = 13.5$, and at $h = 8$, $d = 3.6$. The line slopes downwards and passes through the middle of the points.

questions.question: Use the equation of the least-squares regression line $d = -3.273h + 29.818$ to predict the average hours of sleep on school nights for a student who has 20 distractions in class.
questions.answer:
$20 = -3.273h + 29.818 \Rightarrow 3.273h = 9.818 \Rightarrow h = 3.0$.

About **3 hours** of sleep. (This is an extrapolation outside the data range of $5$ to $8$ hours, so it is not very reliable.)

questions.question: Before the start of an examination, students are required to place their mobile phone in a box. Of the 90 mobile phones in the box, 20 were Samsung, 30 were Apple and 40 were Huawei. A partially completed tree diagram shows the probability of randomly drawing two particular phones (without replacement) from the box. Complete the probability tree diagram, by writing probabilities on each of the branches.
questions.answer:
First phone: Apple $\frac{30}{90}$, Samsung $\frac{20}{90}$, Huawei $\frac{40}{90}$.

Second phone (without replacement):

| First phone | Apple | Samsung | Huawei |
|---|---|---|---|
| Apple | $\frac{29}{89}$ | $\frac{20}{89}$ | $\frac{40}{89}$ |
| Samsung | $\frac{30}{89}$ | $\frac{19}{89}$ | $\frac{40}{89}$ |
| Huawei | $\frac{30}{89}$ | $\frac{20}{89}$ | $\frac{39}{89}$ |

questions.question: In a box of 90 phones (20 Samsung, 30 Apple, 40 Huawei), two phones are drawn without replacement. Calculate the probability that both mobile phones drawn are Samsung.
In a box of 90 phones (20 Samsung, 30 Apple, 40 Huawei), calculate the probability that the first mobile phone drawn is either an Apple or a Huawei.
In a box of 90 phones (20 Samsung, 30 Apple, 40 Huawei), two phones are drawn without replacement. Calculate the probability that neither of the mobile phones drawn are Huawei.
questions.answer:
Neither is Huawei means both are Apple or Samsung (50 phones):

$$P = \frac{50}{90} \times \frac{49}{89} = \frac{2450}{8010} = \frac{245}{801}.$$

(Adding the four branches AA, AS, SA, SS gives the same result: $\frac{870 + 600 + 600 + 380}{8010} = \frac{245}{801}$.)

questions.question: Georgia leaves Sydney ($34^\circ$S, $151^\circ$E) at 11:00 am Friday, flying to Honolulu ($21^\circ$N, $158^\circ$W). Sydney standard time is UTC + 10 and Honolulu standard time is UTC − 10. What is the time and day in Honolulu when Georgia leaves Sydney?
questions.answer: The time difference is $10 - (-10) = 20$ hours, with Honolulu behind Sydney. So $11{:}00$ am Friday in Sydney is $11{:}00$ am $- 20$ h $= 3{:}00$ pm **Thursday** in Honolulu.

questions.question: Georgia leaves Sydney at 11:00 am Friday (3:00 pm Thursday in Honolulu). The flight time is $11\frac{1}{2}$ hours. What is the day and time in Honolulu when she arrives?
questions.answer: $3{:}00\ \text{pm} + 11.5\ \text{h} = 2{:}30$ am **Friday** in Honolulu.

questions.question: Young's rule for calculating the medicine dosage for infants is $D = \dfrac{yA}{y + 12}$, where $y$ is the age of the infant in years and $A$ is the adult dosage. How old is Rita if her medicine dosage is 0.6 mL and the adult dosage is 15 mL?
questions.answer:
$$0.6 = \frac{15y}{y + 12} \Rightarrow 0.6y + 7.2 = 15y \Rightarrow 7.2 = 14.4y \Rightarrow y = 0.5$$

Rita is **0.5 years** (6 months) old.

questions.question: A company has received customer complaints over the past month. The results are shown in the Pareto chart below. Approximately what percentage of complaints were due to late delivery or damaged products?
questions.answer: Late delivery $40$ and damaged products $25$ out of $100$ complaints, so about $65\%$ (the cumulative percentage line after the second bar).

questions.question: A company has received customer complaints over the past month, shown in the Pareto chart below. Approximately what percentage of complaints were due to poor customer service?
questions.answer: The poor customer service bar has a frequency of $10$ out of $100$ complaints, so about $10\%$.

questions.question: Chloe wants to investigate the population of woodlice that live in a greenhouse. On Saturday she caught 90 woodlice. She puts a mark on each of them and returns them to the greenhouse. On Sunday, Chloe caught a number of woodlice ($y$) and found that 12 of these woodlice had been marked. Chloe's estimate for the number of woodlice in the greenhouse is 600. Calculate how many woodlice Chloe caught on Sunday.
questions.answer:
The proportion marked in the sample equals the proportion marked in the population: $\dfrac{12}{y} = \dfrac{90}{600} \Rightarrow y = \dfrac{12 \times 600}{90} = 80$.

Chloe caught **80** woodlice on Sunday.

questions.question: The power consumption of a wash cycle for a front loader washing machine is 1600 W. The machine is used 5 times a week and it takes 36 minutes to complete a wash cycle. Electricity is charged at the rate of 32.8735 cents/kWh. What is the total cost of using this washing machine for one year?
questions.answer:
Energy per week $= 1.6\ \text{kW} \times \dfrac{36}{60}\ \text{h} \times 5 = 4.8$ kWh.

Cost per week $= 4.8 \times \$0.328735 = \$1.5779$.

Cost per year $= 1.5779 \times 52 = \$82.05$.

questions.question: Hari made a silk-covered lampshade in the shape of a square-based pyramid. The lampshade has no base, and consists of the four triangular faces only. The height of the lampshade is 20 cm and the slant height is 32 cm. If the total material required to make the lampshade is $3201\ \text{cm}^2$, find the perimeter of the base of the square pyramid, correct to 1 decimal place.
questions.answer:
Let $x$ be the side length of the base. The four triangular faces each have base $x$ and height $32$ (the slant height):

$$4 \times \tfrac{1}{2} \times x \times 32 = 3201 \Rightarrow 64x = 3201 \Rightarrow x = 50.016\ldots$$

Perimeter of the base $= 4x = 200.1$ cm.

(The school's solution stops at the side length, $x \approx 50$ cm, but the question asks for the perimeter.)

questions.question: A project is represented by the network below, with activity times in days. Determine the critical path by completing the earliest starting time (EST) and latest starting time (LST).
questions.answer:
Forward scan (EST) and backward scan (LST) at each vertex, from left to right: Start $0$ | $0$; after A $6$ | $6$; after B $9$ | $9$; after E $9$ | $17$; after C $11$ | $11$; after F $16$ | $16$; after D (and the dummy) $17$ | $17$; after G and H $20$ | $20$; Finish $27$ | $27$.

The critical path is $A$–$B$–$D$–$G$–$L$ or $A$–$C$–$F$–$H$–$L$ (each $27$ days).

questions.question: In the project network (activities A,6; B,3; C,5; D,8; E,3; F,5; G,3; H,4; K,2; L,7, with a dummy activity from the end of E to the end of D), by how much can the activity E be delayed without affecting the project?
questions.answer: Activity E can start as early as day $6$ and must finish by day $17$ (the latest start of the vertex it leads to through the dummy). Float $= 17 - 6 - 3 = 8$ days.

questions.question:
The tax table shows the income tax rates for the 2023–2024 financial year.

| Taxable income | Tax payable |
|---|---|
| \$0 – \$11 000 | Nil |
| \$11 001 – \$42 400 | 20 cents for each \$1 over \$11 000 |
| \$42 401 – \$78 800 | \$6280 plus 33 cents for each \$1 over \$42 400 |
| \$78 801 – \$108 400 | \$18 292 plus 44 cents for each \$1 over \$78 800 |
| \$108 401 and over | \$31 316 plus 48 cents for each \$1 over \$108 400 |

Sarah works as an accountant and receives a yearly salary of \$64 479 plus an income of \$1950 per year from babysitting. If Sarah has annual tax deductions of \$1570 for home office equipment, and \$575 for union fees, calculate her taxable income.
Using the 2023–2024 tax table (\$42 401 – \$78 800: \$6280 plus 33 cents for each \$1 over \$42 400), calculate the tax payable on a taxable income of \$64 284.

The number of years ($N$) required to carry out a project varies inversely with how much money ($M$) is spent on it. If \$60 000 is spent on the project, it takes 6 years to complete, as shown in the graph. Find the equation for the graph in terms of $M$ and $N$ in the form $N = \dfrac{k}{M}$, where $k$ is a constant.

The number of years required to carry out a project is $N = \dfrac{360\,000}{M}$, where $M$ is the money spent in dollars. The project needs to be carried out in one year or less. What is the least amount of money that could be spent in order to achieve this timeline?
questions.answer:
$1 = \dfrac{360\,000}{M} \Rightarrow M = 360\,000$.

At least **\$360 000** must be spent.

questions.question: Sally starts at a jetty $J$ and swims on a bearing of 105° for 5 km out to a buoy $L$. She then swims on a bearing of 045° for a further 16 km to buoy $M$. Find $\angle JLM$.
questions.answer:
The bearing of $J$ from $L$ is $105^\circ + 180^\circ = 285^\circ$, and the bearing of $M$ from $L$ is $045^\circ$. The angle between them is $360^\circ - 285^\circ + 45^\circ = 120^\circ$.

(Equivalently, co-interior angles give $75^\circ + 45^\circ = 120^\circ$.)

questions.question: Sally swims 5 km from $J$ to $L$ and then 16 km from $L$ to $M$, with $\angle JLM = 120^\circ$. Find the distance $JM$ that Sally will swim back to the jetty.
Sally swims from jetty $J$ on a bearing of 105° for 5 km to buoy $L$. Find the bearing of jetty $J$ from the buoy $L$.
questions.answer: The reverse bearing is $105^\circ + 180^\circ = 285^\circ$.

questions.question: A plumber needs to fix a system of pipes. The sink ($t$) is connected to the water source ($S$) by an interconnected series of one-directional pipes. The capacity of each pipe is shown. What is the capacity of the cut shown?
questions.answer: Add the capacities of the pipes that cross the cut from the source side to the sink side: $7 + 3 + 4 + 6 = 20$. (The pipes carrying flow back across the cut towards the source are not counted.)

questions.question: Draw a cut of capacity 12 on the network diagram below.
questions.answer: Separate $\{S, \text{top-left}, \text{middle}, \text{bottom-left}\}$ from the other vertices and $t$. The pipes crossing from the source side are $3$ (middle to top-right), $4$ (bottom-left to middle-right) and $5$ (bottom-left to bottom-right): $3 + 4 + 5 = 12$.

questions.question: The plumber wants to identify the smallest cut possible (in terms of capacity). By finding the maximum flow, explain why this is the smallest cut possible. Justify your response on the diagram below.
questions.answer:
Only three pipes lead into the sink: from the top-right vertex (capacity 7, but it can only receive 3), from the middle-right vertex (capacity 9, but it can only receive 4) and from the bottom-right vertex (capacity 7, but it can only receive 5). A flow of $12$ can be achieved: send $3$ along $S \to$ middle $\to$ top-right $\to t$; send $3$ along $S \to$ top-left $\to$ middle $\to$ bottom-left, and $6$ along $S \to$ bottom-left, so bottom-left receives $9$ and passes on $4$ to the middle-right vertex and $5$ to the bottom-right vertex, which then reach $t$.

The maximum flow is $12$. By the maximum-flow minimum-cut theorem the minimum cut also has capacity $12$, so the cut of capacity $12$ in part (b) is the smallest possible.

questions.question: Tickets to a concert cost \$5 for children and \$14 for adults. Altogether, 650 people attended the concert and ticket sales totalled \$5824. Let $a$ be the number of adults and $c$ be the number of children. Write two relevant equations from the information provided.

Tickets to a concert cost \$5 for children and \$14 for adults. Altogether, 650 people attended and ticket sales totalled \$5824, so $a + c = 650$ and $14a + 5c = 5824$. Solve the equations simultaneously to find the number of children and adults that attended the concert.
questions.answer:
Multiply the first equation by 5: $5a + 5c = 3250$. Subtract from the second: $9a = 2574 \Rightarrow a = 286$.

$c = 650 - 286 = 364$.

**286 adults and 364 children.**

questions.question: Vicky bought 600 shares in Myer at \$1.82 per share. Brokerage fees were 2% of the purchase price. Vicky is paid a dividend of 25 cents per share, then immediately sells the shares for \$2.50 each. If she pays no further brokerage fees, what is Vicky's total profit?

A lake sits within a rectangular grass picnic area $ABCD$, as shown in the diagram (all measurements in metres, not to scale). Use two applications of the Trapezoidal Rule to approximate the area of the lake's surface.
questions.answer:
The picnic area is $14 \times 50 = 700\ \text{m}^2$ ($50 = 30 + 20$).

Grass above the lake: $\frac{14}{2}(30 + 22) = 364$. Grass below the lake: $\frac{14}{2}(20 + 18) = 266$. Total grass $\approx 630\ \text{m}^2$.

Area of the lake $\approx 700 - 630 = 70\ \text{m}^2$.

questions.question: A lake has a surface area of about $70\ \text{m}^2$ and is 80 cm deep. Arjun thinks he can empty the lake using a five-litre bucket. How many times would he have to fill his bucket from the lake in order to empty the lake?
questions.answer:
Volume $= 70 \times 0.8 = 56\ \text{m}^3 = 56\,000$ L.

Number of buckets $= \dfrac{56\,000}{5} = 11\,200$.

questions.question: The cost ($C$) of producing cotton bags is initially \$2000 plus \$2.50 per item ($n$). Each bag is sold for \$5. (i) Write an equation to represent the cost of production ($C$). (ii) Write an equation to represent the revenue ($R$).
The cost of producing cotton bags is $C = 2.5n + 2000$ and the revenue is $R = 5n$. On the grid below, sketch the graphs of both equations.
questions.answer: Cost line: starts at $(0, 2000)$ and passes through $(1200, 5000)$. Revenue line: starts at $(0, 0)$ and passes through $(1200, 6000)$. The lines cross at $(800, 4000)$.

questions.question: From the graph of $C = 2.5n + 2000$ and $R = 5n$, determine the number of bags that must be sold to break even.
questions.answer: The lines intersect at $n = 800$ (where $2.5n = 2000$), so **800 bags**.

questions.question: From the graph of $C = 2.5n + 2000$ and $R = 5n$, determine how many bags must be sold to make a profit of \$1000.
questions.answer: Profit $= R - C = 2.5n - 2000 = 1000 \Rightarrow n = 1200$. **1200 bags** (where the revenue line is \$1000 above the cost line).

questions.question: It took Bella 3 hours and 20 minutes to travel 180 km from her house to the camping site. What was Bella's average speed?
questions.answer: $3\text{ h }20\text{ min}=3\frac13\text{ h}=\frac{10}3$ h. Speed $=180\div\frac{10}3=54$ km/h (C).

questions.question: Which network is an Eulerian circuit? (A circuit using every edge exactly once exists when every vertex has even degree.)
questions.answer: An Eulerian circuit exists only when every vertex has even degree. In A two vertices have degree 3, and in C and D some vertices have degree 3. In B every vertex has degree 2 or 4 (the doubled edge gives the two middle vertices degree 4), so B is Eulerian (B).

questions.question: Which equation describes the relationship between the two variables $a$ and $b$ shown on the graph? The line has $b$-intercept 3 and passes through $(6,15)$.
questions.answer: Gradient $=\frac{15-3}{6-0}=2$ and the $b$-intercept is $3$, so $b=2a+3$ (A).

questions.question: Majella stands at the school gate and hands over a questionnaire to every 20th student. What kind of sampling is she using?
questions.answer: Choosing every 20th member of a population is systematic sampling (D).

questions.question: Olivia bought a new car three years ago for \$35 500 and since then it has depreciated at 22% p.a. using the declining balance method. What is the current value of the car?
In a car yard, the ratio of red to white cars is 3 : 5 and the ratio of red to black cars is 4 : 3. What is the ratio of white to black cars?
questions.answer: Make the red numbers equal (LCM 12): red : white $=12:20$ and red : black $=12:9$. So white : black $=20:9$ (D).

questions.question: The weight $w$ in kilograms of copper plumbing pipe is directly proportional to the length $d$ of the pipe in metres. A 5 m pipe weighs 2.45 kg. What is the gradient $m$ of the direct variation graph $w=md$?

Aishani's hourly base rate is \$64.50. When she operates the crane she is paid a 22% allowance on top of her normal hourly rate. What is she paid for a 40-hour week in which she operated the crane for 18 hours?

The Pareto chart shows delivery complaints for an online store (shown). Katrina wants to address only the complaints about 'Delivery to Wrong Address'. What percentage of the total complaints will she address?
questions.answer: The bars are $41,22,13,11,9,4$ cases, a total of $100$. 'Delivery to Wrong Address' has $13$ cases, so $13\%$ (A).

questions.question: A researcher calculates Pearson's correlation coefficient as $-0.8$ for a set of bivariate data. Which scatterplot could best represent this data?
questions.answer: $r=-0.8$ is a strong negative linear correlation: the points trend clearly downwards with moderate scatter. Only B does this (A and D slope up, C has weak correlation) (B).

questions.question:
