The stem-and-leaf plot shows the hourly wages (\$) of a manufacturing company.

| Stem | Leaves |
|---|---|
| 4 | 0 0 2 2 2 4 8 8 8 |
| 5 | 0 0 1 5 6 6 8 9 9 |
| 6 | 3 6 7 8 |
| 7 | 1 |
| 8 | 3 7 |
| 9 | 6 |

Which box-and-whisker plot best represents the distribution?
questions.answer: There are $26$ values. Minimum $=40$, maximum $=96$. Median $=\frac{55+56}2=55.5$. $Q_1=48$ (the 7th value) and $Q_3=66$ (the 20th value). The plot with these five numbers, with a long upper whisker, is B (B).

questions.question: Alina bought a car with a cash price of \$9500 on terms. She paid a deposit of \$1000 and the rest plus interest over 12 months in equal instalments. Simple interest of 8% p.a. was charged on the remaining amount. How much was each monthly payment?
questions.answer: Amount borrowed $=9500-1000=\$8500$. $I=Prn=8500\times0.08\times1=\$680$. Total $=\$9180$, so each payment is $9180\div12=\$765.00$ (A).

questions.question: If the GST increases from 10% to 12%, the price of a textbook rises by \$1.44. What is the original price of the textbook, including GST?
questions.answer: The rise is $2\%$ of the pre-GST price, so the pre-GST price is $1.44\div0.02=\$72$. The original price including $10\%$ GST is $72\times1.1=\$79.20$ (D).

questions.question: At a fixed temperature, the pressure $p$ and volume $v$ of a gas satisfy $pv=100$. Which graph could represent this relationship?
questions.answer: $v=\frac{100}p$ is an inverse variation (reciprocal) relationship, whose graph is a hyperbola decreasing towards the $p$-axis without touching either axis (D).

questions.question: Solve the equation $\dfrac x3+2=3x$.
questions.answer: $\frac x3+2=3x\Rightarrow x+6=9x\Rightarrow 6=8x\Rightarrow x=\frac34$.

questions.question: Annie tags 50 kangaroos and releases them. A week later she captures 40 kangaroos, of which 10 are tagged. Using capture-recapture, estimate the total kangaroo population in the park.
questions.answer: $\frac{\text{tagged in sample}}{\text{sample}}=\frac{\text{tagged in total}}{N}$: $\frac{10}{40}=\frac{50}N\Rightarrow N=\frac{50\times40}{10}=200$ kangaroos.

questions.question: A 240 g packet of biscuits costs \$3.91. Week 1: buy two and get one free. Week 2: 30% discount on the regular price. Holly wants 4 packets. Which week is the better deal? Show working.
questions.answer: Week 1: she pays for 2 of the first 3 packets, plus the 4th: $3\times3.91=\$11.73$. Week 2: $4\times3.91\times0.70=\$10.95$ (to the nearest cent). Week 2 is the better deal for 4 packets.

questions.question: In 2022 inflation was 4.6%, in 2023 it was 6.5% and in 2024 it was 2.3%. Alexia's weekly groceries cost \$250.00 at the start of 2022. What would the same basket cost at the end of 2024?
questions.answer: $250\times1.046\times1.065\times1.023=\$284.90$ (to the nearest cent).

questions.question: Rayani is paid an annual salary of \$35 000 plus 1% commission on all sales and a car allowance of \$60 per week (52 weeks). What is her total yearly income if she sold \$12 000 000 of property in the year?

Rayani has taxable income \$158 120 and no deductions. Use the table to find the tax payable, excluding the Medicare levy.

| Taxable income | Tax on this income |
|---|---|
| 0 – \$18 200 | Nil |
| \$18 201 – \$45 000 | 16 cents for each \$1 over \$18 200 |
| \$45 001 – \$135 000 | \$4 288 plus 30 cents for each \$1 over \$45 000 |
| \$135 001 – \$190 000 | \$31 288 plus 37 cents for each \$1 over \$135 000 |
| \$190 001 and over | \$51 638 plus 45 cents for each \$1 over \$190 000 |
Samia's car uses 8.5 litres of petrol per 100 km. She travelled for 4.5 hours at an average speed of 75 km/h. How many litres of petrol (to one decimal place) did the car use?
questions.answer: Distance $=75\times4.5=337.5$ km. Petrol $=\frac{337.5}{100}\times8.5=28.6875\approx28.7$ L.

questions.question: The scatterplot shows the number of ice-creams sold against the daily temperature (°C), with a least-squares regression line fitted (shown). Find the approximate gradient of the regression line.
questions.answer: Read two points on the line, e.g. $(2,0)$ and $(30,25)$: $m=\frac{25-0}{30-2}\approx0.89$ (about $0.9$; values from $0.85$ to $0.9$ are acceptable).

questions.question: For the same scatterplot and regression line (shown), estimate the vertical intercept of the line.
questions.answer: Extending the line back to the vertical axis (where $T=0$) gives an intercept of about $-2$ (the line crosses the horizontal axis near $T=2$).

questions.question: For the same scatterplot and regression line (shown), write the equation of the least-squares regression line.
questions.answer: Using gradient $\approx0.89$ and intercept $\approx-2$: $\text{ice-creams sold}\approx0.89\times\text{temperature}-2$.

questions.question: For the same scatterplot (shown), describe the correlation between temperature and ice-creams sold in your own words.
questions.answer: There is a moderate to strong positive linear correlation: as the temperature rises, the number of ice-creams sold tends to increase.

questions.question: Venice drives at 11 m/s and takes 0.5 seconds to react before applying the brakes. How far does the car travel during her reaction time?
questions.answer: Distance $=\text{speed}\times\text{time}=11\times0.5=5.5$ m.

questions.question: The graph shows braking distance (m) against speed (m/s). What is Venice's braking distance after she applies the brakes, when travelling at 11 m/s?
questions.answer: Reading the graph at $S=11$ gives a braking distance of about $6$ m.

questions.question: Using the same braking-distance graph (shown), if Venice drove at 15 m/s instead with the same 0.5 s reaction time, how much longer would her stopping distance be than at 11 m/s?
questions.answer: At $15$ m/s: reaction distance $=0.5\times15=7.5$ m and braking distance (from the graph) $\approx11.2$ m, so stopping distance $\approx18.7$ m. At $11$ m/s: $5.5+6=11.5$ m. Difference $\approx18.7-11.5=7.2$ m.

questions.question: Sydney is UTC +10 and Vancouver is UTC −7. When it is 4 pm on Friday in Vancouver, what is the time and day in Sydney?
questions.answer: Sydney is $10-(-7)=17$ hours ahead. $4\text{ pm}+17\text{ h}=33{:}00$, i.e. $9$ am on Saturday.

questions.question: At 4 pm Friday (Vancouver time) Monique takes a 16-hour direct flight from Vancouver to Sydney. On which day and at what time (Sydney time) does she land?
questions.answer: She leaves at 9 am Saturday Sydney time. Add $16$ hours: $9+16=25$, so $1$ am on Sunday (Sydney time).

questions.question: Louise's block has one irregular boundary along a road. Offsets taken at right angles to the straight boundary at equal intervals of 90 m are $0$, $140$, $80$ and $105$ m (total length 270 m, shown). Use three applications of the trapezoidal rule to find the area in hectares, to two decimal places.
A cake is a cylinder of diameter 20 cm and height 9 cm topped with a cone of height 10 cm (shown). Calculate the volume of the cake to the nearest cm³.
The conical top of the cake (radius 10 cm, height 10 cm) is coated with chocolate. Find the curved surface area to be coated, using $S=\pi rl$ where $l$ is the slant height.
questions.answer: $l=\sqrt{10^2+10^2}=\sqrt{200}\approx14.14$ cm. $S=\pi\times10\times\sqrt{200}\approx444.29\ \text{cm}^2$. (The school's working writes $\sqrt{250}$, a slip: the value $444.29$ is the correct result for $\sqrt{200}$.)

questions.question: The chocolate coating on the conical part (surface area $444.29\ \text{cm}^2$) is 3 mm thick. Calculate the volume of chocolate used, to the nearest mL.
questions.answer: $3\text{ mm}=0.3$ cm. $V\approx444.29\times0.3=133.29\ \text{cm}^3\approx133$ mL (since $1\ \text{cm}^3=1$ mL).

questions.question: The directed network shows the water supply route from source A to sink J (capacities shown). Find the maximum flow of the network.
questions.answer: Consider the cut separating $\{A,B,C,D,G\}$ from the rest. The edges leaving it are $G\to I$ (35), $D\to E$ (50), $A\to E$ (120) and $C\to F$ (120). Capacity $=35+50+120+120=325$. A flow of 325 can be achieved, so the maximum flow is $325$.

questions.question: Nandha wins the first set against Loretta $\frac27$ of the time. If she wins the first set she wins the second $\frac35$ of the time; if she loses the first set she wins the second $\frac15$ of the time. Complete the probability tree (shown).
questions.answer: First set: $P(W)=\frac27$, $P(L)=1-\frac27=\frac57$. After a win: $P(W)=\frac35$, $P(L)=\frac25$. After a loss: $P(W)=\frac15$, $P(L)=\frac45$.

questions.question: With the probabilities from the tree ($P(\text{lose set 1})=\frac57$, then $P(\text{lose set 2}\mid\text{lost set 1})=\frac45$), what is the probability that Nandha loses both sets?
questions.answer: $P(LL)=\frac57\times\frac45=\frac{20}{35}=\frac47$.

questions.question: The probability that Nandha loses both sets is $\frac47$. What is the probability she wins at least one of the two sets?
questions.answer: $P(\text{at least one win})=1-P(LL)=1-\frac47=\frac37$.

questions.question: Using the table of future value interest factors (5.5% column, 6 periods: $6.888$), Sarah wants \$300 000 in an annuity account after 6 years (5.5% p.a. compounding annually). Her salary is \$125 000. What percentage of her salary should she contribute each year?
questions.answer: Contribution $=\frac{300\,000}{6.888}\approx\$43\,554$. As a percentage of salary: $\frac{43\,554}{125\,000}\approx34.84\%$.

questions.question: Sarah contributes \$43 554 a year for 6 years to reach \$300 000. How much interest does she earn?
Louise owns 600 shares in Logitec bought at \$9.50 each. They are now valued at \$14.25 each and Logitec pays a dividend of \$2.41 per share. What is the dividend yield?
questions.answer: Dividend yield $=\frac{2.41}{14.25}\times100\%\approx16.91\%$.

questions.question: Louise (600 shares bought at \$9.50, dividend \$2.41 per share) sells them at \$14.25 each and pays brokerage of 0.5% of the sale value. What percentage profit did she make on her investment?
The table shows a weighted network (shown). Draw the network as a diagram.
questions.answer: List the edges and weights from the table: $AB=60$, $AC=55$, $AD=70$, $BD=45$, $CD=65$, $CF=70$, $DE=95$, $DF=50$, $EF=40$. Draw the vertices $A$ to $F$ and join each pair with the weight on the edge.

questions.question: Using the same weighted network (edges $AB=60$, $AC=55$, $AD=70$, $BD=45$, $CD=65$, $CF=70$, $DE=95$, $DF=50$, $EF=40$), find the shortest path from $A$ to $E$ and its length.
questions.answer: Candidate paths: $A\!-\!D\!-\!F\!-\!E=70+50+40=160$; $A\!-\!D\!-\!E=165$; $A\!-\!C\!-\!F\!-\!E=165$; $A\!-\!B\!-\!D\!-\!F\!-\!E=195$. The shortest is $A\to D\to F\to E$ with length $160$. (The school lists 'ADFE or ADE', but ADE has length 165 so only ADFE is shortest.)

questions.question: Eleanor borrows \$1200. Interest is added at the end of each month before the \$100 repayment is taken off. The table shows month 1: start \$1200.00, after interest \$1212.00. What is the interest rate per month?
questions.answer: $\frac{1212-1200}{1200}=0.01$, so the rate is $1\%$ per month.

questions.question: Continue the loan table (balance at month 11 start is \$279.3253, repayments of \$100, 1% monthly interest) until the loan is repaid. What is the final repayment and in which month is it made?
questions.answer: Month 11: $279.3253\to282.1186\to182.1186$. Month 12: $182.1186\to183.9397\to83.9397$. Month 13: $83.9397\to84.7791$ with interest, which is less than \$100, so the loan is cleared by a final repayment of $\$84.78$ in month 13.

questions.question: In the diagram (shown), $P,Q,R,T,H$ surround the centre $O$ with $OQ=320$ m, $OR=150$ m and $QR=412$ m. Find $\angle QOR$ to the nearest degree.
questions.answer: $\cos\angle QOR=\frac{320^2+150^2-412^2}{2\times320\times150}=\frac{-44\,844}{96\,000}$, so $\angle QOR=117.85^\circ\approx118^\circ$.

questions.question: Using the same diagram ($OQ=320$ m, $OR=150$ m, $\angle QOR=117.85^\circ$), find the area of triangle $QOR$ to the nearest square metre.
questions.answer: $A=\frac12(320)(150)\sin117.85^\circ\approx21\,221\ \text{m}^2$. (The school uses the rounded angle $118^\circ$ and gets $21\,191$ m²; the unrounded angle gives the more accurate $21\,221$ m².)

questions.question: In the same diagram, $P O R$ is a straight line and $\angle QOR\approx118^\circ$. Find $\angle QOP$.
questions.answer: $\angle QOP=180^\circ-118^\circ=62^\circ$ (angles on a straight line).

questions.question: In the same diagram, $P$ has bearing $315^\circ$ from $O$, $POR$ and $TOQ$ are straight lines and $\angle TOH=30^\circ$. $\angle QOP=62^\circ$. What is the bearing of $H$ from $O$?
questions.answer: $P$ is at $315^\circ$, so $Q$ is $62^\circ$ clockwise from $P$: $315^\circ+62^\circ=377^\circ=17^\circ$. $T$ is opposite $Q$, at $17^\circ+180^\circ=197^\circ$. $H$ is a further $30^\circ$ clockwise: $197^\circ+30^\circ=227^\circ$.

questions.question: In the diagram (shown), $OPQR$ and $OMNL$ are rectangles, $P=(3,0)$, $M=(7,0)$, and $N$ lies on the line $y=3x+1$. What is the value of $L$ (the $y$-coordinate of $L$)?
questions.answer: $N$ has $x=7$, so $y=3(7)+1=22$. Since $L$ is level with $N$, $L=22$.

questions.question: In the same diagram, $Q=(3,10)$ lies on $y=3x+1$ and $N=(7,22)$. What is the length of $QN$?
questions.answer: Horizontal change $=7-3=4$ and vertical change $=22-10=12$. $QN=\sqrt{4^2+12^2}=\sqrt{160}\approx12.65$.

questions.question: Head circumference is normally distributed with mean 54.0 cm and standard deviation 1.0 cm. What is the $z$-score of a person with head circumference 54.5 cm?
Head circumference has mean 54.0 cm and standard deviation 1.0 cm; $P(Z<0.5)=0.6915$ from the table. What percentage of people are expected to have head circumference below 54.5 cm?
questions.answer: $z=0.5$, and the table gives $0.6915$, so about $69.15\%$.

questions.question: Of 1000 participants, head circumference is normally distributed with mean 54.0 cm and standard deviation 1.0 cm. By calculating $z$-scores, find the number of participants with head circumference between 53.5 cm and 54.5 cm. (Use $P(Z<0.5)=0.6915$.)
A set of whole-number scores has interquartile range $p$, lower quartile $2p$, and $73$ as its smallest possible upper outlier. What is the highest possible lower outlier score?
questions.answer: $Q_1=2p$, $IQR=p$, so $Q_3=3p$. The smallest upper outlier is $73$, so $72$ is not an outlier, giving the upper fence $Q_3+1.5p=72$, i.e. $4.5p=72$ and $p=16$. Then $Q_1=32$ and the lower fence is $Q_1-1.5p=32-24=8$. Lower outliers are scores below $8$, so the highest possible is $7$.

questions.question: A project has tasks $A$ to $I$ with the network shown (durations in days: $A=20$, $B=12$, $C=8$, $D=6$, $E=11$, $F=5$, $G=7$, $H=9$, $I=15$). What is the critical path?
questions.answer: Complete paths: $ABDGI=60$, $ABDH=47$, $ACEGI=61$, $ACEH=48$, $ACFI=48$. The longest is $A\,C\,E\,G\,I$, so that is the critical path.

questions.question: Using the same network (shown), what is the minimum time required to complete the project?
questions.answer: The length of the critical path: $20+8+11+7+15=61$ days.

questions.question: The project must be completed in 55 days. Task $A$ cannot be shortened, but any other task can. Using the same network (shown), nominate a task that could be shortened and the minimum number of days it must be reduced by.
questions.answer: The critical path is $61$ days, so $6$ days must be saved. A second path $ABDGI$ is $60$ days, so the task must lie on both paths: $G$ or $I$. Reducing $I$ (or $G$) by $6$ days gives $ACEGI=55$ and $ABDGI=54$, so the project is completed in $55$ days. The minimum reduction is $6$ days (e.g. task $I$).

questions.question: Thomas went for a run. He stopped to check his pulse and counted 39 beats in 15 seconds. How can Thomas calculate his pulse rate in beats per minute?
questions.answer: The rate per second is $39 \div 15$; there are $60$ seconds in a minute, so multiply by $60$: $39 \div 15 \times 60 = 156$ beats per minute. **(C)**

questions.question: A survey asked students to indicate their favourite pet from the list: dog, cat, fish, bird, rabbit, or other. What type of data is this?
questions.answer: The responses are categories with no natural order, so the data is categorical nominal. **(A)**

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a linear function?
questions.answer: $y = -\dfrac{3}{x}$ is a reciprocal (inverse variation) function, whose graph is a hyperbola. The others have the form $y = mx + c$. **(C)**

questions.question: As of 2025, the current official land speed record is held by ThrustSSC at a speed of almost 1228 km/h. What is this speed in metres per second?
A laptop costs \$899, including 10% GST. What is the price of the laptop before GST?
questions.answer: The price including GST is $110\%$ of the original price: $\dfrac{899}{1.1} = \$817.27$. **(C)**
The trains arriving at Gadigal before 8:30 are the ones reaching it at 08:15 and 08:25. The latest of these arrives at Gadigal at 08:25 and leaves Cherrybrook at 07:54. **(D)**

questions.question: Charlie invested \$22 000 that will be compounded monthly at 6% per annum. Which calculation will give the value of his investment after four years?
questions.answer: The monthly rate is $\dfrac{6\%}{12} = 0.5\%$ and the number of compounding periods is $4 \times 12 = 48$. So $FV = 22\,000\left(1 + \dfrac{0.5}{100}\right)^{48}$. **(B)**

questions.question: Daniel has 1000 shares in Alphabet Corp. A dividend of 18 cents per share is paid on his shares with a market value per share of \$4.50. What is the dividend yield?
questions.answer: Dividend yield $= \dfrac{0.18}{4.50} \times 100 = 4\%$. **(D)**

questions.question: Siem Reap has a latitude of $13^\circ$ N and a longitude of $104^\circ$ E. Bangkok is due west of Siem Reap. The coordinates of Bangkok could be:
questions.answer: Due west means the same latitude ($13^\circ$ N) and a smaller longitude east of Greenwich. Only $(13^\circ\text{ N}, 100^\circ\text{ E})$ fits. **(B)**

questions.question: Tom's normal rate of pay is \$26.40 per hour. In one week, he worked 16 hours at the normal rate, 5.5 hours at time-and-a-half, and 3 hours at double time. He also received a danger allowance of \$72 for the week. What were his total earnings for the week?
The Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) of Sydney, Australia is $+10$ hours and the UTC of Toronto, Canada is $-4$ hours. What is the local time in Toronto if it is 8 am on Monday in Sydney?
questions.answer: Toronto is $10 - (-4) = 14$ hours behind Sydney. $8$ am Monday $- 14$ h $= 6$ pm Sunday. **(B)**

questions.question: Jonah is asked to solve $\dfrac{x - 1}{2} = \dfrac{4x}{3} + 3$. Which of the following could be Jonah's next step?
questions.answer: Multiply every term by the lowest common denominator, $6$: $3(x - 1) = 2(4x) + 18$. **(C)**

questions.question: Ten students sat a practice trial examination and received the following marks: 67, 92, 68, 88, 87, 79, 91, 76, 82, 90. After further revision, the examination was repeated and each student's mark increased by 7. When comparing the second set of results with the first:
questions.answer: Adding a constant to every value shifts the mean by that constant but does not change the spread, so the mean increases by $7$ and the standard deviation stays the same. **(B)**
options: the mean had decreased by 7 and the standard deviation had remained the same.
the mean had increased by 7 and the standard deviation had remained the same.
the mean had decreased by 7 and the standard deviation had increased by 7.
the mean had increased by 7 and the standard deviation had increased by 7.

questions.question: A mountain bike course is represented by a network of tracks, where each track is modelled as an edge connecting two vertices. Due to bad weather, two tracks have been closed. After these closures, Thomas is able to cycle a route that uses each remaining track exactly once without repetition. He may start and finish at different locations. Which one of the following options does NOT allow such a route to be completed?
questions.answer:
A route using every edge exactly once exists only if the network has $0$ or $2$ vertices of odd degree. The degrees are $A = 4$, $B = 2$, $C = 3$, $D = 5$, $E = 4$, $F = 2$, $G = 4$.

- (A) $AG$, $CG$ closed: $A = 3$, $G = 2$, $C = 2$, so the odd vertices are $A$ and $D$.
- (B) $AG$, $DG$ closed: $A = 3$, $G = 2$, $D = 4$, so the odd vertices are $A$ and $C$.
- (C) $AG$, $GE$ closed: $A = 3$, $G = 2$, $E = 3$, so the odd vertices are $A$, $C$, $D$, $E$ (four odd vertices).
- (D) $CE$, $DG$ closed: $C = 2$, $E = 3$, $D = 4$, $G = 3$, so the odd vertices are $E$ and $G$.

Only (C) has four odd vertices. **(C)**

questions.question: The area of a trapezium has the formula $A = \dfrac{h}{2}(a + b)$. Make $b$ the subject of the formula.
questions.answer: $$2A = h(a + b) \Rightarrow \frac{2A}{h} = a + b \Rightarrow b = \frac{2A}{h} - a$$

questions.question: A school purchases a photocopier for \$12 000. It depreciates at a rate of 15% per annum, using the declining balance method. Calculate the value of the photocopier after 4 years.

Cohen is taking out a loan of \$60 000 at an interest rate of 8.41% per annum. The interest is calculated monthly on a reducible basis. The table shows the progress of the first three months of the loan.

| Month | Principal | Interest | Balance |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | \$60 000.00 | \$420.50 | \$59 473.02 |
| 2 | \$59 473.02 | \$416.81 | \$58 942.35 |
| 3 | \$58 942.35 | \$413.09 | \$58 407.96 |
| 4 | \$58 407.96 | $A$ | $B$ |

What is the regular monthly repayment?
questions.answer: Repayment $=$ principal $+$ interest $-$ balance $= 60\,000 + 420.50 - 59\,473.02 = \$947.48$.

questions.question: Cohen's loan of \$60 000 has an interest rate of 8.41% per annum, calculated monthly on a reducible basis, with a monthly repayment of \$947.48. In month 4 the principal is \$58 407.96, the interest is $A$ and the balance is $B$. Calculate the values of $A$ and $B$.
Cohen's loan of \$60 000 requires monthly repayments of \$947.48 and will be paid off after 84 months. How much interest will Cohen pay in this time?

A fruit punch is made by mixing orange juice, apple juice, and pineapple juice in the ratio $3 : 4 : 5$. Angus wants to make 96 litres of this fruit punch for his party. How many litres of each type of juice should he use?
questions.answer:
Total parts $= 3 + 4 + 5 = 12$, so each part is $96 \div 12 = 8$ L.

Orange: $3 \times 8 = 24$ L; apple: $4 \times 8 = 32$ L; pineapple: $5 \times 8 = 40$ L.

questions.question: Angus makes 96 litres of fruit punch using 24 L of orange juice, 32 L of apple juice and 40 L of pineapple juice. The cost per litre is \$2.50 for orange juice, \$3.00 for apple juice, and \$3.50 for pineapple juice. What is the total cost of making the fruit punch?
Jake surveyed 300 pupils to find out their daily commute time. The results were used to construct the box plot below. How many pupils have a commute time between 20 and 35 minutes?
questions.answer: The box plot has $Q_1 = 20$ and median $= 35$. The data between $Q_1$ and the median is $25\%$ of the pupils: $0.25 \times 300 = 75$ pupils.

questions.question: Ollie has bought a Toyota RAV4 Hybrid. The fuel consumption is 4.8 litres per 100 kilometres. Calculate the distance that the car can travel on a full tank of 50 litres. Give your answer correct to the nearest kilometre.
questions.answer: Distance $= \dfrac{50}{4.8} \times 100 = 1041.67 \approx 1042$ km.

questions.question: A car has a fuel consumption of 4.8 litres per 100 kilometres. Calculate the number of litres required for the car to make the journey from Sydney to Jindabyne, 458 kilometres away. Give your answer correct to the nearest litre.
questions.answer: Litres $= \dfrac{458}{100} \times 4.8 = 21.984 \approx 22$ L.

questions.question: A journey from Sydney to Jindabyne requires 22 litres of fuel. Calculate the fuel cost for the journey, based on a price of \$1.91 per litre.
questions.answer: $22 \times 1.91 = \$42.02$ (or $21.984 \times 1.91 = \$41.99$ using the unrounded amount).

prev.question: A car has a fuel consumption of 4.8 litres per 100 kilometres. Calculate the number of litres required for the car to make the journey from Sydney to Jindabyne, 458 kilometres away. Give your answer correct to the nearest litre.

questions.question: Tom purchases a gaming console for \$850, using a credit card with no annual fee. The interest rate of 18% per annum is compounded daily on the amount owing. The full amount owing was repaid 15 days later. Calculate the amount of interest charged on the purchase, assuming that interest is charged for the 15 days. Give your answer correct to the nearest cent.
questions.answer:
Amount owing after 15 days $= 850\left(1 + \dfrac{0.18}{365}\right)^{15} = \$856.31$.

Interest $= 856.31 - 850 = \$6.31$.

questions.question: Young's rule is a formula used to calculate a child's medication dosage based on age: $D = \dfrac{yA}{y + 12}$, where $D$ is the child's dosage, $y$ is the age of the child in years and $A$ is the adult dosage. Cohen is 6 years old and needs some amoxicillin, where the adult dosage is 500 mg. What should Cohen's dosage be? Give your answer correct to the nearest mg.
questions.answer: $D = \dfrac{6 \times 500}{6 + 12} = 166.7 \approx 167$ mg.

questions.question: Using Young's rule $D = \dfrac{yA}{y + 12}$, the correct dosage of loratadine for an 8 year old is 4 mg. What is the adult dosage? Give your answer correct to the nearest mg.
questions.answer: $4 = \dfrac{8A}{8 + 12} = \dfrac{8A}{20} \Rightarrow A = \dfrac{4 \times 20}{8} = 10$ mg.

questions.question: According to Young's rule $D = \dfrac{yA}{y + 12}$, if a child's dosage was $\dfrac{1}{2}$ of an adult dosage, what age would the child be?
questions.answer:
Let $A = 2$ and $D = 1$: $1 = \dfrac{2y}{y + 12} \Rightarrow y + 12 = 2y \Rightarrow y = 12$.

The child would be 12 years old.

questions.question:
The table shows the income tax rates for Australian residents for the 2024–25 financial year.

questions.answer:

questions.question: Daniel is a conservationist. He estimates the number of wombats in a reserve using the capture-recapture method. In the first capture, 80 wombats are caught, tagged, and released. A week later, a second capture of 100 wombats is made, and 20 of them are found to be tagged. Estimate the total number of wombats in the reserve.
questions.answer: Let $x$ be the total population. The proportion tagged is the same in the sample and the population: $\dfrac{80}{x} = \dfrac{20}{100} \Rightarrow x = 80 \times \dfrac{100}{20} = 400$ wombats.

questions.question: Daniel estimates the number of wombats in a reserve using the capture-recapture method. Explain one assumption that must be made for this estimate to be valid.
questions.answer: Either: the capture is random, so every wombat has an equal chance of being selected; or the reserve is a closed population, so wombats cannot enter or leave (and none are born or die) between the two captures.

Is 75 minutes an outlier? Justify your answer with calculations.
questions.answer:
There are 13 values. The median is the 7th value, $34$. $Q_1 = \dfrac{28 + 30}{2} = 29$ and $Q_3 = \dfrac{45 + 49}{2} = 47$, so $\text{IQR} = 47 - 29 = 18$.

questions.question: Angus's exercise times include an outlier at 75 minutes. Which is the better measure of spread for this data set, the interquartile range (IQR) or the standard deviation? Justify your answer.

questions.question: Cohen has a bag containing 4 red and 6 black marbles. Two marbles are selected at random without replacement. A partially completed tree diagram is shown below (the branch from black to black is already marked $\frac{5}{9}$). Complete the tree diagram by including the missing probabilities. Calculate the probability of choosing at least 1 black marble.
questions.answer:
First marble: $P(R) = \frac{4}{10}$, $P(B) = \frac{6}{10}$. Second marble: after R, $P(R) = \frac{3}{9}$, $P(B) = \frac{6}{9}$; after B, $P(R) = \frac{4}{9}$, $P(B) = \frac{5}{9}$.

$$P(\text{at least 1 black}) = 1 - P(\text{no black}) = 1 - \frac{4}{10} \times \frac{3}{9} = 1 - \frac{2}{15} = \frac{13}{15}$$

questions.question: The time $T$ (in hours) it takes to paint a big fence varies inversely with the number of workers $W$ painting. If it takes 4 workers 3 hours to paint the fence, how long would it take 6 workers?
questions.answer:
$T = \dfrac{k}{W}$, so $k = WT = 4 \times 3 = 12$ and $T = \dfrac{12}{W}$.

With $6$ workers: $T = \dfrac{12}{6} = 2$ hours.

questions.answer: $0.5 = \dfrac{12}{W} \Rightarrow W = 24$ workers.

questions.question: Jake always records the time he takes to run 10 km. His times follow a normal distribution, with a mean of 52 minutes and a standard deviation of 4 minutes. What is the probability that Jake completes the run between 48 and 60 minutes?

questions.answer:
The fastest $2.5\%$ of times are those more than $2$ standard deviations below the mean (the empirical rule leaves $2.5\%$ in each tail beyond $z = \pm 2$).

$52 - 2 \times 4 = 44$ minutes.

questions.question: Tom is a surveyor. He stands at a fixed point $O$ and records the position of three boundary markers using bearings and distances: $P$ is 12 m from $O$ on a bearing of 020°, $Q$ is 9 m from $O$ on a bearing of 120°, and $R$ is 15 m from $O$ on a bearing of 240°. Find the area of $\triangle POQ$. Give your answer correct to 1 decimal place.
questions.answer:
$\angle POQ = 120^\circ - 20^\circ = 100^\circ$.

$A = \tfrac{1}{2}(12)(9)\sin 100^\circ = 53.2\ \text{m}^2$.

questions.question: Tom is a surveyor standing at $O$. $Q$ is 9 m from $O$ on a bearing of 120° and $R$ is 15 m from $O$ on a bearing of 240°. Find the bearing of $Q$ from $R$.
questions.answer:
$\angle QOR = 240^\circ - 120^\circ = 120^\circ$.

Cosine rule: $QR^2 = 9^2 + 15^2 - 2(9)(15)\cos 120^\circ = 441 \Rightarrow QR = 21$ m.

Sine rule: $\dfrac{\sin\theta}{9} = \dfrac{\sin 120^\circ}{21} \Rightarrow \theta = \sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{9\sin 120^\circ}{21}\right) = 21.8^\circ$, where $\theta = \angle ORQ$.

$R$ is at $240^\circ$ from $O$, so $O$ is on a bearing of $240^\circ - 180^\circ = 060^\circ$ from $R$ (that is, $\angle NRO = 60^\circ$). $Q$ lies a further $21.8^\circ$ clockwise from $O$, so the bearing of $Q$ from $R$ is $60^\circ + 21.8^\circ = 081.8^\circ \approx 082^\circ$ T.

questions.answer: $$5200 = 9800(1 - r)^4 \Rightarrow 1 - r = \sqrt[4]{\frac{5200}{9800}} \approx 0.853 \Rightarrow r \approx 15\% \quad \textbf{(A)}$$

questions.question: A group of 32 farmers can harvest crops in 15 days. The number of days varies inversely with the number of farmers working at a constant rate. How long would it take a group of 8 farmers to complete the same task?
questions.answer: $d = \dfrac{k}{F}$ with $k = 32 \times 15 = 480$, so $d = \dfrac{480}{8} = 60$ days. **(C)**

questions.question: Below shows a cumulative frequency histogram of the ages of 30 students. What is approximately the median age of the students?

questions.question: The marks in a test were normally distributed. The mean mark was 56 and the standard deviation was 12. What was the percentage of marks higher than 80?
questions.answer: $z = \dfrac{80 - 56}{12} = 2$. About 95% lie within 2 standard deviations, so $\frac{5\%}{2} = 2.5\%$ lie above. **(A)**

options: The Firenze would use the least fuel.

The Firenze and the Vortex are equal in using the least amount of fuel.

$$270^\circ - 110^\circ = 160^\circ$$

questions.question:
Kara is training for the swim leg of a triathlon and decides to go for a training swim in the harbour. She starts at a jetty $J$ and swims on a bearing of 105° for 0.9 km out to a buoy $L$. She then changes direction and swims on a bearing of 045° for a further 1.6 km to buoy $M$ before returning to the jetty $J$.

What is the total distance that Kara swam, correct to 2 decimal places?
questions.answer:
At $L$, the bearing back to $J$ is $285^\circ$ and the new bearing is $045^\circ$, so $\angle JLM = 285^\circ - 45^\circ = 240^\circ$ reflex, i.e. $120^\circ$ inside the triangle.
$$JM^2 = 0.9^2 + 1.6^2 - 2(0.9)(1.6)\cos 120^\circ = 4.81 \Rightarrow JM \approx 2.193\text{ km}$$
$$\text{Total} = 0.9 + 1.6 + 2.193 \approx 4.69\text{ km}$$
(The school's sheet gives no worked answer for this part.)

questions.question:
Kara is training for the swim leg of a triathlon and decides to go for a training swim in the harbour. She starts at a jetty $J$ and swims on a bearing of 105° for 0.9 km out to a buoy $L$. She then changes direction and swims on a bearing of 045° for a further 1.6 km to buoy $M$ before returning to the jetty $J$.

Find the bearing of the jetty $J$ from the buoy $M$ to the nearest degree. ($JM \approx 2.193$ km.)
questions.answer:
$$\frac{\sin\angle JML}{0.9} = \frac{\sin 120^\circ}{2.193} \Rightarrow \angle JML \approx 20.8^\circ$$
The bearing of $L$ from $M$ is $045^\circ + 180^\circ = 225^\circ$, and $J$ is $20.8^\circ$ further clockwise:
$$225^\circ + 20.8^\circ \approx 246^\circ$$

*Note: the school's solution uses 4.96 km for $JM$ and gets $234^\circ$; with the correct $JM \approx 2.19$ km the bearing is $246^\circ$.*

Michael wishes to buy a used car that has a sale price of \$19 820. In addition to the sale price, the following costs are charged:

- Stamp duty, which is calculated at \$3 for every \$100, or part thereof, of the sale price.

Michael borrows the total amount to be paid for the car, including transfer of registration and stamp duty. Simple interest at the rate of 6.3% per annum is charged on the loan. The loan is to be repaid in equal monthly repayments over 4 years.

Calculate Michael's monthly repayment.
questions.answer:
- Stamp duty: \$19 820 is 199 lots of \$100 or part, so $199 \times 3 = \$597$
- Amount borrowed: $19\,820 + 50 + 597 = \$20\,467$
- Interest: $20\,467 \times 0.063 \times 4 \approx \$5157.68$
- Total to repay: $\$25\,624.68$

$$\text{Monthly repayment} = \frac{25\,624.68}{48} \approx \$533.85$$

questions.question:
A company is designing a water bottle with the shape below as its cross-section. It consists of an isosceles triangle with a base 10 cm and a semicircle with a diameter that fits perfectly to one equal side of the isosceles triangle. The area of the triangle is 60 cm².

If the bottle is to have a depth of 25 cm, calculate the volume of the bottle to two decimal places.
questions.answer:
Triangle height: $60 = \frac12 \times 10 \times h \Rightarrow h = 12$ cm.

Equal side (the semicircle's diameter): $\sqrt{5^2 + 12^2} = 13$ cm, so the radius is 6.5 cm.
$$A = 60 + \tfrac12\pi(6.5)^2 \approx 126.366\text{ cm}^2$$
$$V = 126.366 \times 25 \approx 3159.15\text{ cm}^3$$

questions.question:
In a flock of 22 400 sheep, the ratio of males to females is $9 : 15$. The weights of the female sheep are normally distributed with a mean of 78.4 kg and a standard deviation of 5.6 kg. In the flock, 13 979 of the female sheep each weigh more than $x$ kg.

Find the value of $x$.
questions.answer:
Females: $\dfrac{15}{24} \times 22\,400 = 14\,000$.

$\dfrac{13\,979}{14\,000} \approx 99.85\%$ weigh more than $x$, so $0.15\%$ weigh less. By the empirical rule that is $z = -3$.
$$x = 78.4 - 3 \times 5.6 = 61.6\text{ kg}$$

questions.question: Stanley wants to know the present value of an investment which will earn 3% per annum, compounded monthly. In ten years' time, the future value will be \$5000. Which calculation will result in the correct answer?

questions.question:
Consider the network diagram.

Which of the following is true?
questions.answer:
Degrees: $a = 3$, $b = 3$, $c = 4$, $d = 2$, $e = 4$, so exactly two vertices ($a$ and $b$) are odd.

With exactly two odd vertices, a trail using every edge once exists (starting at $a$ and ending at $b$), but a circuit does not: that needs every vertex to be even. **(A)**

*Note: the school's solutions give (C), but a circuit using every edge once is impossible when any vertex has odd degree.*
options: A trail that uses every edge of the network only once exists because the network contains exactly two odd vertices.
A trail that uses every edge of the network only once exists because the network contains at least two odd vertices.
A circuit that uses every edge of the network only once exists because the network contains exactly two odd vertices.
A circuit that uses every edge of the network only once exists because the network contains at least two odd vertices.

Make $x$ the subject of the formula below, leaving your answer as a simplified fraction.
$$\frac{x + y}{y} = \frac{y}{a} + \frac{a}{y}$$
questions.answer:
Multiply both sides by $y$:
$$x + y = \frac{y^2}{a} + a \Rightarrow x = \frac{y^2}{a} + a - y = \frac{y^2 + a^2 - ay}{a}$$

questions.answer: A straight line from $(0, 100)$ with gradient 25, e.g. through $(20, 600)$ and $(40, 1100)$.

questions.question:
Riley has \$100. He starts to save \$25 each week to buy a new racing bike. His savings can be modelled by $S = 100 + 25t$, where $S$ is the dollars saved and $t$ is the time in weeks from when he started saving money.

Amelia, Riley's sister, wanted to start saving 8 weeks after Riley began saving. She initially had no money, but saves \$40 per week.

By drawing a line on the grid above, or otherwise, find the value of $t$ when the siblings have the same amount of money.
questions.answer:
Amelia: $S = 40(t - 8) = 40t - 320$ (a line from $(8, 0)$).
$$100 + 25t = 40t - 320 \Rightarrow 15t = 420 \Rightarrow t = 28\text{ weeks}$$

questions.question:

questions.question:

questions.answer:
Right of the dotted line, use three strips of height 43 m with widths 82, 87, 89 and 99 m:
$$\frac{43}{2}(82 + 87) + \frac{43}{2}(87 + 89) + \frac{43}{2}(89 + 99) = 3633.5 + 3784 + 4042 = 11\,459.5\text{ m}^2$$
Left of the dotted line is a right triangle with base 41 m and height $3 \times 43 = 129$ m:
$$\tfrac12 \times 41 \times 129 = 2644.5\text{ m}^2$$

Draw a diagram to represent this information.
questions.answer: $AB = 7$ km at $050^\circ$, then $BC = 8$ km at $120^\circ$. At $B$ the back bearing to $A$ is $230^\circ$, so $\angle ABC = 230^\circ - 120^\circ = 110^\circ$.

Find the distance from point $C$ to point $A$, to one decimal place.
questions.answer: $$AC^2 = 7^2 + 8^2 - 2(7)(8)\cos 110^\circ \approx 151.31 \Rightarrow AC \approx 12.3\text{ km}$$

questions.question:

What is the bearing of $C$ from $A$?
questions.answer:
$$\frac{\sin \angle BAC}{8} = \frac{\sin 110^\circ}{12.30} \Rightarrow \angle BAC \approx 37.7^\circ$$
Bearing $= 50^\circ + 37.7^\circ \approx 088^\circ$.

questions.question: If $m$ is inversely proportional to $n$, and $m = 10$ when $n = 25$, find $k$, the constant of proportionality.
questions.answer: $m = \dfrac{k}{n} \Rightarrow 10 = \dfrac{k}{25} \Rightarrow k = 250$

questions.answer: $50 = \dfrac{250}{n} \Rightarrow n = 5$

The basal metabolic rate (BMR) of a person refers to the minimum amount of energy (in kilojoules) needed to sustain basic bodily functions (that is, to keep the person alive) for a 24-hour period.

The energy output needed is then given by:
$$\text{Energy out} = \text{BMR} \times \text{physical activity level (PAL)}$$

The Harris–Benedict model can be used to estimate BMR, in kJ/day. It is given by:
- $\text{BMR}_{\text{male}} = 278 + 57.5W + 20.9H - 28.2A$
- $\text{BMR}_{\text{female}} = 278 + 40.0W + 7.7H - 19.6A$

where $W$ is weight (in kg), $H$ is height (in cm) and $A$ is age (in years).

A 25-year-old woman weighs 62 kg and she has a height of 159 cm. Use the Harris–Benedict model to estimate the woman's BMR, to the nearest kJ/day.

By using graphical means, or otherwise, find and label the point of intersection of $x + 3y = 1$ and $y = 2x + 5$.
questions.answer:
Substitute $y = 2x + 5$:
$$x + 3(2x + 5) = 1 \Rightarrow 7x = -14 \Rightarrow x = -2, \quad y = 1$$
The lines intersect at $(-2, 1)$.

questions.question:
Ingrid lives in Spain, located at (50°N, 1°E). She is trading in US stocks with her broker in New York, which is located at (40°N, 74°W).

The New York stock exchange closes at 4:30 pm New York time. What is the latest time and day, in Spain, that Ingrid can place an order through her broker?

Note: You may use the fact that 15° = 1 hour time difference. Ignore daylight saving.
questions.answer:
Longitude difference $= 74^\circ + 1^\circ = 75^\circ$, i.e. $75 \div 15 = 5$ hours. Spain is east, so it is ahead.

4:30 pm + 5 h $=$ **9:30 pm on the same day**.

questions.question:
Hebe owns a chicken enclosure in the shape of a right-angled triangle. The hypotenuse of the triangle is given by $x$, and its two other sides have lengths 1.8 m and 2 m.

Hebe wants to give the chickens more space to roam by removing the fence that forms the hypotenuse of the right-angled triangle, $AC$, and adding a new triangular section to the enclosure, as shown in the diagram.

Find the area of the new triangular section, $\triangle ACD$, of the enclosure and the lengths of the fencing $AC$ and $DC$, in metres. Give your answers correct to three decimal places.
questions.answer:
**$AC$** (Pythagoras): $x = \sqrt{1.8^2 + 2^2} = \sqrt{7.24} \approx 2.691$ m.

**$DC$**: in $\triangle ACD$, $\angle D = 180^\circ - 52^\circ - 74^\circ = 54^\circ$. By the sine rule:
$$\frac{DC}{\sin 52^\circ} = \frac{\sqrt{7.24}}{\sin 54^\circ} \Rightarrow DC \approx 2.621\text{ m}$$

**Area:**
$$A = \tfrac12 \times AC \times DC \times \sin 74^\circ = \tfrac12(2.6907)(2.6209)\sin 74^\circ \approx 3.389\text{ m}^2$$

Sasa opened an account and deposited \$15 000 at the end of each year for 6 years. At the end of the 7th year, he deposited \$20 000 in the same account and continued to deposit \$20 000 at the end of each year until the end of the 10th year. He made no more deposits after the 10th year.

The money in his account was earning interest at 2.5% per annum, compounded annually.

How much money will Sasa have in his account at the end of 15 years?
questions.answer:
**\$15 000 deposits** (6 years, 2.5%): $15\,000 \times 6.38774 = \$95\,816.10$ at the end of year 6, which then grows for 9 years:
$$95\,816.10 \times 1.025^9 \approx \$119\,661.18$$

A thin pole stands vertically in the middle of a level playing ground. From point $A$ on the ground, the angle of elevation to the top of the pole, $T$, is 18°. From point $B$, also on the ground but 5.35 metres further from the foot of the pole than $A$, the angle of elevation to the top of the pole is 15°.

Draw a sketch to represent this information.
questions.answer: A right triangle with the pole (height $y$) on one side; $A$ and $B$ on the ground, $B$ 5.35 m further out. The angles of elevation are $18^\circ$ at $A$ and $15^\circ$ at $B$, so $\angle BAT = 162^\circ$ and $\angle ATB = 3^\circ$.

questions.question:
A thin pole stands vertically in the middle of a level playing ground. From point $A$ on the ground, the angle of elevation to the top of the pole, $T$, is 18°. From point $B$, also on the ground but 5.35 metres further from the foot of the pole than $A$, the angle of elevation to the top of the pole is 15°.

Determine the height of the pole.
questions.answer:
In $\triangle ABT$: $\angle BAT = 180^\circ - 18^\circ = 162^\circ$ and $\angle ATB = 18^\circ - 15^\circ = 3^\circ$.
$$\frac{BT}{\sin 162^\circ} = \frac{5.35}{\sin 3^\circ} \Rightarrow BT \approx 31.58\text{ m}$$
$$y = 31.58 \sin 15^\circ \approx 8.18\text{ m}$$

|---|---|
| Straight line depreciation | \$4000 per annum |
| Declining-balance depreciation | 10% p.a. |

Under which method of depreciation would the salvage value of the equipment be lower at the end of 5 years? Justify your answer with appropriate mathematical calculations.
questions.answer:
- Straight line: $S = 55\,000 - 4000 \times 5 = \$35\,000$
- Declining balance: $S = 55\,000(0.9)^5 \approx \$32\,476.95$

The **declining-balance** method gives the lower salvage value.

State, with justification, which of the three random variables has the largest mean.
questions.answer: **$Y$**: its curve is centred furthest to the right (the peak of a normal curve is at the mean).

State, with justification, which of the three random variables has the smallest standard deviation.
questions.answer: **$X$**: its curve is the tallest and narrowest, so its data is least spread out.

questions.question: Is this graph Eulerian? Justify your answer with mathematical reasoning.
questions.answer:
Degrees: top-left vertex 1, middle-left vertex 4, top-middle vertex 3 (straight edge, arc and edge to the right), right vertex 2, bottom-middle vertex 2, bottom-left vertex 2.

Exactly two vertices (top-left and top-middle) have odd degree. So the graph has an **Euler trail** (starting at one odd vertex and finishing at the other) and is semi-Eulerian, but it is **not Eulerian**: an Euler circuit needs every vertex to have even degree.

*Note: the school's solution says "2 odd vertices, therefore Eulerian", which describes an Euler trail rather than an Euler circuit.*

questions.question:
The weights of students in a class were recorded. The results for this class are displayed in the cumulative frequency graph shown (25 students).

The lightest student in the class weighed 40 kg and the heaviest in the class weighed 90 kg.

Construct a box-plot for this class, using a number line.
questions.answer:
With 25 students, read across from cumulative frequencies of about 6.25 ($Q_1$), 12.5 (median) and 18.75 ($Q_3$) to the ogive, then down to the weight axis.

Five-number summary (approximately): min 40, $Q_1 \approx 51$, median $\approx 60$, $Q_3 \approx 67$, max 90. Draw whiskers from 40 to $Q_1$ and from $Q_3$ to 90, with a box from $Q_1$ to $Q_3$ split at the median.

(The school's solution reads $Q_1 = 54$, median $= 61$ and $Q_3 = 66$; values read from a graph will vary slightly.)

questions.question:
A bag contains 4 red balls and 5 black balls. Two balls are selected at random without replacement. A partially completed tree diagram is shown below.

Complete the probability tree diagram and calculate the probability of selecting two balls of the same colour.
questions.answer:
- First selection: $P(R) = \frac49$, $P(B) = \frac59$
- After $R$: $P(R) = \frac38$, $P(B) = \frac58$
- After $B$: $P(R) = \frac48$, $P(B) = \frac48$

$$P(\text{same}) = \frac49 \times \frac38 + \frac59 \times \frac48 = \frac{12}{72} + \frac{20}{72} = \frac49$$

questions.question:
Sonya and James each invest \$2000 for 10 years.
- Sonya's investment earns simple interest at a rate of 5.5% per annum.
- James' investment earns an interest rate of 4.5% per annum, compounding quarterly.

By calculating the interest earned over the 10 years, determine who will have the greater amount.
questions.answer:
- Sonya: $I = 2000 \times 0.055 \times 10 = \$1100$
- James: $FV = 2000\left(1 + \frac{0.045}{4}\right)^{40} \approx \$3128.75$, so $I = \$1128.75$

**James** will have the greater amount.

Calculate the temperature of the soup after 2.5 minutes.

A bowl of hot soup is cooling on a table. Its temperature, $T$°C, after $t$ minutes is given by the formula $T = 100(1.075)^{-t}$.

What is the vertical intercept of this function and what does it represent?
questions.answer: At $t = 0$: $T = 100(1.075)^0 = 100$. The intercept is 100°C, the temperature of the soup at the start.

questions.question: Jack and Jill are going to the beach 5 km away. Jill will ride her bike at 12 km/h while Jack will jog at 8 km/h. How much head start should Jill give Jack so that they arrive at the beach at the same time?
questions.answer:
- Jack: $t = \frac58 = 0.625$ h $= 37.5$ min
- Jill: $t = \frac{5}{12} \approx 0.4167$ h $= 25$ min

Head start $= 37.5 - 25 = 12.5$ minutes.

questions.question:
The following formula can be used to calculate an estimate for blood alcohol content (BAC) for females.
$$BAC_{\text{female}} = \frac{10N - 7.5H}{5.5M}$$
where $N$ is the number of standard drinks consumed, $H$ is the number of hours drinking and $M$ is the person's weight in kilograms.

Samantha weighs 65 kg. Her BAC was zero when she began drinking alcohol. At 10:00 pm, after consuming 4 standard drinks, her BAC was 0.04.

Using the formula, estimate at what time Samantha began drinking alcohol, to the nearest minute.
questions.answer:
$$0.04 = \frac{10(4) - 7.5H}{5.5(65)} \Rightarrow 14.3 = 40 - 7.5H \Rightarrow H \approx 3.4267\text{ h} \approx 3\text{ h }26\text{ min}$$
10:00 pm − 3 h 26 min $=$ **6:34 pm**.

questions.question: Use forward and backward scanning to identify the critical path. (Activities: $A$ 7, $B$ 1, $C$ 5, $D$ 2, $E$ 4, $F$ 5, $G$ 1, $H$ 1.)
questions.answer:
Forward scan: 0, 7, 8, 10 (after $D$), 12 (after $E$), 15 (after $F$), 16 (finish). The backward scan gives the same latest times along $A$–$B$–$D$–$F$–$H$.

Critical path: **A, B, D, F, H** (16).

questions.question: The marks, $x$, obtained by students in a maths exam were normally distributed with a mean of 85 and a standard deviation of 4. If the top 2.5% of students received an A, what was the minimum score to achieve an A?
questions.answer: The top 2.5% is $z > 2$: $x = 85 + 2 \times 4 = 93$.

questions.question:
A cake is created using a cylinder and a hemisphere shaped top. The cylinder has a height of 10 cm and the hemisphere has a radius of 7 cm.

Calculate the surface area of the cake that is to be covered in icing (not including the base), correct to the nearest cm².
questions.answer:
Curved surface of the cylinder plus the hemisphere:
$$SA = 2\pi rh + 2\pi r^2 = 2\pi(7)(10) + 2\pi(7)^2 \approx 439.82 + 307.88 \approx 748\text{ cm}^2$$

questions.question: An oil tanker hits a reef in the Pacific ocean and releases oil from its reservoirs. The oil slick extends 10 km NE from the tanker and from the air can be seen to turn to a bearing of 158° for 25 km, then back to the tanker. Calculate the area of the oil slick.
questions.answer:
The first leg is on a bearing of $045^\circ$. At the turn, the angle between the back bearing ($225^\circ$) and $158^\circ$ is $225^\circ - 158^\circ = 67^\circ$ (equivalently $180^\circ - 45^\circ - (158^\circ - 90^\circ)$).
$$A = \tfrac12 \times 10 \times 25 \times \sin 67^\circ \approx 115.06\text{ km}^2$$

questions.question: A full container has 5.2 L of a mixture of cordial and water in the ratio $1 : 3$. After removing 1.6 L of the mixture, more water is added to refill the container. What is the ratio of cordial to water in the final mixture?
questions.answer:
Remaining mixture: $5.2 - 1.6 = 3.6$ L, i.e. 0.9 L cordial and 2.7 L water.

Add 1.6 L water: $0.9 : 4.3 = 9 : 43$.

questions.answer: The lines $R = 10n$ and $C = 4n + 420$ meet at $(70, 700)$: this is the **break-even point**. Selling 70 masks brings in \$700, exactly covering costs.

questions.question: A soccer goal is 8 m wide. A player shoots for goal when he is 20 m from one post and 15 m from the other post. Within what angle must the shot be made to score a goal?
questions.answer: $$\cos\theta = \frac{20^2 + 15^2 - 8^2}{2 \times 20 \times 15} = \frac{561}{600} = 0.935 \Rightarrow \theta \approx 20.77^\circ$$

|---|---|

| \$18 201 – \$45 000 | 16c for each \$1 over \$18 200 |
| \$45 001 – \$135 000 | \$4288 plus 30c for each \$1 over \$45 000 |
| \$135 001 – \$190 000 | \$31 288 plus 37c for each \$1 over \$135 000 |
| \$190 001 and over | \$51 638 plus 45c for each \$1 over \$190 000 |

At the end of the 2025 – 2026 financial year, Kale's tax payable was \$154 536, excluding the Medicare levy. What was Kale's taxable income?
questions.answer:
That much tax is only possible in the top bracket:
$$154\,536 = 51\,638 + 0.45(x - 190\,000) \Rightarrow x - 190\,000 = \frac{102\,898}{0.45} \approx 228\,662.22$$
$$x \approx \$418\,662.22$$

questions.question: Sam believes he did better on his Math exam than his Physics exam. The Physics exam had a mean score of 55 and a standard deviation of 17 and he achieved 67 out of 100. On the Math exam, he achieved 72 out of 100 and the class had a mean of 64 and a standard deviation of 12. Evaluate the reasonableness of Sam's statement, using mathematical reasoning.
questions.answer:
$$z_{\text{physics}} = \frac{67 - 55}{17} \approx 0.71, \qquad z_{\text{math}} = \frac{72 - 64}{12} \approx 0.67$$
Sam is **not** correct: relative to the class he did slightly better in Physics.

questions.question: A plumber needs to fix a system of pipes from source $S$ to sink $t$ (network shown). The plumber experienced difficulty in cutting the pipes and wants to identify the smallest cut possible (in terms of capacity). By finding the maximum flow, explain why this is the smallest cut possible. Justify your response on the diagram below.
questions.answer:
Pushing flow along augmenting paths saturates the pipes $3$, $2$, $2$ and $5$ shown in the solution, giving a maximum flow of 12. The cut through these saturated pipes has capacity
$$3 + 2 + 2 + 5 = 12.$$
By the maximum-flow minimum-cut theorem, no cut can be smaller than the maximum flow, so this is the minimum cut. (It passes only through saturated pipes, or pipes flowing back towards the source.)

Carmine has a credit card which has no interest-free period. Interest is charged at 19.5% per annum, compounding daily, on the amount owing.

At the start of the month Carmine had an opening balance of \$162, and during the month Carmine used his credit card to purchase a phone for \$700.

He was charged interest on the opening balance for 30 days and on the purchase of the phone for 24 days.

How much interest was Carmine charged for the month?
questions.answer:
Daily rate $= \dfrac{0.195}{365}$.
$$I = 162\left[\left(1 + \tfrac{0.195}{365}\right)^{30} - 1\right] + 700\left[\left(1 + \tfrac{0.195}{365}\right)^{24} - 1\right] \approx 2.62 + 9.03 = \$11.65. \quad \textbf{(A)}$$

questions.answer: In winter Perth is $13 - 8 = 5$ hours behind New Zealand: 6:30 pm $-$ 5 h $=$ 1:30 pm. **(A)**

questions.question:
A ball is shot vertically into the air from the ground. The height of the ball above the ground, $h$ metres, can be modelled using the function $h = 20t - 5t^2$, where $t$ is measured in seconds. The graph of the height of the ball during its flight time is shown below.

For how many seconds is the height of the ball at least half its maximum height?
questions.answer:
The maximum is at $t = 2$ (the axis of symmetry, halfway between the zeros $t = 0$ and $t = 4$): $h = 40 - 20 = 20$ m.

Half the maximum is 10 m: $20t - 5t^2 = 10 \Rightarrow t^2 - 4t + 2 = 0 \Rightarrow t = 2 \pm \sqrt2$.

Time at or above 10 m $= (2 + \sqrt2) - (2 - \sqrt2) = 2\sqrt2 \approx 2.8$ s. **(C)**

questions.question:
Box A contains 3 red balls and 2 white balls while box B contains 6 red balls and 1 white ball.

John draws a ball randomly from box A and then puts it into box B. If John draws a ball randomly from box B afterwards, what is the probability that John draws a red ball?
questions.answer:
Box B then holds 8 balls.
- Red moved ($\frac35$): B has 7 red, $P(\text{red}) = \frac78$.
- White moved ($\frac25$): B has 6 red, $P(\text{red}) = \frac68$.

$$P(\text{red}) = \frac35 \times \frac78 + \frac25 \times \frac68 = \frac{21}{40} + \frac{12}{40} = \frac{33}{40}. \quad \textbf{(C)}$$

A company hires electric bicycles to tourists. Company A charges according to $C = 24h + 18$, where $C$ is the total cost (dollars) and $h$ is the number of hours hired. The graph for Company B passes through the points $(0, 42)$ and $(6, 150)$.

Determine the equation representing Company B.
questions.answer:
Gradient $= \dfrac{150 - 42}{6 - 0} = 18$, intercept 42:
$$C = 18h + 42$$

questions.question: On the Cartesian plane above, graph the equation representing Company B.
questions.answer: Draw the straight line through $(0, 42)$ and $(6, 150)$. It meets Company A's line at $(4, 114)$.

questions.question: Using the graph, or otherwise, determine the number of hours for which the two companies charge the same amount.
questions.answer:
$$24h + 18 = 18h + 42 \Rightarrow 6h = 24 \Rightarrow h = 4\text{ hours}$$
(Both charge \$114.)

questions.question: A family plans to hire bicycles for 7 hours. Which company should they choose? Justify your answer using calculations.
questions.answer:
- Company A: $C = 24(7) + 18 = \$186$
- Company B: $C = 18(7) + 42 = \$168$

They should choose **Company B**, which is \$18 cheaper.

questions.question:

Determine the maximum number of full bottles that can be filled.
questions.answer:
Water is 3 parts, so 1 part $= 150$ L and the batch is $10 \times 150 = 1500$ L $= 1\,500\,000$ mL.
$$\frac{1\,500\,000}{600} = 2500\text{ bottles}$$

- Small arc (diameter 5 cm, radius 2.5 cm): $\frac12 \times 2\pi \times 2.5 = 2.5\pi$

questions.answer:
The cross-section is a regular pentagon: 5 congruent triangles with two sides of 10 cm and an included angle of $\frac{360^\circ}{5} = 72^\circ$.
$$A = 5 \times \tfrac12 \times 10 \times 10 \times \sin 72^\circ \approx 237.7641\text{ cm}^2$$

$1\text{ cm}^3 = 1000\text{ mm}^3$, so $V \approx 1\,902\,113.03\text{ mm}^3$.

questions.question:
Two hundred tickets are sold in a raffle in which there are two prizes. Amanda purchased five tickets in the raffle. The first ticket drawn wins the first prize, while the second ticket drawn wins the second prize.

Complete the tree diagram by including the missing probabilities. Calculate the probability that Amanda wins at least one of the prizes.
questions.answer:
Tree diagram ($W$ = Amanda wins, $\overline{W}$ = does not win):
- First prize: $P(W) = \frac{5}{200}$, $P(\overline{W}) = \frac{195}{200}$
- After $W$: $P(W) = \frac{4}{199}$, $P(\overline{W}) = \frac{195}{199}$
- After $\overline{W}$: $P(W) = \frac{5}{199}$, $P(\overline{W}) = \frac{194}{199}$

$$P(\text{at least one}) = 1 - P(\overline{W}\,\overline{W}) = 1 - \frac{195}{200} \times \frac{194}{199} = \frac{197}{3980} \approx 0.0495$$

questions.question:
The diagram below shows the location of three cities and the airline routes connecting them.

City $H$ is 860 km from city $G$ on a bearing of $110^\circ$. City $F$ is 730 km due south of city $G$.

Find the distance, correct to the nearest km, and the bearing, correct to the nearest degree, of city $F$ from city $H$.
questions.answer:
$\angle FGH = 180^\circ - 110^\circ = 70^\circ$.

**Distance** (cosine rule):
$$FH^2 = 860^2 + 730^2 - 2(860)(730)\cos 70^\circ \approx 843\,059 \Rightarrow FH \approx 918\text{ km}$$

**Angle at $H$** (sine rule):
$$\frac{\sin \angle GHF}{730} = \frac{\sin 70^\circ}{918.18} \Rightarrow \angle GHF \approx 48.3^\circ$$

**Bearing:** the bearing of $G$ from $H$ is $110^\circ + 180^\circ = 290^\circ$. $F$ is $48.3^\circ$ anticlockwise from that direction:
$$290^\circ - 48.3^\circ \approx 242^\circ$$

$F$ is about **918 km from $H$ on a bearing of $242^\circ$**.

Find the durations (in days) for activities F and G. Include a network diagram in your answer.
questions.answer:
Network: Start $\to$ A, B; A $\to$ C, E; B $\to$ D; D $\to$ E, G; C, E $\to$ F; F, G $\to$ H $\to$ Finish.

Critical path B–D–E–F–H: $6 + 9 + 7 + F + 4 = 32 \Rightarrow F = 6$.

Find the range of durations possible for activities A and C, assuming whole number durations.
questions.answer:
F starts on day $15 + 7 = 22$. C has 4 days of float, so $A + C + 4 = 22 \Rightarrow A + C = 18$.

A is not critical, so A must finish before E's earliest start of day 15: $A \le 14$. Every duration is at least 1 day.

So $1 \le A \le 14$ and $C = 18 - A$, giving $4 \le C \le 17$.

questions.answer:
$(0.65 - 0.57) \times 3543 \approx 283$. **(B)**

questions.question: When properly managed, cotton plant height is normally distributed with a mean of 90 cm and a standard deviation of 12 cm. What percentage of a properly managed crop is expected to be more than 102 cm tall?
questions.answer: 102 cm is $z = 1$. 68% lie within one standard deviation, so $\frac{32\%}{2} = 16\%$ lie above. **(A)**

questions.question: Terry and Kris are selling lemonade for \$2 a cup. Their parents are requiring them to pay them back \$10 for the cost of lemons. The following graph shows their profit based on the number of cups sold. What is the value and meaning of the gradient of this graph?
questions.answer: The line rises from $-10$ at 0 cups to 0 at 5 cups: $m = \frac{10}{5} = 2$, the profit per cup. **(A)**
options: $m = 2$, 2 dollars profit for each cup sold
$m = 5$, 5 dollars profit for each cup sold

questions.question:

Calculate the fortnightly cost of water for a family who washes two loads a day. Correct your answer to the nearest cent.
questions.answer:
$2 \times 50 = 100$ L per day, so $14 \times 100 = 1400$ L $= 1.4$ kL per fortnight.
$$1.4 \times 3.17 \approx \$4.44$$

A teacher was exploring the relationship between students' homework completion and their marks in the Half Yearly Examination. The data for seventeen students is shown on the graph (homework completed (%) against Half Yearly mark), with the least-squares regression line. The line passes through $(0, 10)$. The student who received a Half Yearly mark of 45, and completed 80% of their homework, lies exactly on the least-squares regression line.

What is the equation of the least-squares regression line for this data set?
questions.answer:
Through $(0, 10)$ and $(45, 80)$: $m = \frac{80 - 10}{45} = \frac{14}{9}$.
$$\text{Homework (\%)} = \frac{14}{9} \times \text{Mark} + 10$$

questions.question:
A teacher was exploring the relationship between students' homework completion and their marks in the Half Yearly Examination. The data for seventeen students is shown on the graph (homework completed (%) against Half Yearly mark), with the least-squares regression line. The line passes through $(0, 10)$. The student who received a Half Yearly mark of 45, and completed 80% of their homework, lies exactly on the least-squares regression line.

Another student, whose marks are not on the graph, completed 16 out of 20 homework assignments and scored 30 on the Half Yearly Examination. Did this student do better or worse on the test than the regression line predicts? Provide a reason for your answer.
questions.answer: $\frac{16}{20} = 80\%$ homework. The line predicts a mark of 45 for 80% homework, but this student scored 30, so they did **worse** than predicted. (The point $(30, 80)$ lies above the line.)

This represented a dividend yield of 9.8%. What was the market price of the shares in August?
questions.answer: $$0.098 = \frac{0.15}{\text{price}} \Rightarrow \text{price} = \frac{0.15}{0.098} \approx \$1.53$$

questions.question:
Keeley used her credit card to purchase a jacket for \$800 on June 8th. She made a repayment of \$400 on June 30th. She made no other purchases on her account in June.

The credit card account has no interest free period. Compound interest is charged daily at the rate of 23% per annum, including the date of purchase and the date the account is paid.

Calculate the amount Keeley owes on the credit card immediately after the \$400 payment is made, correct to the nearest cent.
questions.answer:
8 June to 30 June inclusive is 23 days.
$$800\left(1 + \frac{0.23}{365}\right)^{23} \approx \$811.68$$
After paying \$400: **\$411.68**.

questions.question:
The graphs below compare the blood pressure of two groups of volunteers in a medical study. The trial group undertook a structured program of exercise and diet, while the control group maintained their previous habits.

Compare the two data sets by examining the skewness of the distributions, and the measures of central tendency and spread.
questions.answer:
Reading the box plots: Trial group: min 102, $Q_1$ 104, median 108, $Q_3$ 116, max 135. Control group: min 102, $Q_1$ 119, median 129, $Q_3$ 131, max 135.
- **Skewness:** the trial group is positively skewed (long right whisker); the control group is negatively skewed (long left whisker).
- **Centre:** the trial group's median (about 108) is much lower than the control group's (about 129), so the program is associated with lower blood pressure.
- **Spread:** both have the same range ($135 - 102 = 33$) and the same IQR (12).

*Note: the school's sheet gives the range as 23 and the trial median as 118; the box plots show 33 and 108.*

questions.question:
Rebecca, a 75 kg human female, consumes 3 canned margarita drinks at a party over the course of 2 hours and fifteen minutes. There are 1.2 standard drinks in each can. The blood alcohol content (BAC) for human females can be estimated by
$$BAC_{\text{female}} = \frac{10N - 7.5H}{5.5M}$$
where $N$ = number of standard drinks, $H$ = number of hours drinking and $M$ = mass in kilograms.

Calculate Rebecca's BAC at the end of the party, correct to three decimal places.

Rebecca, a 75 kg human female, consumes 3 canned margarita drinks at a party over the course of 2 hours and fifteen minutes. There are 1.2 standard drinks in each can. The blood alcohol content (BAC) for human females can be estimated by
$$BAC_{\text{female}} = \frac{10N - 7.5H}{5.5M}$$
where $N$ = number of standard drinks, $H$ = number of hours drinking and $M$ = mass in kilograms.

The time it takes a person's BAC to reach zero is given by $\text{Time} = \dfrac{BAC}{0.015}$. Calculate the time it takes for Rebecca's BAC to return to zero, assuming she stopped drinking after 2 hours and fifteen minutes. Give your answer to the nearest minute.
questions.answer: $$\text{Time} = \frac{0.046}{0.015} \approx 3.07\text{ h} \approx 3\text{ hours }4\text{ minutes}$$

questions.answer:
Measure Bed 1 on the plan and compare with its real width of 2.0 m to find the scale (about 1 : 100 on the printed page), then measure Bed 2 and apply the same scale.

Bed 2 is about **1.5 m × 2.7 m**.

questions.question:
Higgins is paid \$780 for working 30 hours at the normal rate per hour. Overtime is paid for working over 30 hours. When Higgins works 40 hours, he is paid a total of \$1170.

Use calculations to show that Higgins is paid at time-and-a-half for overtime.
questions.answer:
Normal rate $= \frac{780}{30} = \$26$/h.

Overtime pay $= 1170 - 780 = \$390$ for 10 hours $= \$39$/h.

$26 \times 1.5 = 39$, so overtime is paid at time-and-a-half.

questions.question:
The figure below shows a circular dartboard with two circles sharing the same centre with radii of 12 cm and 9 cm respectively. The shaded region is the ring between the two circles. Two darts are thrown and hit the dartboard. To compare the probability of darts landing in various regions, a tree diagram is drawn, where $S$ represents the shaded area and $U$ represents the unshaded area. Assume each dart is equally likely to land on any point on the dartboard, so the probability of hitting a region depends only on its area.

Calculate each probability and complete the probability tree diagram by writing probabilities on each of the branches.
questions.answer:
Total area $= \pi(12)^2 = 144\pi$; unshaded (inner circle) $= \pi(9)^2 = 81\pi$; shaded $= 63\pi$.
$$P(U) = \frac{81}{144} = \frac{9}{16}, \qquad P(S) = \frac{63}{144} = \frac{7}{16}$$
These are the same on every branch (the darts are independent).

questions.question:
The figure below shows a circular dartboard with two circles sharing the same centre with radii of 12 cm and 9 cm respectively. The shaded region is the ring between the two circles. Two darts are thrown and hit the dartboard. To compare the probability of darts landing in various regions, a tree diagram is drawn, where $S$ represents the shaded area and $U$ represents the unshaded area. Assume each dart is equally likely to land on any point on the dartboard, so the probability of hitting a region depends only on its area.

With $P(S) = \frac{63}{144}$ and $P(U) = \frac{81}{144}$, which has a higher probability?
- both darts land in the shaded region
- only one dart lands in the shaded region

Justify your answer with calculations.
questions.answer:
$$P(SS) = \left(\frac{63}{144}\right)^2 = \frac{3969}{20\,736} \approx 0.19$$
$$P(\text{only one}) = 2 \times \frac{63}{144} \times \frac{81}{144} = \frac{10\,206}{20\,736} \approx 0.49$$
**Only one dart in the shaded region** is more likely.

questions.question:
The weekly rental on a house is shared by a number of people. The rent per person, $R$, varies inversely with the number of people living in the house, $N$. If there are 4 people living in the house, each person pays \$72.

If $R = \dfrac{k}{N}$, where $k$ is the constant of variation, find the value of $k$.
questions.answer: $72 = \frac{k}{4} \Rightarrow k = 288$

questions.question:
The weekly rental on a house is shared by a number of people. The rent per person, $R$, varies inversely with the number of people living in the house, $N$. If there are 4 people living in the house, each person pays \$72.

How much would each person pay if there were 3 people living in the house? ($k = 288$.)

How many people would need to live in the house if each person were only to pay \$48 per week? ($k = 288$.)
questions.answer: $48 = \frac{288}{N} \Rightarrow N = 6$ people

questions.question:
When the Tasmanian devil population was impacted by devil facial tumour disease (DFTD), populations declined rapidly. The graph shows the decreasing population of one population of Tasmanian devils.

This population had an initial population of 800 devils. For the first 5 years, the population declined by 30 devils per year.

At the end of the 5th year, the population ($P$) began to decline exponentially, according to the model $P = P_0(1 - r)^t$ where $P_0$ is the population on the 5th year, $t$ is the number of years after the 5th year, and $r$ is the annual rate of decline.

If the annual rate of decline after the 5th year was 20%, what was the total population after 15 years?
questions.answer:
After 5 years: $800 - 5 \times 30 = 650$.

15 years is $t = 10$ years after that:
$$P = 650(1 - 0.2)^{10} \approx 69.8 \approx 70\text{ devils}$$

questions.answer: Increase $D \to E$ from 100 to 150. $C \to D$ already brings 150 into $D$, so the flow into $E$ becomes $150 + 150 = 300$ (and $B \to C$ can carry 300).

questions.question:
According to the Australian Design Rules, for a road with a speed limit of 80 km/h, a passing lane should be 650 m long.

On a mountain pass, a road with a speed limit of 80 km/h is formed as two consecutive sectors of circles, as shown, from $C$ to $B$ to $E$. The first sector, centred at $A$, has a radius of 220 m. The second sector, centred at $D$, has a radius of 190 m. Suppose $\angle CAB = 110^\circ$ and $\angle BDE = 61^\circ$.

Is there enough space to build a passing lane on the curved road $C$-$B$-$E$? Justify your response with calculations.
questions.answer:
$$\text{Arc } CB = \frac{110}{360} \times 2\pi(220) \approx 422.37\text{ m}, \qquad \text{Arc } BE = \frac{61}{360} \times 2\pi(190) \approx 202.28\text{ m}$$
Total $\approx 624.65$ m $< 650$ m, so there is **not** enough space.

questions.question: In the diagram, $AD$ and $DC$ are both 30 cm, $\angle ADB = 60^\circ$ and $\angle BDC = 20^\circ$. Find the length of $DB$, correct to 2 decimal places.
questions.answer:
$\triangle ADC$ is isosceles with apex angle $80^\circ$, so $\angle DAB = \frac{180^\circ - 80^\circ}{2} = 50^\circ$. In $\triangle ADB$: $\angle ABD = 180^\circ - 50^\circ - 60^\circ = 70^\circ$.
$$\frac{DB}{\sin 50^\circ} = \frac{30}{\sin 70^\circ} \Rightarrow DB \approx 24.46\text{ cm}$$

questions.question:
The braking distance of a car, in metres, is modelled by the quadratic equation graphed below.

The car travels at 110 km/h, with a braking distance of 50 m. What is the car's total stopping distance if the driver responds to a hazard in 0.3 seconds? Correct your answer to 2 decimal places.
questions.answer:
$110\text{ km/h} = \frac{110\,000}{3600} \approx 30.56$ m/s. Reaction distance $= 30.56 \times 0.3 \approx 9.17$ m.
$$\text{Stopping distance} = 50 + 9.17 = 59.17\text{ m}$$

questions.question:
Sydney is 10 hours ahead of Coordinated Universal Time (UTC+10) and Vancouver is 7 hours behind Coordinated Universal Time (UTC−7).

Roy travels from Sydney to Vancouver. His plane leaves Sydney at 9:20 am on Tuesday and travels to Vancouver non-stop. When he arrives, it is 5:20 am in Vancouver on Tuesday.

How long was Roy's flight?
questions.answer:
Sydney is 17 hours ahead of Vancouver, so departure was 9:20 am Tuesday − 17 h $=$ 4:20 pm Monday, Vancouver time.

4:20 pm Monday to 5:20 am Tuesday $=$ **13 hours**.

questions.question:
The following diagram shows the result of a compass radial survey: $P$ ($320^\circ$, 90 m), $Q$ (85 m), $T$ ($100^\circ$) and $R$ ($225^\circ$) from $O$.

If the distance between $P$ and $Q$ is 100 m, show that the true bearing of $Q$ is $29^\circ 38'$.
questions.answer:
$$\cos\angle POQ = \frac{90^2 + 85^2 - 100^2}{2(90)(85)} = \frac{5325}{15\,300} \Rightarrow \angle POQ \approx 69.63^\circ = 69^\circ 38'$$
$Q$ is clockwise from $P$: $320^\circ + 69^\circ 38' - 360^\circ = 29^\circ 38'$.

questions.question:

Find the area of the triangle $POQ$, rounded to the nearest square metre. ($\angle POQ = 69^\circ 38'$.)
questions.answer: $$A = \tfrac12 \times 90 \times 85 \times \sin 69^\circ 38' \approx 3586\text{ m}^2$$

questions.question:
A bowl is formed with two hemispheres. The inner radius is $r$ cm and outer radius is $R$ cm as shown below. Concrete is used to form the bowl.

Find a formula in terms of $r$ and $R$ for the total volume of concrete needed to form the bowl.
questions.answer: $$V = \frac12 \cdot \frac43\pi R^3 - \frac12 \cdot \frac43\pi r^3 = \frac23\pi\left(R^3 - r^3\right)$$

questions.question:
A bowl is formed with two hemispheres. The inner radius is $r$ cm and outer radius is $R$ cm as shown below. Concrete is used to form the bowl.

Using your formula from (a), calculate how many litres of concrete will be needed if $R = 50$ cm and $r = 30$ cm, correct to the nearest litre.
questions.answer: $$V = \frac23\pi\left(50^3 - 30^3\right) \approx 205\,251\text{ cm}^3 \approx 205\text{ L}$$

| $z$ | 0.6 | 0.7 | 0.8 | 0.9 | 1.0 | 1.1 | 1.2 | 1.3 |

The scores for the final exam in a TAFE course in Electrotechnology are normally distributed with mean 62 and standard deviation 10.

Explain why the percentage of scores between 54 and 70 is twice the answer you provided in (a) (28.81%).
questions.answer: 54 is $z = -0.8$ and 70 is $z = 0.8$. The normal curve is symmetric about the mean (62), so the area from 54 to 62 equals the area from 62 to 70, and together they make twice 28.81%.

questions.question:
A random variable is normally distributed with mean 0 and standard deviation 1. The table gives the probability that this random variable is less than $z$.

| $z$ | 0.6 | 0.7 | 0.8 | 0.9 | 1.0 | 1.1 | 1.2 | 1.3 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Probability | 0.7275 | 0.7580 | 0.7881 | 0.8159 | 0.8413 | 0.8643 | 0.8849 | 0.9032 |

The scores for the final exam in a TAFE course in Electrotechnology are normally distributed with mean 62 and standard deviation 10.

By using the values in the table above, find an approximate minimum score that a student would need to be placed in the top 30% of candidates.
questions.answer:
The top 30% need $P(Z < z) \approx 0.70$. The nearest table value is $z = 0.6$ ($0.7275$):
$$0.6 = \frac{x - 62}{10} \Rightarrow x = 68$$
A score of about **68** or more places a student in the top 30%.

The graph of the Income ($I = 45x$) has been drawn on the grid below. Draw a graph of the cost equation $C = 650 + 20x$ on the same grid.
questions.answer: A straight line from $(0, 650)$ through $(10, 850)$ and $(40, 1450)$.

questions.question:
A tour bus company offers tours at \$45 per person. The tour bus company has a fixed cost of \$650 per tour and a variable cost of \$20 per person.

State the coordinates of the point of intersection of the two lines $I = 45x$ and $C = 650 + 20x$. Briefly explain the significance of this point of intersection.
questions.answer:
$$45x = 650 + 20x \Rightarrow x = 26, \quad I = C = 1170$$
The lines meet at **(26, 1170)**: the break-even point. With 26 people income equals cost; with more, the tour makes a profit.

Concrete is to be made up of crushed rock, sand and cement in the ratio of $4 : 2 : 1$ by weight.

questions.answer: Rock : sand $= 4 : 2$, so sand $= \frac{6}{2} = 3$ kg.

questions.question:

Bricks are to be made to weigh 3 kg. How many bricks can be made with a mixture that contains 6 kg of crushed rock?
questions.answer: Cement $= 1.5$ kg, so the mixture weighs $6 + 3 + 1.5 = 10.5$ kg. $\frac{10.5}{3} = 3.5$, so **3** full bricks.

questions.question:

| A | – | 5 |

| C | – | 3 |
| D | A | 3 |
| E | B | 7 |
| F | D, E | 2 |
| G | C | 1 |
| H | F | 3 |
| I | G, H | 5 |

Find the float time of activity $G$.
questions.answer:
Forward scan: $D$ ends at 8, $E$ at 11, so $F$ runs 11–13, $H$ 13–16; $G$ can run 3–4. $I$ starts at $\max(4, 16) = 16$ and the project takes 21 hours.

$G$ must finish by 16, so its latest start is 15. Earliest start is 3:
$$\text{Float}(G) = 15 - 3 = 12\text{ hours}$$

*Note: the school's solution gives 10 hours.*

questions.question:
Blood alcohol for a female can be estimated using the following BAC formula
$$BAC_{\text{female}} = \frac{10N - 7.5H}{5.5M},$$
where $N$ is the number of standard drinks consumed, $H$ is the number of hours since they started drinking and $M$ is the person's mass in kilograms. Lucy weighs 58 kg and had a BAC of 0.08 after drinking for 2 hours. How many standard drinks did she have?
questions.answer: $0.08 = \frac{10N - 15}{319} \Rightarrow 10N - 15 = 25.52 \Rightarrow N \approx 4.1$. **(C)**

questions.question:
A parent used Young's formula to calculate the required medication dosage for their child. Young's formula is
$$\text{Dosage} = \frac{\text{Age of child (years)} \times \text{Adult dose}}{\text{Age of child (years)} + 12}.$$
They found that the child's dosage was one quarter of the adult dose. How old is the child?
questions.answer:
Let the age be $a$ and the adult dose $d$:
$$\frac{ad}{a + 12} = \frac{d}{4} \Rightarrow 4a = a + 12 \Rightarrow a = 4$$
The child is **4 years old**.

questions.question:
Ashaal is standing at a lookout. She looks up and sees a seagull. The seagull is 153 m from Ashaal at an angle of elevation of 63°. Ashaal then looks down and sees the seagull's nest directly below the seagull. The nest is 87 m from Ashaal at an angle of depression of 27°.

Draw a labelled diagram to represent this information. Hence, calculate the distance between the seagull and its nest. Give your answer to the nearest metre.
questions.answer:
The angle at Ashaal between the two sight lines is $63^\circ + 27^\circ = 90^\circ$, so the triangle (Ashaal, seagull, nest) is right-angled at Ashaal:
$$d = \sqrt{153^2 + 87^2} \approx 176\text{ m}$$
(The given data is not fully consistent: other valid methods, e.g. the sine rule or vertical heights, give about 192 m, and the school accepted both.)

questions.question:
Scientists perform two wildlife surveys six months apart to estimate the total koala population in a valley. In the first survey they tagged 70 koalas and then released them back into the wild. In the second survey six months later, they caught and checked 100 koalas. Of these 100 koalas, 35 had tags.

The scientists then discovered that 6 of the koalas that had been tagged in the first survey had been moved to another location to help with a breeding program, so were not in the valley at the time of the second survey. What is the better estimate for the number of koalas in the valley at the time of the second survey?
questions.answer:
Only $70 - 6 = 64$ tagged koalas were in the valley:
$$T = \frac{64 \times 100}{35} \approx 182.9 \approx 183\text{ koalas}$$
