A large farm shed has a flat rectangular roof which is 12 metres wide by 24 metres long. During a thunder storm 20 mm of rain falls onto the roof in 10 minutes. Rain that falls on the roof drains immediately into a cylindrical rainwater tank with a diameter of 4 metres.

Calculate the average rate at which the water level in the tank changes during the storm. Answer in centimetres per minute to 1 decimal place.
questions.answer:
Water: $12 \times 24 \times 0.02 = 5.76\text{ m}^3$. The tank's base area is $\pi(2)^2 = 4\pi\text{ m}^2$:
$$h = \frac{5.76}{4\pi} \approx 0.4584\text{ m} = 45.84\text{ cm}$$
$$\text{Rate} = \frac{45.84}{10} \approx 4.6\text{ cm/min}$$

By first drawing a network diagram showing all seven activities, find the maximum duration of $X$ if it does not increase the minimum time to complete the project.
questions.answer:
Critical path $A$–$C$–$D$–$E$: $6 + 4 + 3 + 2 = 15$ minutes (paths $A$–$B$–$E$ = 10, $A$–$C$–$F$ = 14).

$X$ can start at 6 and must finish by 15:
$$\text{Maximum duration of } X = 15 - 6 = 9\text{ minutes}$$

questions.question: In $\triangle ABC$, $AC = 10$ cm, $AB = 6$ cm and $\angle ACB = 20^\circ 41'$. Given that $\angle ABC$ is obtuse, find the size of $\angle BAC$ to the nearest minute.
questions.answer:
$$\frac{\sin\angle ABC}{10} = \frac{\sin 20^\circ 41'}{6} \Rightarrow \angle ABC = 36^\circ 4' \text{ (acute)}$$
It is obtuse, so $\angle ABC = 180^\circ - 36^\circ 4' = 143^\circ 56'$.
$$\angle BAC = 180^\circ - 143^\circ 56' - 20^\circ 41' = 15^\circ 23'$$

To support the claim, the financial adviser shows the following calculations.

| Investment | Principal | Interest rate | Compounding | Time | Final balance |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | \$10 000 | 6% p.a. | Annually | 5 years | \$13 382.26 |
| B | \$10 000 | 6% p.a. | Monthly | 5 years | \$13 382.26 |

Analyse the financial adviser's claim. In your response: calculate the correct final balance for Investment B; identify any errors in the financial adviser's reasoning; determine whether the claim is valid; justify your conclusion using appropriate calculations and financial reasoning.
questions.answer:
- A: $10\,000(1.06)^5 = \$13\,382.26$ (correct).
- B: $10\,000\left(1 + \frac{0.06}{12}\right)^{60} \approx \$13\,488.50$, not \$13 382.26.

The adviser applied the annual formula to B, ignoring the monthly compounding. B earns \$106.24 more, because interest is added more often and then earns interest itself. **The claim is not valid**: with the same annual rate, more frequent compounding gives a larger final balance.

A yacht leaves point $P$ and sails 12 km on a bearing of 055° to point $Q$. Another yacht leaves point $P$ and sails on a bearing of 080° to point $R$. The distance between $Q$ and $R$ is 8.5 km.

Show that the obtuse angle $\angle QRP$ is $143^\circ 22'$ to the nearest minute.
questions.answer:
$\angle QPR = 80^\circ - 55^\circ = 25^\circ$. Sine rule:
$$\frac{\sin\angle QRP}{12} = \frac{\sin 25^\circ}{8.5} \implies \sin\angle QRP = 0.5966\ldots$$
The acute solution is $36^\circ 38'$, so the obtuse angle is $180^\circ - 36^\circ 38' = 143^\circ 22'$.

questions.question:
A yacht leaves point $P$ and sails 12 km on a bearing of 055° to point $Q$. Another yacht leaves point $P$ and sails on a bearing of 080° to point $R$. The distance between $Q$ and $R$ is 8.5 km.

$\angle QPR = 25^\circ$ and the obtuse angle $\angle QRP = 143^\circ 22'$. Find the bearing of point $Q$ from point $R$ to the nearest degree.
questions.answer:
$\angle PQR = 180^\circ - 25^\circ - 143^\circ 22' = 11^\circ 38'$.

The bearing of $P$ from $R$ is $080^\circ + 180^\circ = 260^\circ$. With the obtuse angle at $R$, $R$ is only about 4 km from $P$ and $Q$ lies to the north-east of $R$, so turning clockwise from $RP$ through $143^\circ 22'$:
$$260^\circ + 143^\circ 22' - 360^\circ = 43^\circ 22'.$$
The bearing of $Q$ from $R$ is about **043°T**.

questions.answer:
With 35 trees, $Q_3$ is the 27th value. With the 16 m tree there are 36 trees, and $Q_3$ becomes the average of the 27th and 28th values (the 16 m tree is above $Q_3$, so these are the old 27th and 28th values).

- Otherwise $Q_3$ increases slightly, to halfway between the old 27th and 28th heights.

Twenty years ago, Jordan deposited a single lump sum into a new bank account earning 3.6% interest per annum, compounding monthly. Present value interest factors for an annuity of \$1 for various interest rates ($r$) and numbers of periods ($n$) are given in the table.

| Period ($n$) | $r = 0.001$ | $r = 0.002$ | $r = 0.003$ | $r = 0.004$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|

| 120 | 113.026 | 106.592 | 100.649 | 95.156 |
| 180 | 164.655 | 151.036 | 138.927 | 128.137 |
| 240 | 213.278 | 190.460 | 170.908 | 154.093 |
| 300 | 259.071 | 225.430 | 197.627 | 174.521 |

Jordan made the following withdrawals from this account:
- \$1500 at the end of each month for the first 10 years, beginning at the end of the first month.
- \$900 at the end of each month for the next 10 years, beginning at the end of the 121st month after the account was opened.

questions.answer:

questions.answer:
$41\,751 = 2977x - 2904 \implies x = \dfrac{44\,655}{2977} = 15$.

questions.question:
The graph shows the relationship between the shoe size of primary school students and the size of their vocabulary.

The line of best fit is $y = 2977x - 2904$. A new elementary school student was added to the data set with a shoe size of 1.0 and a vocabulary of 4000 words. Explain the impact this would have on the gradient, $y$-intercept and correlation coefficient of the line of best fit. (You are not required to recalculate them.)
questions.answer:
At $x = 1$ the line predicts only about 73 words, so $(1, 4000)$ lies far above the line at the left end. It pulls the left end of the line up:
- the **gradient decreases** (the line becomes flatter),
- the **$y$-intercept increases**,
- the **correlation coefficient decreases** (the association becomes weaker), because the point does not follow the trend.

questions.question:

questions.answer:
$BC^2 = 40^2 + 60^2 - 2(40)(60)\cos 30^\circ \approx 1043.1 \implies BC \approx 32.3$ m.

A manufacturing plant has the following process for producing one of its most important products. Each of the processes $A$–$I$ is given its completion time (hours) in the network: $A$ (8), $B$ (5) and $C$ (17) start the project; $D$ (12) and $E$ (15) follow $A$; $H$ (6) follows $B$ and $E$; $G$ (7) follows $D$; $F$ (2) follows $C$; $I$ (1) follows $F$; the project finishes after $G$, $H$ and $I$.

The minimum completion time is 29 hours with critical path $A$–$E$–$H$. A systems engineer has found a more efficient way to complete process $E$, reducing its completion time by 7 hours. Explain the effect this would have on the minimum completion time, fully justifying your answer.
questions.answer:
$E$ becomes 8 hours, so $A$–$E$–$H$ $= 8 + 8 + 6 = 22$ hours. But $A$–$D$–$G = 8 + 12 + 7 = 27$ hours becomes the longest path.

The minimum completion time falls by only **2 hours, to 27 hours**, and the new critical path is $A$–$D$–$G$.

questions.question:
Six towns are linked by a road network. Two of the towns have roads leading directly to three other towns, while all the other towns have roads leading directly to two other towns.
- From town $P$, roads lead to towns $Q$ and $U$ only.
- From town $Q$, roads lead to towns $P$, $R$ and $S$.

Which of the following network diagrams could represent the positions of towns $P$ and $T$ on the road network linking the six towns?
questions.answer:
$P$ has degree 2 and one of its neighbours, $Q$, has degree 3 (joined to $P$, $R$, $S$), so $T$ cannot be adjacent to $P$ or $Q$.
- (A): $T$ is joined to the degree-3 vertex next to $P$, which must be $Q$, but $Q$ is not joined to $T$.
- (B): $T$ is joined to $P$, but $P$ only leads to $Q$ and $U$.
- (C): $P$ has degree 3.
- (D): $P$ (degree 2) is joined to $U$ and to the degree-3 vertex $Q$, which leads on to $R$ and $S$; $T$ fits. **(D)**

questions.question: A van was bought 8 years ago and has been depreciating using the declining-balance method, at 14% per annum. Its salvage value is \$12 540. Calculate its purchase price.

On 14 April 2025, Damien used his credit card to purchase a flight ticket valued at \$2150. He made no other purchases on his credit card during that month and paid the outstanding amount in full on 6 May 2025.

The credit card does not offer an interest-free period. Compound interest was charged daily at a rate of 20.5% per annum. The period for which interest was charged included the date of purchase and the date of payment.

How much interest did Damien pay on this transaction? Round your answer to the nearest cent.
questions.answer:
Days: 14–30 April is 17 days, plus 1–6 May is 6 days, so 23 days.
$$FV = 2150\left(1 + \frac{0.205}{365}\right)^{23} \approx \$2177.95$$
$$\text{Interest} = 2177.95 - 2150 = \$27.95$$

questions.question:
The formulas below are used to calculate an estimate for blood alcohol content (BAC) for females and males respectively.
$$\text{BAC}_{\text{female}} = \frac{10N - 7.5H}{5.5M} \qquad \text{BAC}_{\text{male}} = \frac{10N - 7.5H}{6.8M}$$
where $N$ is the number of standard drinks consumed, $H$ is the number of hours of drinking and $M$ is the person's weight in kilograms.

Juliana and Donald go to a party together and both start drinking at 8.30 pm. The party ends at 1.30 am. At this point Donald and Juliana have the same BAC.

Donald is male, weighs 73 kilograms and drank 4 full-strength beers during the party. Each full-strength beer is equivalent to 1.4 standard drinks.

Juliana is female, weighs 51 kilograms and drank low-strength beer. Each low-strength beer is equivalent to 0.8 standard drinks.

How many low-strength beers did Juliana drink during the party? Answer correct to the nearest whole number.
questions.answer:
$H = 5$ hours. Donald: $N = 4 \times 1.4 = 5.6$.
$$\text{BAC} = \frac{10(5.6) - 7.5(5)}{6.8 \times 73} = \frac{18.5}{496.4} \approx 0.037268$$
Juliana, with $N$ standard drinks:
$$\frac{10N - 37.5}{5.5 \times 51} = 0.037268 \Rightarrow 10N - 37.5 \approx 10.454 \Rightarrow N \approx 4.795$$
Number of low-strength beers $= \dfrac{4.795}{0.8} \approx 6$.

questions.question:
The network diagram shows a series of footpaths directing spectators from the stadium, $A$, to the carpark, $G$. The edges represent the footpaths. The numbers on the edges represent the capacity of the footpaths in people per minute.

Show the maximum flow of the network is 310 people/minute.
questions.answer:
Take the cut through $B \to C$ (140), $D \to C$ (50) and $E \to F$ (120). Every path from $A$ to $G$ crosses it, and its capacity is
$$140 + 50 + 120 = 310.$$
Flows of 310 can be sent (e.g. $ABCF$ 140, $ABDCF$ 50, $ABEF$ 120), so by the maximum-flow minimum-cut theorem the maximum flow is 310 people/minute.

questions.question:
The network diagram shows a series of footpaths directing spectators from the stadium, $A$, to the carpark, $G$. The edges represent the footpaths. The numbers on the edges represent the capacity of the footpaths in people per minute.

The owner of the stadium decides they can afford to upgrade the capacity of one of the footpaths by 90 people per minute, to increase the maximum flow of the footpath network to 400 people per minute.

Which footpath should they upgrade to reach a maximum flow of 400 people per minute?
questions.answer: Upgrade the footpath **from $B$ to $C$**, from 140 to 230 people per minute. The extra 90 can then travel $A \to B \to C \to F \to G$ ($C \to F$ then carries $230 + 50 = 280 \le 300$, and $AB$, $FG$ have 500), giving a maximum flow of 400.

questions.question:
A coastal ferry departs from Dock $A$ near Newcastle at 6.00 am and travels 88 km on a bearing of $055^\circ$ to reach buoy $B$, a navigational marker at sea.

At buoy $B$, the ferry changes direction and travels 62 km on a bearing of $140^\circ$ to reach Harbour $C$, located near a regional tourist inlet.

The Maritime Authority is reviewing this route for efficiency and safety. The diagram shows the ferry's journey.

Using the cosine rule, find the distance from Dock $A$ to Harbour $C$. Give your answer correct to the nearest whole number.
questions.answer:
At $B$: the back bearing to $A$ is $235^\circ$, so $\angle ABC = 235^\circ - 140^\circ = 95^\circ$ (equivalently $55^\circ + 40^\circ$).
$$AC^2 = 88^2 + 62^2 - 2(88)(62)\cos 95^\circ \approx 12\,539 \Rightarrow AC \approx 112\text{ km}$$

questions.answer:
The other paths are A–C–G (12), E–G (14), A–B–D–F (12), A–C–F (9) and E–F (11).
- **D** (2 → 1): A–B–D–G becomes 14, and E–G is also 14, so the project time drops by 1 month, the same as the saving. ✓
- **G** (6 → 3): longest path becomes A–B–D–F = 12, a drop of 3 months, the same as the saving. ✓
- A (3 → 1.5) or B (4 → 2): E–G (14) then becomes critical, so the time drops by only 1 month, less than the saving. ✗

**D or G.**

Sierra is looking to buy her first home, and would like to buy a house in a nearby suburb with a current value of \$1 000 000. She will take out a mortgage to purchase the house, and intends to repay the loan before she retires in 30 years' time.

The house is expected to increase in value by 4.5% per annum for the first 25 years, then decrease in value by 1.3% per annum until Sierra retires.

What is the expected value of the house when Sierra retires?

Sierra is looking to buy her first home, and would like to buy a house in a nearby suburb with a current value of \$1 000 000. She will take out a mortgage to purchase the house, and intends to repay the loan before she retires in 30 years' time.

Sierra has saved up a deposit of \$60 000 and will take out a mortgage from the bank for the balance at an interest rate of 6% per annum, compounding monthly. Her parents have agreed to cover any other costs of the purchase.

She decides that she can afford a maximum monthly repayment of \$5000 at the end of the month for the first ten years, after which time she will be able to increase her monthly repayment to \$7000 for the remainder of the loan.

The table below gives the present value of \$1 invested at the end of each month at varying annual rates of interest compounding monthly, for varying terms in years.

| Years | 2% | 4% | 6% | 8% | 10% |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5 | 57.0524 | 54.2991 | 51.7256 | 49.3184 | 47.0654 |
| 10 | 108.6798 | 98.7702 | 90.0735 | 82.4215 | 75.6712 |
| 15 | 155.3981 | 135.1921 | 118.5035 | 104.6406 | 93.0574 |
| 20 | 197.6740 | 165.0219 | 139.5808 | 119.5543 | 103.6246 |
| 25 | 235.9301 | 189.4525 | 155.2069 | 129.5645 | 110.0472 |
| 30 | 270.5485 | 209.4612 | 166.7916 | 136.2835 | 113.9508 |

Will Sierra be able to repay the mortgage before she retires? Justify your answer with calculations.
questions.answer:
Loan $= 1\,000\,000 - 60\,000 = \$940\,000$.

Present value of the repayments over 30 years (6%):
- First 10 years at \$5000: $5000 \times 90.0735 = \$450\,367.50$
- Years 11–30 at \$7000: $7000 \times (166.7916 - 90.0735) = \$537\,026.70$

Total present value $= \$987\,394.20$.

This is more than the \$940 000 borrowed, so **yes**: her repayments will pay off the loan before she retires (with about \$47 394 to spare in present-value terms).

questions.answer: Check which lines pass through $(1, 3)$: $y = 2x + 1$ gives $3$ ✓ and $y = 4 - x$ gives $3$ ✓. The other lines give $y = -3$ ($-2x - 1$), $-2.5$ ($\frac12 x - 3$) and $-1$ ($-2x + 1$) at $x = 1$. **(C)**

questions.question: The graph shows the value of three different annuities over time. Which of the following statements gives a plausible explanation for the different values after seven terms?
questions.answer: All three annuities start at the same value (about \$500) and have the same number of terms, so the starting value and term length cannot explain the gap. Annuity 1 grows most, then 2, then 3, which is consistent with larger regular deposits (or a higher interest rate) for Annuity 1, then 2, then 3. Only **(D)** is a plausible explanation.
options: Annuity 2 and Annuity 3 have higher interest rates than Annuity 1.
Annuity 2 and Annuity 3 have a lower initial value than Annuity 1.
Annuity 1 and Annuity 2 have shorter interest terms than Annuity 3.
Annuity 1 and Annuity 2 have higher regular deposits than Annuity 3.

questions.question: A \$15 000 commercial oven was purchased for a school's hospitality kitchen. After 3 years, its value is \$10 935. The oven depreciates using the declining balance method. What is the annual rate of depreciation, correct to the nearest whole percentage?

$B$ boxes of nails in a factory were inspected and found to be normally distributed with a mean of $r$ nails. The probability that a box had between $r + k$ and $r + 2k$ nails was $9\%$. The probability that a box had between $r - 2k$ and $r + 2k$ nails was $54\%$. Given that 5508 boxes were inspected to have more than $r - k$ nails, how many boxes inspected had more than $r + k$ nails?
The vertices $O$, $A$ and $B$ of an equilateral triangle represent three bus stops. The bearing of $A$ from $O$ is $330^\circ$. Which of the following could be the bearing of $B$ from $A$?
questions.answer: The bearing of $O$ from $A$ is $330^\circ - 180^\circ = 150^\circ$. $B$ lies $60^\circ$ either side of the line $AO$, so the bearing of $B$ from $A$ is $150^\circ + 60^\circ = 210^\circ$ or $150^\circ - 60^\circ = 090^\circ$. Only $210^\circ$ is offered. **(C)**

questions.question: Kayne and Aria leave from the same location at the same time and jog in the same direction. If Kayne jogs at an average speed of 10 km/h and Aria at 7 km/h, calculate how far Aria is behind Kayne after 40 minutes.
questions.answer:
Aria falls behind at $10 - 7 = 3$ km/h. In $40$ min $= \frac23$ h:
$$d = 3 \times \tfrac23 = 2\text{ km}$$
Aria is **2 km** behind.

questions.question:
Solve the following equation:
$$\frac{4x - 7}{6} + 2 = \frac{9 - 3x}{4}$$
questions.answer:
Multiply every term by the common denominator 12:
$$2(4x - 7) + 24 = 3(9 - 3x)$$
$$8x + 10 = 27 - 9x \Rightarrow 17x = 17 \Rightarrow x = 1$$
Check: LHS $= \frac{-3}{6} + 2 = 1.5$; RHS $= \frac64 = 1.5$ ✓.

questions.question:
The mass in grams of eight Granny Smith apples picked off a tree are shown.

161, 179, 183, 186, 189, 193, 197, 207

Would the mass of the lightest apple be considered to be an outlier? Justify your answer with calculations.
questions.answer:
$Q_1 = \frac{179 + 183}{2} = 181$, $Q_3 = \frac{193 + 197}{2} = 195$, so $\text{IQR} = 195 - 181 = 14$.

Lower fence $= Q_1 - 1.5 \times \text{IQR} = 181 - 21 = 160$.

The lightest apple (161 g) is above 160 g, so it is **not** an outlier.

questions.question:
Emily looked at her receipt for groceries from the supermarket and noted that she had paid GST of $10\%$ on some items she bought, and no GST on other items. Emily paid a total of \$35.33 for her groceries including GST. The only item she bought that was GST-free was a bunch of grapes for \$7.94. The items she bought that included GST were chocolate for \$9.00, a frozen pizza for \$7.50 and some cat litter.

What was the total amount of GST that Emily paid?
questions.answer:
The items with GST cost $35.33 - 7.94 = \$27.39$ in total (price already includes GST, which is $\frac{1}{11}$ of it):
$$\text{GST} = \frac{27.39}{11} = \$2.49$$

questions.question: A company has decided to distribute \$63 million of its profits as dividends. The company has issued 210 million shares, and each share is valued at \$174.62. Calculate the dividend yield (as a percentage) of each share to 2 decimal places.
questions.answer:
Dividend per share $= \dfrac{63}{210} = \$0.30$.
$$\text{Yield} = \frac{0.30}{174.62} \times 100\% \approx 0.17\%$$
(The school's working contains a slip but reaches the same value, $0.17\%$.)

questions.question:
Susan travels from city $P$ (UTC $-7$) to city $Q$ (UTC $-3$). The flight between these two cities took 6 hours. The flight arrived at city $Q$ at 3:30 a.m. local time on Thursday the 4th of October.

On what day and what time did Susan's flight leave city $P$ for this journey?
questions.answer:
City $Q$ is $4$ hours ahead of city $P$.
- Departure in $Q$'s time: $3{:}30\text{ am} - 6\text{ h} = 9{:}30\text{ pm}$ on Wednesday 3 October.
- Convert to $P$'s time: $9{:}30\text{ pm} - 4\text{ h} = 5{:}30\text{ pm}$.

The flight left city $P$ at **5:30 pm on Wednesday 3 October**.

questions.question:
Jenny weighs 74 kg. She ate 143 g of trout and 48 g of noodles. The labels on these products indicate that the trout has 220 kJ of energy in a 55 g serve, and the noodles has 1020 kJ in a 120 g serve.

Calculate the number of kJ in her trout and noodles.
questions.answer:
Trout: $\frac{143}{55} \times 220 = 572$ kJ. Noodles: $\frac{48}{120} \times 1020 = 408$ kJ.

Total $= 572 + 408 = 980$ kJ.

questions.answer:

questions.question:
In a game, Joe has three attempts to roll two dice, each with faces numbered 1 to 6. In any attempt she will:
- WIN A PRIZE if the sum of the topmost faces is at least 8.
- TRY AGAIN if the sum of the topmost faces is 5, 6 or 7.
- LOSE if the sum of the topmost faces is 4 or less.

If Joe wins a prize, or loses, the game is over.

Complete the table, using W for win, T for try again and L for lose.
questions.answer:
Each cell is decided by the sum of the two dice.

| 2nd die \ 1st die | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | L | L | L | T | T | T |
| 2 | L | L | T | T | T | W |
| 3 | L | T | T | T | W | W |
| 4 | T | T | T | W | W | W |
| 5 | T | T | W | W | W | W |
| 6 | T | W | W | W | W | W |

There are $15$ W, $15$ T and $6$ L out of $36$ outcomes.

questions.question:
In a game, Joe has three attempts to roll two dice, each with faces numbered 1 to 6. In any attempt she will:
- WIN A PRIZE if the sum of the topmost faces is at least 8.
- TRY AGAIN if the sum of the topmost faces is 5, 6 or 7.
- LOSE if the sum of the topmost faces is 4 or less.

If Joe wins a prize, or loses, the game is over.

Fill in the probabilities in the probability tree below (each attempt has the branches WIN, TRY AGAIN and LOSE).
questions.answer:
From the table: $P(W) = \frac{15}{36} = \frac{5}{12}$, $P(T) = \frac{15}{36} = \frac{5}{12}$, $P(L) = \frac{6}{36} = \frac16$.

The probabilities are the same on every attempt: WIN $\frac{5}{12}$, TRY AGAIN $\frac{5}{12}$, LOSE $\frac16$.

questions.question:
In a game, Joe has three attempts to roll two dice, each with faces numbered 1 to 6. In any attempt she will:
- WIN A PRIZE if the sum of the topmost faces is at least 8.
- TRY AGAIN if the sum of the topmost faces is 5, 6 or 7.
- LOSE if the sum of the topmost faces is 4 or less.

If Joe wins a prize, or loses, the game is over.

What is the probability that Joe wins a prize in this game?
questions.answer:
She wins on the 1st attempt, or tries again then wins on the 2nd, or tries twice then wins on the 3rd:
$$P(\text{win}) = \frac{5}{12} + \frac{5}{12}\cdot\frac{5}{12} + \left(\frac{5}{12}\right)^2\cdot\frac{5}{12} = \frac{5}{12} + \frac{25}{144} + \frac{125}{1728} = \frac{1145}{1728} \approx 66.26\%$$

questions.question:
A new laptop is purchased for \$2450 using a credit card. The credit card has an interest-free period of 55 days from and including the date of purchase. After this period ends, interest is charged on the purchase made, compounding daily at a rate of $15.4\%$ per annum, from and including the day following the interest-free period. The full payment for the laptop is made on the 90th day from the date of purchase. There were no other purchases on this credit card.

What was the total interest charged when the account was paid in full?
questions.answer:
Interest is charged from day 56 to day 90: $90 - 55 = 35$ days. The daily rate is $\frac{15.4\%}{365} = \frac{0.154}{365}$.
$$A = 2450\left(1 + \frac{0.154}{365}\right)^{35} \approx 2486.44$$
$$\text{Interest} = 2486.44 - 2450 \approx \$36.44$$

questions.question:
A shopkeeper notes how much money, $\$A$, customers have spent in the store and how many minutes, $t$, it took them to decide what they wanted to buy. The diagram shows the dataset and a line of best fit.

Find the equation of the line of best fit.
questions.answer:
The line passes through $(0, 40)$ and $(8, 0)$: gradient $m = \frac{0 - 40}{8 - 0} = -5$, vertical intercept $40$.
$$A = -5t + 40$$

questions.question:
A shopkeeper notes how much money, $\$A$, customers have spent in the store and how many minutes, $t$, it took them to decide what they wanted to buy. The diagram shows the dataset and a line of best fit.

Suppose another customer spent \$20 after taking 7 minutes to decide what they wanted to buy. A new line of best fit is created to account for this extra customer. Describe how the gradient of the line of best fit would change from the answer found in part (a).
questions.answer: The point $(7, 20)$ lies well above the current line (which gives $A = 5$ at $t = 7$), so the line is pulled up at the right-hand end. The gradient becomes **less negative** (it increases, closer to zero).

questions.question:
Buntings can be made from individual flags held together with string. The diagram below shows five identical flags on a 1 metre length of string. There is a 1 cm gap between each flag and 8 cm at each end of the string to tie the bunting on display.

The material for one flag consists of two shapes, a rectangle and an equilateral triangle. The diagram shows the shape and dimensions of one flag (the rectangle is 16 cm by 4 cm).

Determine whether or not it is suitable to have six identical flags on the 1 metre length of string. Justify your statement with relevant calculations.
questions.answer:
Six flags need $6 \times 16 = 96$ cm, five 1 cm gaps $= 5$ cm and $2 \times 8 = 16$ cm at the ends:
$$96 + 5 + 16 = 117\text{ cm} > 100\text{ cm}$$
Six flags would not fit, so it is **not suitable**.

questions.question:
Buntings can be made from individual flags held together with string. The diagram below shows five identical flags on a 1 metre length of string. There is a 1 cm gap between each flag and 8 cm at each end of the string to tie the bunting on display.

The material for one flag consists of two shapes, a rectangle and an equilateral triangle. The diagram shows the shape and dimensions of one flag (the rectangle is 16 cm by 4 cm).

questions.answer:
Rectangle: $16 \times 4 = 64\text{ cm}^2$.
Equilateral triangle of side 16 cm: $\frac12(16)(16)\sin 60^\circ \approx 110.85\text{ cm}^2$.
$$A \approx 64 + 110.85 = 174.85\text{ cm}^2$$

questions.question:
After a ball is thrown off a building, the height of the ball can be modelled by the equation $h = at^2 + 4t + c$, where $t$ is time in seconds after the ball is thrown off the building, and $h$ is the height of the ball above the ground in metres. The graph shows the height of the ball above the ground after $t$ seconds. Two points, $(0, 16)$ and $(3, 10)$, are also shown on the graph.

Only a part of the graph applies to this model. Find all values of $t$ that are not suitable to use with this model and explain why these values are not suitable.
questions.answer:
The $t$-intercepts are $t = -2$ and $t = 4$.
- $t < 0$ is not suitable: time before the ball was thrown is meaningless.
- $t > 4$ is not suitable: the height would be negative (below the ground), because the ball has already hit the ground at $t = 4$.

A passenger had to fly from Orange to Coffs Harbour in an emergency. They intended to take the cheapest route, but when they went to book the flights they found that all the Orange to Sydney services had been cancelled for the day. They booked the cheapest route that did NOT include a flight from Orange to Sydney. What was the percentage increase in the cost of their flights due to the cancelled services? Answer as a percentage correct to 1 decimal place.
questions.answer:
Cheapest route: $O \to S \to C = 231 + 205 = \$436$.

Without $O$–$S$: $O \to M \to S \to C = 499 + 174 + 205 = \$878$ (the other option $O \to M \to C = \$1092$ is dearer).
$$\text{Increase} = \frac{878 - 436}{436} \times 100\% \approx 101.4\%$$

questions.question:
In the diagram, $AB$ is a road running in the south-east direction, $C$ is an observatory on a bearing of $205^\circ$ from $A$, and $BC = 30$ km. A man travels along the road from $B$ to $A$. After walking 20 km to $D$, he is 21 km from $C$.

Calculate how far the man is from $A$. Give your answer correct to the nearest kilometre.
questions.answer:
**Angle $B$** (cosine rule in $\triangle CBD$, $CB = 30$, $BD = 20$, $CD = 21$):
$$\cos B = \frac{30^2 + 20^2 - 21^2}{2(30)(20)} = \frac{859}{1200} \Rightarrow B \approx 44.29^\circ$$
**Angle $A$:** $AB$ runs on bearing $135^\circ$ and $AC$ on bearing $205^\circ$, so $\angle BAC = 205^\circ - 135^\circ = 70^\circ$. Then $\angle C = 180^\circ - 70^\circ - 44.29^\circ = 65.71^\circ$.

**Sine rule in $\triangle ABC$:**
$$AB = \frac{30\sin 65.71^\circ}{\sin 70^\circ} \approx 29.1\text{ km}$$
$$AD = AB - BD \approx 29.1 - 20 \approx 9\text{ km}$$

Identify the direction and strength of the linear association between $M$ and $E$.
questions.answer: $r \approx -0.99$ is close to $-1$: a **strong negative** linear association.

questions.question:
A set of bivariate data was collected by recording the marks students received in a Music quiz, $M$, and an Economics quiz, $E$. In each quiz students gained either 0 marks or 1 mark for each question. The graph shows a scatterplot of these measurements: the points $(1, 8)$, $(3, 5)$ and $(6, 2)$.

Another student was absent for the Economics quiz but achieved 10 marks in the Music quiz. By creating a line of best fit or otherwise, explain why the student's Economics mark could not be estimated using the association between $M$ and $E$ for the other students.
questions.answer: The line of best fit is about $E = -1.2M + 9.2$. A Music mark of 10 is outside the range of the data ($1 \le M \le 6$), so using it is **extrapolation**, which is unreliable. Here it would also give $E \approx -2.8$, an impossible negative mark.

questions.question:
A flu virus spreads in a little town on an island. The number of people $N$ infected $D$ days after the virus started to spread can be modelled by the equation $N = Ka^D$, where $K$ and $a$ are constants. The graph shows the number of people $N$ infected after $D$ days, passing through $(0, 4)$ and $(3, 32)$.

Using the information shown on the graph, find the number of people infected after 10 days.
questions.answer:
At $(0, 4)$: $4 = Ka^0 = K$, so $K = 4$.
At $(3, 32)$: $32 = 4a^3 \Rightarrow a^3 = 8 \Rightarrow a = 2$.

So $N = 4 \times 2^D$ and
$$N(10) = 4 \times 2^{10} = 4096\text{ people}$$

questions.question:
The diagram shows a slide in a fun park. The slide has a curved surface on the top and a uniform cross-sectional area in the front as shown. Also, its left side and its base are rectangular faces. The base is 15.6 m long, the left side is 9.6 m high, and the heights 6.8 m and 3.4 m are measured at equal intervals along the base.

Use three applications of the trapezoidal rule to find an approximate area for the cross section.
questions.answer:
Three strips of width $h = \frac{15.6}{3} = 5.2$ m with heights $9.6,\ 6.8,\ 3.4,\ 0$:
$$A \approx \frac{5.2}{2}\left[9.6 + 2(6.8 + 3.4) + 0\right] = 2.6 \times 30 = 78\text{ m}^2$$

questions.question:
The diagram shows a slide in a fun park. The slide has a curved surface on the top and a uniform cross-sectional area in the front as shown. Also, its left side and its base are rectangular faces. The base is 15.6 m long, the left side is 9.6 m high, and the heights 6.8 m and 3.4 m are measured at equal intervals along the base.

If the curved area on the top is $169.68\text{ m}^2$ and the total surface area of the slide (including the base) is $537.36\text{ m}^2$, what is an approximate value of the width $W$?
questions.answer:
Total surface area $=$ curved top $+$ base $+$ left side $+$ two identical cross-sections:
$$537.36 = 169.68 + 15.6W + 9.6W + 2(78)$$
$$211.68 = 25.2W \Rightarrow W = 8.4\text{ m}$$

questions.question:
Peter placed 15 identical small spherical marbles each of radius 2 cm in a large hemispherical bowl of radius $R$. The volume of the empty space in the bowl is $992\pi\text{ cm}^3$.

What is the radius $R$ of the hemispherical bowl?
questions.answer:
Volume of the 15 marbles $= 15 \times \frac43\pi(2)^3 = 160\pi$.

Volume of the bowl $= \frac23\pi R^3$. Empty space $=$ bowl $-$ marbles:
$$\tfrac23\pi R^3 - 160\pi = 992\pi \Rightarrow \tfrac23 R^3 = 1152 \Rightarrow R^3 = 1728$$
$$R = 12\text{ cm}$$

questions.question:
Water is to be pumped through a field, from the source at $A$ to the sink at $E$, using a series of pipes from pumping station locations, labelled $A$ to $G$. The network diagram shows the maximum flow rate through each of these pipes, measured in thousands of litres per hour.

What is the capacity of the cut shown in the diagram?
questions.answer:
Add the capacities of the pipes that cross the cut from the source side to the sink side: $BC = 19$ and $FE = 16$ (the pipes $CG$ and $DF$ carry flow back towards the source side, so they are not counted):
$$19 + 16 = 35$$

questions.question:
Water is to be pumped through a field, from the source at $A$ to the sink at $E$, using a series of pipes from pumping station locations, labelled $A$ to $G$. The network diagram shows the maximum flow rate through each of these pipes, measured in thousands of litres per hour.

Calculate the maximum flow of this network.
questions.answer:
The maximum flow equals the minimum cut. The cut through $CD$ and $GF$ has capacity $15 + 10 = 25$, and no other cut is smaller.

Maximum flow $= 25$ thousand litres per hour.

questions.question:
Water is to be pumped through a field, from the source at $A$ to the sink at $E$, using a series of pipes from pumping station locations, labelled $A$ to $G$. The network diagram shows the maximum flow rate through each of these pipes, measured in thousands of litres per hour.

The owners of this field want to increase the flow of water through one of the pipes in order to increase the maximum flow of this network. Which pipe should they choose, and what is the minimum amount by which its flow should be increased in order to maximise the amount of water flowing through this network?
questions.answer:
The minimum cut ($CD$ and $GF$, capacity 25) must be raised, so the pipe to increase is $CD$ or $GF$.
- **Increase $CD$:** the cut $AB + GF = 16 + 10 = 26$ then limits the flow to 26, so the gain is only 1.
- **Increase $GF$ by $x$:** the minimum cut becomes $CD + GF = 25 + x$, until it reaches the next smallest cut, $CD + FE = 15 + 16 = 31$.

Choose pipe **$GF$** and increase it by **6** thousand litres per hour, giving a maximum flow of $31$ thousand litres per hour.

The activity table shows the tasks required to complete a construction project.

| Activity | Prerequisite/s | Duration (days) |
|---|---|---|
| A | – | 4 |
| B | A | 6 |
| C | A | 5 |
| D | B, C | 3 |
| E | C | 4 |
| F | D, E | 2 |

Activity $C$ is delayed by two days. Determine the new critical path to describe how this delay affects the project's completion time. Construct a network diagram to support your answer.
questions.answer:
**Original:** the longest path is $A$–$B$–$D$–$F$ $= 4 + 6 + 3 + 2 = 15$ days (the path $A$–$C$–$E$–$F$ is $4 + 5 + 4 + 2 = 15$ days as well, and $A$–$C$–$D$–$F$ is $14$).

**After the delay** ($C$ now takes $7$ days): $A$–$C$–$E$–$F$ $= 4 + 7 + 4 + 2 = 17$ days and $A$–$C$–$D$–$F$ $= 16$ days, so these are now longer than $A$–$B$–$D$–$F$ $= 15$.

The new critical path is **$A$–$C$–$E$–$F$**, and the minimum completion time increases from 15 days to **17 days**: the delay of 2 days in $C$ delays the whole project by 2 days. The network diagram (earliest and latest start times in boxes, with a dummy activity from $B$ to the start of $D$) is shown in the answer image.

The tables show the future values and present values of annuities of \$1 for a variety of periods and interest rates. Contributions are made at the end of each period.

Jane invested \$3500 at the end of each year for 12 years into an annuity with an interest rate of 9% per annum. After 5 years, she decided to invest in an additional annuity at 6% per annum, making equal annual contributions at the end of each year for the next 7 years. She wants the total value of both annuities after 12 years to be \$100 000.

To fund the annual contributions to the second annuity, Jane borrows each contribution amount at an interest rate of 6% per annum and repays it in 12 equal monthly instalments over the following year.

Calculate the amount Jane must pay back each month for the contributions to the additional annuity.
questions.answer:
**First annuity** (12 years, 9%, factor $20.141$): $3500 \times 20.141 = \$70\,493.50$.

**Second annuity** must provide $100\,000 - 70\,493.50 = \$29\,506.50$. Over 7 years at 6% the future value factor is $8.394$:
$$C = \frac{29\,506.50}{8.394} = \$3515.19$$
**Monthly repayments:** borrowing $C$ at 6% p.a. $= 0.5\%$ per month for 12 months, the present value factor is $11.619$:
$$\text{Instalment} = \frac{3515.19}{11.619} \approx \$302.54\text{ per month}$$

questions.question: The maximum speed of a train going up a hill varies inversely with the square of its weight. What is the effect on the maximum speed of the train if the weight of the train is halved?
questions.answer: $S = \dfrac{k}{w^2}$. Halving $w$: $S = \dfrac{k}{(w/2)^2} = \dfrac{4k}{w^2}$, so the speed is multiplied by 4. **(D)**

questions.answer:
Length of the given tree: $20 + 25 + 22 + 20 + 25 + 30 = 142$ m.

A minimum spanning tree (e.g. by Kruskal's algorithm) uses $DE = 15$, $AB = 20$, $AF = 20$, $AG = 20$, $CF = 22$, $CD = 22$, with length $15 + 20 + 20 + 20 + 22 + 22 = 119$ m.

The following formula can be used to calculate an estimate for blood alcohol content (BAC) for males.

Gregor weighs 80 kg. His BAC was zero when he began drinking alcohol. At 10 pm, after consuming 6 standard drinks, his BAC was 0.075. Using the formula above, estimate the time at which Gregor began drinking alcohol. Give your answer correct to the nearest minute.

$$P = \frac79 \times \frac29 + \frac29 \times \frac79 = \frac{28}{81}.$$

questions.question:
A ball is thrown vertically upwards from a balcony and its height $h$ metres above the ground over time $t$ seconds is modelled using the equation $h = -5t^2 + 10t + 40$. The graph of $h$ against $t$ is shown.

The equation $h = -5t^2 + 10t + 40$ only models the flight of the ball for some values of $t$. Explain which values are invalid and why.
questions.answer:
- $t < 0$: time cannot be negative (before the ball is thrown).
- $t > 4$: the ball hits the ground at $t = 4$ ($h = 0$); after that the model gives negative heights, i.e. below the ground, which is impossible.

The model is only valid for $0 \le t \le 4$.

Median \$510; $Q_1 = \$350$, $Q_3 = \$610$, so $\text{IQR} = 260$.

questions.question:
A compass radial survey of the field $ABCD$ has been conducted from a central point $O$. The readings are: $A$ on a bearing of 310°, $OA = 85$ m; $B$ on 021°, $OB = 64$ m; $D$ on 256°, $OD = 70$ m; $OC = 52$ m.

Farmer Tran wants to fence around the area $ABOD$. Find the cost of this project if each metre of fencing costs \$22.
questions.answer:
$\angle AOB = 360^\circ - 310^\circ + 21^\circ = 71^\circ$ and $\angle AOD = 310^\circ - 256^\circ = 54^\circ$.
$$AB^2 = 85^2 + 64^2 - 2(85)(64)\cos 71^\circ \implies AB \approx 88.20 \text{ m}$$
$$AD^2 = 85^2 + 70^2 - 2(85)(70)\cos 54^\circ \implies AD \approx 71.63 \text{ m}$$
Perimeter of $ABOD = 88.20 + 64 + 70 + 71.63 \approx 293.82$ m. Cost $\approx 293.82 \times 22 = \$6464.13$.

questions.question:
A compass radial survey of the field $ABCD$ has been conducted from a central point $O$. The readings are: $A$ on a bearing of 310°, $OA = 85$ m; $B$ on 021°, $OB = 64$ m; $D$ on 256°, $OD = 70$ m; $OC = 52$ m.

The surveyor finds that the area of triangle $BOC$ is $1664\ \text{m}^2$. Find the bearing of $C$ from $O$.
questions.answer:
$\frac12 \times 64 \times 52 \times \sin\angle BOC = 1664 \implies \sin\angle BOC = 1 \implies \angle BOC = 90^\circ$.

Bearing of $C$ from $O$ $= 21^\circ + 90^\circ = 111^\circ$T.

Activities with zero float: $A, D, E, G, H, L, M$ — **7 activities**.

questions.question:
Track works are required across the Sydney rail network and 13 activities are needed to be completed. The network diagram shows these activities, including their completion times in weeks: $A$ (6) and $B$ (3) start the project; $C$ (2) follows $B$; $D$ (3) and $E$ (5) follow $A$ and $C$; $F$ (5) follows $B$; $G$ (4) follows $D$; $H$ (2), $I$ (2) and $J$ (3) follow $E$; $L$ (5) follows $G$ and $H$; $K$ (3) follows $F$ and $J$; $M$ (1) follows $I$ and $L$. The project finishes after $K$ and $M$.

The project currently takes 19 weeks. The contractor proposes a reduction in completion time for activities $A$, $E$, $F$ and $L$, at an additional cost. The table below summarises these costs. Each activity can only be reduced by a maximum of three weeks.

| Activity | Weekly cost (\$) |
|---|---|
| $A$ | 130 000 |
| $E$ | 110 000 |
| $F$ | 120 000 |
| $L$ | 100 000 |

If the overall completion time for the project can be reduced to 15 weeks, find the minimum cost of this change. Your answer should explain clearly why the minimum cost is achieved.
questions.answer:
Every path must end up at most 15 weeks. Let $a$, $e$, $l$ be the reductions of $A$, $E$, $L$ ($F$ is on no long path, so reducing it does not help).

| Path | Length | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| $A$–$D$–$G$–$L$–$M$ | 19 | $a + l \ge 4$ |
| $A$–$E$–$H$–$L$–$M$ | 19 | $a + e + l \ge 4$ |
| $B$–$C$–$D$–$G$–$L$–$M$ | 18 | $l \ge 3$ |
| $B$–$C$–$E$–$H$–$L$–$M$ | 18 | $e + l \ge 3$ |
| $A$–$E$–$J$–$K$ | 17 | $a + e \ge 2$ |
| $B$–$C$–$E$–$J$–$K$ | 16 | $e \ge 1$ |

$B$–$C$–$D$–$G$–$L$–$M$ forces $l = 3$ (the maximum), so $a + l \ge 4$ forces $a \ge 1$; $B$–$C$–$E$–$J$–$K$ forces $e \ge 1$. Taking $a = 1$, $e = 1$, $l = 3$ meets every condition:
$$\text{Minimum cost} = 130\,000 + 110\,000 + 3 \times 100\,000 = \$540\,000.$$

(The paper's sample answer gives \$430 000 by reducing only $A$ and $L$, but that leaves $A$–$E$–$J$–$K$ at 16 weeks and $B$–$C$–$E$–$J$–$K$ at 16 weeks, so the project would still take 16 weeks.)
